1887-a-study-in-scarlet-1-03-the-laurist.subject: Enoch J. Drebber
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-1-03-the-laurist.statement: Enoch J. Drebber is associated with Cleveland, Ohio, U.S.A.
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-1-03-the-laurist.quote: bearing the name of ‘Enoch J. Drebber, Cleveland, Ohio, U.S.A.’

1887-a-study-in-scarlet-1-03-the-laurist.subject: Lauriston Gardens
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-1-03-the-laurist.statement: The mystery takes place at 3, Lauriston Gardens.
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-1-03-the-laurist.quote: There has been a bad business during the night at 3, Lauriston Gardens, off the Brixton Road.

1887-a-study-in-scarlet-1-03-the-laurist.subject: John Rance
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-1-03-the-laurist.statement: John Rance found Drebber's body in the empty house.
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-1-03-the-laurist.quote: He found the door open, and in the front room, which is bare of furniture, discovered the body of a gentleman

1887-a-study-in-scarlet-1-03-the-laurist.subject: Enoch J. Drebber
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-1-03-the-laurist.statement: Holmes says Drebber was killed by poison.
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-1-03-the-laurist.quote: “Poison,” said Sherlock Holmes curtly, and strode off.

1887-a-study-in-scarlet-1-03-the-laurist.subject: Holmes
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-1-03-the-laurist.statement: Holmes decides to go to Lauriston Gardens to investigate.
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-1-03-the-laurist.quote: However, we may as well go and have a look.

1887-a-study-in-scarlet-1-03-the-laurist.subject: Holmes
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-1-03-the-laurist.statement: Holmes and Watson travel by hansom toward Brixton Road.
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-1-03-the-laurist.quote: A minute later we were both in a hansom, driving furiously for the Brixton Road.

1887-a-study-in-scarlet-1-03-the-laurist.subject: Holmes
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-1-03-the-laurist.statement: Holmes scrutinizes the ground and surroundings before entering the house.
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-1-03-the-laurist.quote: With an air of nonchalance which, under the circumstances, seemed to me to border upon affectation, he lounged up and down the pavement, and gazed vacantly at the ground, the sky, the opposite houses and the line of railings.

1887-a-study-in-scarlet-1-03-the-laurist.subject: Tobias Gregson
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-1-03-the-laurist.statement: Tobias Gregson is a detective.
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-1-03-the-laurist.quote: the detective said evasively.

1887-a-study-in-scarlet-1-03-the-laurist.subject: Lestrade
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-1-03-the-laurist.statement: Lestrade is a detective.
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-1-03-the-laurist.quote: “There is no clue?” said Gregson.

1887-a-study-in-scarlet-1-03-the-laurist.subject: Gregson
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-1-03-the-laurist.statement: Gregson and Lestrade are rivals and are jealous of one another.
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-1-03-the-laurist.quote: They have their knives into one another, too. They are as jealous as a pair of professional beauties.

1887-a-study-in-scarlet-1-03-the-laurist.subject: Holmes
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-1-03-the-laurist.statement: Holmes kneels beside Drebber's body and examines it.
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-1-03-the-laurist.quote: Sherlock Holmes approached the body, and, kneeling down, examined it intently.

1887-a-study-in-scarlet-1-03-the-laurist.subject: Holmes
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-1-03-the-laurist.statement: Holmes concludes that the blood around Drebber belongs to another person, presumably the murderer.
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-1-03-the-laurist.quote: Then, of course, this blood belongs to a second individual—presumably the murderer, if murder has been committed.

1887-a-study-in-scarlet-1-03-the-laurist.subject: Lestrade
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-1-03-the-laurist.statement: Lestrade finds a woman's wedding ring when Drebber is lifted.
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-1-03-the-laurist.quote: As they raised him, a ring tinkled down and rolled across the floor.

1887-a-study-in-scarlet-1-03-the-laurist.subject: Holmes
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-1-03-the-laurist.statement: Holmes says that “Rache” is German for “revenge.”
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-1-03-the-laurist.quote: ‘Rache,’ is the German for ‘revenge’; so don’t lose your time looking for Miss Rachel.

1887-a-study-in-scarlet-1-03-the-laurist.subject: Lestrade
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-1-03-the-laurist.statement: Lestrade discovers the word “RACHE” written on the wall in blood-red letters.
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-1-03-the-laurist.quote:
Across this bare space there was scrawled in blood-red letters a single word—

RACHE.

1887-a-study-in-scarlet-1-03-the-laurist.subject: Lestrade
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-1-03-the-laurist.statement: Lestrade interprets “RACHE” as the beginning of the name Rachel.
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-1-03-the-laurist.quote: Why, it means that the writer was going to put the female name Rachel, but was disturbed before he or she had time to finish.

1887-a-study-in-scarlet-1-03-the-laurist.subject: Holmes
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-1-03-the-laurist.statement: Holmes searches the room with a tape measure and magnifying glass, collecting grey dust and inspecting the wall inscription.
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-1-03-the-laurist.quote: In one place he gathered up very carefully a little pile of grey dust from the floor, and packed it away in an envelope.

1887-a-study-in-scarlet-1-03-the-laurist.subject: Holmes
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-1-03-the-laurist.statement: Holmes asks for the name and address of the constable who found the body.
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-1-03-the-laurist.quote: In the meantime I should like to speak to the constable who found the body.

1887-a-study-in-scarlet-1-03-the-laurist.subject: Holmes
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-1-03-the-laurist.value: man over six feet tall, in the prime of life, with small feet, coarse square-toed boots, and long right-hand fingernails
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-1-03-the-laurist.statement: Holmes describes the murderer as a man over six feet tall, in the prime of life, with small feet, coarse square-toed boots, and unusually long fingernails on his right hand.
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-1-03-the-laurist.quote: There has been murder done, and the murderer was a man. He was more than six feet high, was in the prime of life, had small feet for his height, wore coarse, square-toed boots and smoked a Trichinopoly cigar.

1887-a-study-in-scarlet-1-03-the-laurist.subject: Holmes
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-1-03-the-laurist.value: arrived in a four-wheeled cab drawn by a horse with three old shoes and one new shoe on its off fore leg
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-1-03-the-laurist.statement: Holmes says the murderer came with Drebber in a four-wheeled cab drawn by a horse with three old shoes and one new shoe on its off fore leg.
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-1-03-the-laurist.quote: He came here with his victim in a four-wheeled cab, which was drawn by a horse with three old shoes and one new one on his off fore leg.

1887-a-study-in-scarlet-1-03-the-laurist.subject: Holmes
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-1-03-the-laurist.statement: Holmes leaves to visit John Rance.
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-1-03-the-laurist.quote: “Come along, Doctor,” he said; “we shall go and look him up.

1887-a-study-in-scarlet-1-04-what-john-r.subject: Holmes
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-1-04-what-john-r.statement: Holmes led Watson to the nearest telegraph office after they left Lauriston Gardens.
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-1-04-what-john-r.quote: Sherlock Holmes led me to the nearest telegraph office, whence he dispatched a long telegram.

1887-a-study-in-scarlet-1-04-what-john-r.subject: Holmes
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-1-04-what-john-r.statement: Holmes dispatched a long telegram at the telegraph office.
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-1-04-what-john-r.quote: Sherlock Holmes led me to the nearest telegraph office, whence he dispatched a long telegram.

1887-a-study-in-scarlet-1-04-what-john-r.subject: Holmes
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-1-04-what-john-r.statement: Holmes ordered the cab driver to take him and Watson to the address Lestrade had given them.
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-1-04-what-john-r.quote: He then hailed a cab, and ordered the driver to take us to the address given us by Lestrade.

1887-a-study-in-scarlet-1-04-what-john-r.subject: Holmes
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-1-04-what-john-r.statement: Holmes said his mind was entirely made up about the case before hearing Rance's account.
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-1-04-what-john-r.quote: as a matter of fact, my mind is entirely made up upon the case, but still we may as well learn all that is to be learned.

1887-a-study-in-scarlet-1-04-what-john-r.subject: Holmes
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-1-04-what-john-r.statement: Holmes inferred that the cab had brought two individuals to the house during the night.
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-1-04-what-john-r.quote: it follows that it must have been there during the night, and, therefore, that it brought those two individuals to the house.

1887-a-study-in-scarlet-1-04-what-john-r.subject: Holmes
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-1-04-what-john-r.statement: Holmes said a man's height can usually be inferred from the length of his stride.
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-1-04-what-john-r.quote: the height of a man, in nine cases out of ten, can be told from the length of his stride.

1887-a-study-in-scarlet-1-04-what-john-r.subject: Holmes
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-1-04-what-john-r.statement: Holmes inferred that a man able to stride four and a half feet without effort could not be old.
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-1-04-what-john-r.quote: if a man can stride four and a-half feet without the smallest effort, he can’t be quite in the sere and yellow.

1887-a-study-in-scarlet-1-04-what-john-r.subject: Holmes
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-1-04-what-john-r.statement: Holmes inferred that the man's fingernail was not trimmed because it scratched the plaster while writing.
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-1-04-what-john-r.quote: My glass allowed me to observe that the plaster was slightly scratched in doing it, which would not have been the case if the man’s nail had been trimmed.

1887-a-study-in-scarlet-1-04-what-john-r.subject: Holmes
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-1-04-what-john-r.statement: Holmes identified the scattered ash as ash from a Trichinopoly cigar.
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-1-04-what-john-r.quote: It was dark in colour and flakey—such an ash as is only made by a Trichinopoly.

1887-a-study-in-scarlet-1-04-what-john-r.subject: Holmes
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-1-04-what-john-r.statement: Holmes concluded that the person who wrote RACHE was not German but a clumsy imitator.
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-1-04-what-john-r.quote: Now, a real German invariably prints in the Latin character, so that we may safely say that this was not written by one, but by a clumsy imitator who overdid his part.

1887-a-study-in-scarlet-1-04-what-john-r.subject: Holmes
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-1-04-what-john-r.statement: Holmes said the RACHE writing was a ruse to divert inquiry into a wrong channel.
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-1-04-what-john-r.quote: It was simply a ruse to divert inquiry into a wrong channel.

1887-a-study-in-scarlet-1-04-what-john-r.subject: Holmes
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-1-04-what-john-r.statement: Holmes told Watson that Patent-leathers and Square-toes came in the same cab and walked down the pathway together, probably arm-in-arm.
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-1-04-what-john-r.quote: Patent-leathers and Square-toes came in the same cab, and they walked down the pathway together as friendly as possible—arm-in-arm, in all probability.

1887-a-study-in-scarlet-1-04-what-john-r.subject: Holmes
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-1-04-what-john-r.statement: Holmes inferred that Square-toes became increasingly excited as he paced the room.
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-1-04-what-john-r.quote: I could read that as he walked he grew more and more excited.

1887-a-study-in-scarlet-1-04-what-john-r.subject: Holmes
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-1-04-what-john-r.statement: Holmes inferred that Square-toes was talking and working himself into a fury while he paced.
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-1-04-what-john-r.quote: He was talking all the while, and working himself up, no doubt, into a fury.

1887-a-study-in-scarlet-1-04-what-john-r.subject: Holmes
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-1-04-what-john-r.statement: Holmes said the tragedy occurred after Square-toes worked himself into a fury.
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-1-04-what-john-r.quote: Then the tragedy occurred.

1887-a-study-in-scarlet-1-04-what-john-r.subject: Holmes
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-1-04-what-john-r.statement: Holmes and Watson traveled by cab to Audley Court to question Rance.
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-1-04-what-john-r.quote: That’s Audley Court in there,” he said, pointing to a narrow slit in the line of dead-coloured brick.

1887-a-study-in-scarlet-1-04-what-john-r.subject: Rance
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-1-04-what-john-r.statement: Rance lived at Number 46, Audley Court.
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-1-04-what-john-r.quote: until we came to Number 46, the door of which was decorated with a small slip of brass on which the name Rance was engraved.

1887-a-study-in-scarlet-1-04-what-john-r.subject: Holmes
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-1-04-what-john-r.statement: Holmes offered Rance a half-sovereign to hear his account.
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-1-04-what-john-r.quote: Holmes took a half-sovereign from his pocket and played with it pensively.

1887-a-study-in-scarlet-1-04-what-john-r.subject: Rance
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-1-04-what-john-r.value: ten at night to six in the morning
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-1-04-what-john-r.statement: Rance said his working hours ran from ten at night to six in the morning.
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-1-04-what-john-r.quote: My time is from ten at night to six in the morning.

1887-a-study-in-scarlet-1-04-what-john-r.subject: Rance
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-1-04-what-john-r.statement: Rance reported that there was a fight at the White Hart at eleven.
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-1-04-what-john-r.quote: At eleven there was a fight at the ‘White Hart’;

1887-a-study-in-scarlet-1-04-what-john-r.subject: Rance
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-1-04-what-john-r.statement: At one o’clock, Rance met Harry Murcher and talked with him at the corner of Henrietta Street.
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-1-04-what-john-r.quote: At one o’clock it began to rain, and I met Harry Murcher—him who has the Holland Grove beat—and we stood together at the corner of Henrietta Street a-talkin’.

1887-a-study-in-scarlet-1-04-what-john-r.subject: Rance
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-1-04-what-john-r.statement: Around two or a little after, Rance went to check that all was right down Brixton Road.
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-1-04-what-john-r.quote: Presently—maybe about two or a little after—I thought I would take a look round and see that all was right down the Brixton Road.

1887-a-study-in-scarlet-1-04-what-john-r.subject: Rance
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-1-04-what-john-r.statement: Rance knew that the two houses in Lauriston Gardens were empty because their owner would not have the drains seen to.
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-1-04-what-john-r.quote: Now, I knew that them two houses in Lauriston Gardens was empty on account of him that owns them who won’t have the drains seen to, though the very last tenant what lived in one of them died o’ typhoid fever.

1887-a-study-in-scarlet-1-04-what-john-r.subject: last tenant
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-1-04-what-john-r.statement: The last tenant of one of the Lauriston Gardens houses died of typhoid fever.
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-1-04-what-john-r.quote: though the very last tenant what lived in one of them died o’ typhoid fever.

1887-a-study-in-scarlet-1-04-what-john-r.subject: Rance
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-1-04-what-john-r.statement: Rance saw a light in a window of the Lauriston Gardens house and suspected something was wrong.
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-1-04-what-john-r.quote: I was knocked all in a heap therefore at seeing a light in the window, and I suspected as something was wrong.

1887-a-study-in-scarlet-1-04-what-john-r.subject: Rance
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-1-04-what-john-r.statement: Rance walked back from the house door to the garden gate because the place was silent and lonely and he wanted someone with him.
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-1-04-what-john-r.quote: Ye see, when I got up to the door it was so still and so lonesome, that I thought I’d be none the worse for some one with me.

1887-a-study-in-scarlet-1-04-what-john-r.subject: Rance
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-1-04-what-john-r.statement: Rance went back to the gate to see whether he could see Murcher's lantern, but saw no sign of him or anyone else.
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-1-04-what-john-r.quote: The thought gave me a kind o’ turn, and I walked back to the gate to see if I could see Murcher’s lantern, but there wasn’t no sign of him nor of anyone else.

1887-a-study-in-scarlet-1-04-what-john-r.subject: Rance
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-1-04-what-john-r.statement: Rance pulled himself together, returned to the house, and pushed the door open.
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-1-04-what-john-r.quote: Then I pulled myself together and went back and pushed the door open.

1887-a-study-in-scarlet-1-04-what-john-r.subject: Rance
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-1-04-what-john-r.statement: After finding the interior quiet, Rance entered the room where a candle was burning.
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-1-04-what-john-r.quote: All was quiet inside, so I went into the room where the light was a-burnin’.

1887-a-study-in-scarlet-1-04-what-john-r.subject: candle
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-1-04-what-john-r.statement: The candle on the mantelpiece was red wax.
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-1-04-what-john-r.quote: There was a candle flickerin’ on the mantelpiece—a red wax one—and by its light I saw——

1887-a-study-in-scarlet-1-04-what-john-r.subject: Rance
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-1-04-what-john-r.statement: Rance returned to the gate and sounded his whistle, bringing Murcher and two others to the spot.
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-1-04-what-john-r.quote: I went back to the gate and sounded my whistle.

1887-a-study-in-scarlet-1-04-what-john-r.subject: Murcher
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-1-04-what-john-r.statement: Murcher and two others came to the spot after Rance sounded his whistle.
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-1-04-what-john-r.quote: That brought Murcher and two more to the spot.

1887-a-study-in-scarlet-1-04-what-john-r.subject: drunk man
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-1-04-what-john-r.statement: The drunk man was leaning against the railings at the gate when Rance came out.
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-1-04-what-john-r.quote: He was at the gate when I came out, a-leanin’ up agin the railings, and a-singin’ at the pitch o’ his lungs about Columbine’s New-fangled Banner, or some such stuff.

1887-a-study-in-scarlet-1-04-what-john-r.subject: drunk man
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-1-04-what-john-r.statement: The drunk man was too drunk to stand or help.
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-1-04-what-john-r.quote: He couldn’t stand, far less help.

1887-a-study-in-scarlet-1-04-what-john-r.subject: drunk man
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-1-04-what-john-r.value: long chap with a red face and lower part muffled
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-1-04-what-john-r.statement: Rance described the drunk man as a long man with a red face and his lower part muffled.
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-1-04-what-john-r.quote: He was a long chap, with a red face, the lower part muffled round——

1887-a-study-in-scarlet-1-04-what-john-r.subject: drunk man
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-1-04-what-john-r.statement: The drunk man wore a brown overcoat.
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-1-04-what-john-r.quote: “A brown overcoat.”

1887-a-study-in-scarlet-1-04-what-john-r.subject: drunk man
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-1-04-what-john-r.statement: Rance said the drunk man did not have a whip in his hand.
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-1-04-what-john-r.quote: “A whip—no.”

1887-a-study-in-scarlet-1-04-what-john-r.subject: Holmes
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-1-04-what-john-r.statement: Holmes told Rance that the drunk man he had held was the man who held the clue to the mystery and whom they were seeking.
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-1-04-what-john-r.quote: The man whom you held in your hands is the man who holds the clue of this mystery, and whom we are seeking.

1887-a-study-in-scarlet-1-04-what-john-r.subject: Holmes
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-1-04-what-john-r.statement: Holmes gave Rance a half-sovereign before leaving.
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-1-04-what-john-r.quote: “There’s a half-sovereign for you,” my companion said, standing up and taking his hat.

1887-a-study-in-scarlet-1-04-what-john-r.subject: Holmes
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-1-04-what-john-r.statement: Holmes and Watson drove back to their lodgings by cab.
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-1-04-what-john-r.quote: as we drove back to our lodgings.

1887-a-study-in-scarlet-1-04-what-john-r.subject: Holmes
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-1-04-what-john-r.statement: Holmes said the man returned to the house to retrieve the ring.
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-1-04-what-john-r.quote: The ring, man, the ring: that was what he came back for.

1887-a-study-in-scarlet-1-04-what-john-r.subject: Holmes
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-1-04-what-john-r.statement: Holmes said they could use the ring as bait to catch the man if they had no other way.
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-1-04-what-john-r.quote: If we have no other way of catching him, we can always bait our line with the ring.

1887-a-study-in-scarlet-1-04-what-john-r.subject: Holmes
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-1-04-what-john-r.statement: Holmes planned to go to Halle’s concert to hear Norman Neruda that afternoon.
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-1-04-what-john-r.quote: We must hurry up, for I want to go to Halle’s concert to hear Norman Neruda this afternoon.

1887-a-study-in-scarlet-1-05-our-adverti.subject: Watson
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-1-05-our-adverti.statement: Watson is Dr. Watson.
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-1-05-our-adverti.quote: “Does Dr. Watson live here?”

1887-a-study-in-scarlet-1-05-our-adverti.subject: Holmes
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-1-05-our-adverti.statement: Holmes gives Watson a ring to use as a facsimile of the missing wedding ring.
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-1-05-our-adverti.quote: “Oh yes, you have,” said he, handing me one. “This will do very well. It is almost a facsimile.”

1887-a-study-in-scarlet-1-05-our-adverti.subject: Holmes
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-1-05-our-adverti.statement: Holmes places an advertisement in every paper announcing that a gold wedding ring was found in Brixton Road.
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-1-05-our-adverti.quote: “I had one sent to every paper this morning immediately after the affair.”

1887-a-study-in-scarlet-1-05-our-adverti.subject: Holmes
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-1-05-our-adverti.statement: Holmes predicts that the man in the brown coat will answer the ring advertisement, either in person or through an accomplice.
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-1-05-our-adverti.quote: “Why, the man in the brown coat—our florid friend with the square toes. If he does not come himself he will send an accomplice.”

1887-a-study-in-scarlet-1-05-our-adverti.subject: Holmes
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-1-05-our-adverti.statement: Holmes believes the man in the brown coat dropped the ring while stooping over Drebber’s body.
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-1-05-our-adverti.quote: “According to my notion he dropped it while stooping over Drebber’s body, and did not miss it at the time.”

1887-a-study-in-scarlet-1-05-our-adverti.subject: Holmes
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-1-05-our-adverti.statement: Holmes believes the man returned to the house after discovering his loss but found the police already there.
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-1-05-our-adverti.quote: After leaving the house he discovered his loss and hurried back, but found the police already in possession, owing to his own folly in leaving the candle burning.

1887-a-study-in-scarlet-1-05-our-adverti.subject: Holmes
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-1-05-our-adverti.statement: Holmes believes the man pretended to be drunk to allay suspicion at the gate.
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-1-05-our-adverti.quote: He had to pretend to be drunk in order to allay the suspicions which might have been aroused by his appearance at the gate.

1887-a-study-in-scarlet-1-05-our-adverti.subject: Watson
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-1-05-our-adverti.statement: Watson cleans and loads his old service revolver in preparation for the visitor.
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-1-05-our-adverti.quote: I went to my bedroom and followed his advice.

1887-a-study-in-scarlet-1-05-our-adverti.subject: Holmes
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-1-05-our-adverti.statement: Holmes receives an answer to his American telegram and says it confirms his view of the case.
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-1-05-our-adverti.quote: “The plot thickens,” he said, as I entered; “I have just had an answer to my American telegram. My view of the case is the correct one.”

1887-a-study-in-scarlet-1-05-our-adverti.subject: Watson
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-1-05-our-adverti.statement: Watson opens the door slightly and puts the key on the inside at Holmes’s instruction.
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-1-05-our-adverti.quote: Open the door slightly. That will do. Now put the key on the inside.

1887-a-study-in-scarlet-1-05-our-adverti.subject: Holmes
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-1-05-our-adverti.statement: Holmes expects the visitor to arrive within a few minutes after eight o’clock.
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-1-05-our-adverti.quote: “Yes. He will probably be here in a few minutes.”

1887-a-study-in-scarlet-1-05-our-adverti.subject: Mrs. Sawyer
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-1-05-our-adverti.statement: Mrs. Sawyer arrives at 221B Baker Street in response to the ring advertisement.
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-1-05-our-adverti.quote: At my summons, instead of the man of violence whom we expected, a very old and wrinkled woman hobbled into the apartment.

1887-a-study-in-scarlet-1-05-our-adverti.subject: Mrs. Sawyer
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-1-05-our-adverti.statement: Mrs. Sawyer claims the ring belongs to her daughter Sally.
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-1-05-our-adverti.quote: “It belongs to my girl Sally, as was married only this time twelvemonth”

1887-a-study-in-scarlet-1-05-our-adverti.subject: Sally
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-1-05-our-adverti.statement: Sally is married to Tom Dennis.
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-1-05-our-adverti.quote: “My name is Sawyer—hers is Dennis, which Tom Dennis married her”

1887-a-study-in-scarlet-1-05-our-adverti.subject: Tom Dennis
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-1-05-our-adverti.statement: Tom Dennis is a steward aboard a Union boat.
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-1-05-our-adverti.quote: “which her husband is steward aboard a Union boat”

1887-a-study-in-scarlet-1-05-our-adverti.subject: Mrs. Sawyer
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-1-05-our-adverti.statement: Mrs. Sawyer gives her address as 13, Duncan Street, Houndsditch.
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-1-05-our-adverti.quote: “13, Duncan Street, Houndsditch. A weary way from here.”

1887-a-study-in-scarlet-1-05-our-adverti.subject: Sally
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-1-05-our-adverti.statement: Sally lives in lodgings at 3, Mayfield Place, Peckham.
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-1-05-our-adverti.quote: “Sally lives in lodgings at 3, Mayfield Place, Peckham.”

1887-a-study-in-scarlet-1-05-our-adverti.subject: Holmes
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-1-05-our-adverti.statement: Holmes points out that Brixton Road does not lie between a circus and Houndsditch.
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-1-05-our-adverti.quote: “The Brixton Road does not lie between any circus and Houndsditch,” said Sherlock Holmes sharply.

1887-a-study-in-scarlet-1-05-our-adverti.subject: Watson
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-1-05-our-adverti.statement: Watson hands the ring to Mrs. Sawyer, saying it belongs to her daughter.
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-1-05-our-adverti.quote: “Here is your ring, Mrs. Sawyer,” I interrupted, in obedience to a sign from my companion; “it clearly belongs to your daughter, and I am glad to be able to restore it to the rightful owner.”

1887-a-study-in-scarlet-1-05-our-adverti.subject: Holmes
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-1-05-our-adverti.statement: Holmes follows Mrs. Sawyer after she leaves, believing she is an accomplice who will lead him to the man.
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-1-05-our-adverti.quote: “I’ll follow her,” he said, hurriedly; “she must be an accomplice, and will lead me to him.”

1887-a-study-in-scarlet-1-05-our-adverti.subject: Holmes
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-1-05-our-adverti.statement: Holmes follows Mrs. Sawyer at a distance along the street.
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-1-05-our-adverti.quote: Looking through the window I could see her walking feebly along the other side, while her pursuer dogged her some little distance behind.

1887-a-study-in-scarlet-1-05-our-adverti.subject: Mrs. Sawyer
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-1-05-our-adverti.statement: The person disguised as Mrs. Sawyer hails a passing four-wheeler and gives the driver the address 13, Duncan Street, Houndsditch.
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-1-05-our-adverti.quote: Presently she came to a halt, and hailed a four-wheeler which was passing.

1887-a-study-in-scarlet-1-05-our-adverti.subject: Holmes
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-1-05-our-adverti.statement: Holmes follows the four-wheeler by riding behind it.
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-1-05-our-adverti.quote: I hopped off before we came to the door, and strolled down the street in an easy, lounging way.

1887-a-study-in-scarlet-1-05-our-adverti.subject: disguised man
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-1-05-our-adverti.statement: The disguised man escapes from the moving four-wheeler without Holmes or the driver seeing him leave.
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-1-05-our-adverti.quote: “You don’t mean to say,” I cried, in amazement, “that that tottering, feeble old woman was able to get out of the cab while it was in motion, without either you or the driver seeing her?”

1887-a-study-in-scarlet-1-05-our-adverti.subject: disguised man
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-1-05-our-adverti.value: a young man and an active, incomparable actor
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-1-05-our-adverti.statement: The person disguised as the old woman is a young, active man and an incomparable actor.
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-1-05-our-adverti.quote: “It must have been a young man, and an active one, too, besides being an incomparable actor.”

1887-a-study-in-scarlet-1-05-our-adverti.subject: Holmes
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-1-05-our-adverti.statement: Holmes concludes that the man they are pursuing has friends willing to take risks for him.
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-1-05-our-adverti.quote: “It shows that the man we are after is not as lonely as I imagined he was, but has friends who are ready to risk something for him.”

1887-a-study-in-scarlet-1-05-our-adverti.subject: Holmes
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-1-05-our-adverti.statement: Holmes recognizes that the visitor was not an old woman but a man in disguise.
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-1-05-our-adverti.quote: “Old woman be damned!” said Sherlock Holmes, sharply. “We were the old women to be so taken in.”

1887-a-study-in-scarlet-1-05-our-adverti.subject: Holmes
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-1-05-our-adverti.statement: Holmes returns to Baker Street close upon midnight after failing to catch the disguised man.
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-1-05-our-adverti.quote: It was close upon twelve before I heard the sharp sound of his latch-key.

1887-a-study-in-scarlet-1-05-our-adverti.subject: Holmes
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-1-05-our-adverti.statement: Holmes says he would not want Scotland Yard to learn that he was deceived by the disguise.
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-1-05-our-adverti.quote: “I wouldn’t have the Scotland Yarders know it for the world,” he cried, dropping into his chair; “I have chaffed them so much that they would never have let me hear the end of it.”

1887-a-study-in-scarlet-1-05-our-adverti.subject: Watson
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-1-05-our-adverti.statement: Watson follows Holmes’s advice and goes to bed.
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-1-05-our-adverti.quote: I was certainly feeling very weary, so I obeyed his injunction.

1887-a-study-in-scarlet-1-05-our-adverti.subject: Holmes
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-1-05-our-adverti.statement: Holmes remains awake, playing melancholy music on his violin while pondering the case.
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-1-05-our-adverti.quote: I left Holmes seated in front of the smouldering fire, and long into the watches of the night I heard the low, melancholy wailings of his violin, and knew that he was still pondering over the strange problem which he had set himself to unravel.

1887-a-study-in-scarlet-1-06-tobias-greg.subject: Holmes
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-1-06-tobias-greg.object: Baker Street division of the detective police force
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-1-06-tobias-greg.statement: Holmes employs the Baker Street division of the detective police force on the Brixton case.
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-1-06-tobias-greg.quote:
“Is it on this Brixton case that you are employing them?” I asked.

“Yes; there is a point which I wish to ascertain.

1887-a-study-in-scarlet-1-06-tobias-greg.subject: Holmes
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-1-06-tobias-greg.statement: Holmes orders the youths to send Wiggins alone to report and tells the rest to wait in the street.
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-1-06-tobias-greg.quote: “In future you shall send up Wiggins alone to report, and the rest of you must wait in the street.

1887-a-study-in-scarlet-1-06-tobias-greg.subject: Holmes
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-1-06-tobias-greg.object: Baker Street division of the detective police force
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-1-06-tobias-greg.statement: Holmes hands each of the six youths a shilling as wages.
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-1-06-tobias-greg.quote: He handed each of them a shilling.

1887-a-study-in-scarlet-1-06-tobias-greg.subject: Holmes
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-1-06-tobias-greg.object: Baker Street division of the detective police force
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-1-06-tobias-greg.statement: Holmes tells the youths to keep searching until they find the point he wants to ascertain.
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-1-06-tobias-greg.quote: “I hardly expected you would. You must keep on until you do.

1887-a-study-in-scarlet-1-06-tobias-greg.subject: Holmes
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-1-06-tobias-greg.value: a point on the Brixton case
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-1-06-tobias-greg.statement: Holmes is employing the youths to ascertain a point in the Brixton case.
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-1-06-tobias-greg.quote: “Yes; there is a point which I wish to ascertain.

1887-a-study-in-scarlet-1-06-tobias-greg.subject: Holmes
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-1-06-tobias-greg.value: the youths go everywhere and hear everything
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-1-06-tobias-greg.statement: Holmes says the youths go everywhere and hear everything, and that they are sharp but need organisation.
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-1-06-tobias-greg.quote: These youngsters, however, go everywhere and hear everything. They are as sharp as needles, too; all they want is organisation.

1887-a-study-in-scarlet-1-06-tobias-greg.subject: Gregson
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-1-06-tobias-greg.statement: Gregson identifies Arthur Charpentier as the man he has under lock and key.
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-1-06-tobias-greg.quote:
“The right track! Why, sir, we have the man under lock and key.”

“And his name is?”

“Arthur Charpentier, sub-lieutenant in Her Majesty’s navy,” cried Gregson

1887-a-study-in-scarlet-1-06-tobias-greg.subject: Arthur Charpentier
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-1-06-tobias-greg.statement: Arthur Charpentier is a sub-lieutenant in Her Majesty’s navy.
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-1-06-tobias-greg.quote: “Arthur Charpentier, sub-lieutenant in Her Majesty’s navy,”

1887-a-study-in-scarlet-1-06-tobias-greg.subject: Gregson
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-1-06-tobias-greg.statement: Gregson traces Drebber’s hat to Charpentier’s Boarding Establishment and obtains Drebber’s address.
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-1-06-tobias-greg.quote: He had sent the hat to a Mr. Drebber, residing at Charpentier’s Boarding Establishment, Torquay Terrace. Thus I got at his address.

1887-a-study-in-scarlet-1-06-tobias-greg.subject: Charpentier’s Boarding Establishment
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-1-06-tobias-greg.statement: Charpentier’s Boarding Establishment is on Torquay Terrace.
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-1-06-tobias-greg.quote: He had sent the hat to a Mr. Drebber, residing at Charpentier’s Boarding Establishment, Torquay Terrace.

1887-a-study-in-scarlet-1-06-tobias-greg.subject: Gregson
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-1-06-tobias-greg.statement: Gregson questions Madame Charpentier about Drebber’s departure for the train.
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-1-06-tobias-greg.quote: ‘At what o’clock did Mr. Drebber leave your house for the train?’ I asked.

1887-a-study-in-scarlet-1-06-tobias-greg.subject: Madame Charpentier
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-1-06-tobias-greg.statement: Madame Charpentier says Drebber had boarded with her for nearly three weeks.
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-1-06-tobias-greg.quote: ‘Mr. Drebber has been with us nearly three weeks.

1887-a-study-in-scarlet-1-06-tobias-greg.subject: Drebber
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-1-06-tobias-greg.statement: Drebber and Stangerson had been travelling on the Continent together.
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-1-06-tobias-greg.quote: He and his secretary, Mr. Stangerson, had been travelling on the Continent.

1887-a-study-in-scarlet-1-06-tobias-greg.subject: Drebber
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-1-06-tobias-greg.statement: Madame Charpentier says Copenhagen was the last stopping place shown by the labels on Drebber and Stangerson’s trunks.
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-1-06-tobias-greg.quote: I noticed a “Copenhagen” label upon each of their trunks, showing that that had been their last stopping place.

1887-a-study-in-scarlet-1-06-tobias-greg.subject: Stangerson
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-1-06-tobias-greg.statement: Madame Charpentier describes Stangerson as a quiet, reserved man.
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-1-06-tobias-greg.quote: Stangerson was a quiet reserved man,

1887-a-study-in-scarlet-1-06-tobias-greg.subject: Drebber
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-1-06-tobias-greg.value: coarse in his habits and brutish in his ways
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-1-06-tobias-greg.statement: Madame Charpentier describes Drebber as coarse in his habits and brutish in his ways.
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-1-06-tobias-greg.quote: He was coarse in his habits and brutish in his ways.

1887-a-study-in-scarlet-1-06-tobias-greg.subject: Drebber
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-1-06-tobias-greg.value: after twelve o’clock in the day he could hardly ever be said to be sober
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-1-06-tobias-greg.statement: Madame Charpentier says Drebber was rarely sober after noon.
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-1-06-tobias-greg.quote: after twelve o’clock in the day he could hardly ever be said to be sober.

1887-a-study-in-scarlet-1-06-tobias-greg.subject: Drebber
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-1-06-tobias-greg.statement: Madame Charpentier says Drebber seized Alice and embraced her on one occasion.
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-1-06-tobias-greg.quote: On one occasion he actually seized her in his arms and embraced her—an outrage which caused his own secretary to reproach him for his unmanly conduct.

1887-a-study-in-scarlet-1-06-tobias-greg.subject: Stangerson
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-1-06-tobias-greg.statement: Stangerson reproached Drebber for embracing Alice.
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-1-06-tobias-greg.quote: an outrage which caused his own secretary to reproach him for his unmanly conduct.

1887-a-study-in-scarlet-1-06-tobias-greg.subject: Madame Charpentier
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-1-06-tobias-greg.statement: Madame Charpentier gave Drebber notice to leave after his conduct toward Alice.
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-1-06-tobias-greg.quote: This last was too much, however, and I gave him notice to leave on account of it.

1887-a-study-in-scarlet-1-06-tobias-greg.subject: Drebber
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-1-06-tobias-greg.statement: Drebber left the boarding establishment after Madame Charpentier gave him notice.
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-1-06-tobias-greg.quote: That was the reason of his going.

1887-a-study-in-scarlet-1-06-tobias-greg.subject: Drebber
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-1-06-tobias-greg.statement: Madame Charpentier says Drebber returned to the boarding establishment less than an hour after leaving.
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-1-06-tobias-greg.quote: Alas, in less than an hour there was a ring at the bell, and I learned that Mr. Drebber had returned.

1887-a-study-in-scarlet-1-06-tobias-greg.subject: Drebber
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-1-06-tobias-greg.statement: Drebber proposed that Alice fly away with him.
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-1-06-tobias-greg.quote: He then turned to Alice, and before my very face, proposed to her that she should fly with him.

1887-a-study-in-scarlet-1-06-tobias-greg.subject: Drebber
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-1-06-tobias-greg.statement: Drebber caught Alice by the wrist and tried to draw her toward the door.
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-1-06-tobias-greg.quote: Poor Alice was so frightened that she shrunk away from him, but he caught her by the wrist and endeavoured to draw her towards the door.

1887-a-study-in-scarlet-1-06-tobias-greg.subject: Arthur Charpentier
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-1-06-tobias-greg.statement: Arthur came into the room while Drebber was trying to pull Alice toward the door.
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-1-06-tobias-greg.quote: I screamed, and at that moment my son Arthur came into the room.

1887-a-study-in-scarlet-1-06-tobias-greg.subject: Arthur Charpentier
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-1-06-tobias-greg.statement: Arthur said he would follow Drebber and see what he did, then took his hat and left.
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-1-06-tobias-greg.quote: “I will just go after him and see what he does with himself.” With those words he took his hat and started off down the street.

1887-a-study-in-scarlet-1-06-tobias-greg.subject: Arthur Charpentier
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-1-06-tobias-greg.statement: Gregson says Arthur still carried the stout oak cudgel his mother described.
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-1-06-tobias-greg.quote: He still carried the heavy stick which the mother described him as having with him when he followed Drebber. It was a stout oak cudgel.

1887-a-study-in-scarlet-1-06-tobias-greg.subject: Gregson
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-1-06-tobias-greg.statement: Gregson found Arthur and arrested him with two officers.
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-1-06-tobias-greg.quote: I found out where Lieutenant Charpentier was, took two officers with me, and arrested him.

1887-a-study-in-scarlet-1-06-tobias-greg.subject: Arthur Charpentier
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-1-06-tobias-greg.value: he supposes he is being arrested for being concerned in Drebber’s death
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-1-06-tobias-greg.statement: When arrested, Arthur said he supposed he was being arrested for involvement in Drebber’s death.
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-1-06-tobias-greg.quote: ‘I suppose you are arresting me for being concerned in the death of that scoundrel Drebber,’ he said.

1887-a-study-in-scarlet-1-06-tobias-greg.subject: Gregson
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-1-06-tobias-greg.statement: Gregson theorizes that Arthur followed Drebber to Brixton Road and killed him with a blow from the stick.
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-1-06-tobias-greg.quote: my theory is that he followed Drebber as far as the Brixton Road. When there, a fresh altercation arose between them, in the course of which Drebber received a blow from the stick, in the pit of the stomach, perhaps, which killed him without leaving any mark.

1887-a-study-in-scarlet-1-06-tobias-greg.subject: Arthur Charpentier
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-1-06-tobias-greg.statement: Arthur said that after following Drebber, Drebber noticed him and took a cab to get away.
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-1-06-tobias-greg.quote: The young man volunteered a statement, in which he said that after following Drebber some time, the latter perceived him, and took a cab in order to get away from him.

1887-a-study-in-scarlet-1-06-tobias-greg.subject: Arthur Charpentier
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-1-06-tobias-greg.statement: Arthur said he met an old shipmate on his way home and took a long walk with him.
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-1-06-tobias-greg.quote: On his way home he met an old shipmate, and took a long walk with him.

1887-a-study-in-scarlet-1-06-tobias-greg.subject: Lestrade
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-1-06-tobias-greg.statement: Lestrade is pursuing Stangerson in connection with the case.
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-1-06-tobias-greg.quote: He is after the secretary Stangerson,

1887-a-study-in-scarlet-1-06-tobias-greg.subject: Lestrade
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-1-06-tobias-greg.statement: Lestrade reports that Stangerson was murdered at Halliday’s Private Hotel about six o’clock that morning.
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-1-06-tobias-greg.quote: “The Secretary, Mr. Joseph Stangerson,” said Lestrade gravely, “was murdered at Halliday’s Private Hotel about six o’clock this morning.”

1887-a-study-in-scarlet-1-06-tobias-greg.subject: Halliday’s Private Hotel
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-1-06-tobias-greg.statement: Stangerson was murdered at Halliday’s Private Hotel.
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-1-06-tobias-greg.quote: was murdered at Halliday’s Private Hotel about six o’clock this morning.

1887-a-study-in-scarlet-1-06-tobias-greg.subject: The Standard
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-1-06-tobias-greg.statement: The Standard reports that Drebber and Stangerson bade farewell to their landlady on Tuesday the 4th and left for Euston Station intending to catch the Liverpool express.
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-1-06-tobias-greg.quote: The two bade adieu to their landlady upon Tuesday, the 4th inst., and departed to Euston Station with the avowed intention of catching the Liverpool express.

1887-a-study-in-scarlet-1-06-tobias-greg.subject: Drebber
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-1-06-tobias-greg.statement: The Standard reports that Drebber’s body was discovered in an empty house in Brixton Road.
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-1-06-tobias-greg.quote: Mr. Drebber’s body was, as recorded, discovered in an empty house in the Brixton Road, many miles from Euston.

1887-a-study-in-scarlet-1-06-tobias-greg.subject: Holmes
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-1-06-tobias-greg.value: Drebber’s hat was made by John Underwood and Sons, 129 Camberwell Road
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-1-06-tobias-greg.statement: Holmes knows the maker and address printed on Drebber’s hat.
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-1-06-tobias-greg.quote: “Yes,” said Holmes; “by John Underwood and Sons, 129, Camberwell Road.”

1887-a-study-in-scarlet-1-06-tobias-greg.subject: Madame Charpentier
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-1-06-tobias-greg.statement: Madame Charpentier says Drebber left her house for the train at eight o’clock.
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-1-06-tobias-greg.quote: ‘At eight o’clock,’ she said, gulping in her throat to keep down her agitation.

1887-a-study-in-scarlet-1-06-tobias-greg.subject: Stangerson
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-1-06-tobias-greg.statement: Stangerson told Madame Charpentier that there were trains at 9.15 and 11, and that Drebber was to catch the first.
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-1-06-tobias-greg.quote: ‘His secretary, Mr. Stangerson, said that there were two trains—one at 9.15 and one at 11. He was to catch the first.’

1887-a-study-in-scarlet-1-06-tobias-greg.subject: Madame Charpentier
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-1-06-tobias-greg.statement: Madame Charpentier says she saw Drebber again after he left for the train.
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-1-06-tobias-greg.quote: “‘No good can ever come of falsehood, mother,’ she said. ‘Let us be frank with this gentleman. We did see Mr. Drebber again.’”

1887-a-study-in-scarlet-1-06-tobias-greg.subject: Madame Charpentier
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-1-06-tobias-greg.statement: Madame Charpentier says Arthur is utterly innocent of Drebber’s death.
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-1-06-tobias-greg.quote: He is utterly innocent of it.

1887-a-study-in-scarlet-1-06-tobias-greg.subject: Madame Charpentier
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-1-06-tobias-greg.statement: Madame Charpentier says Drebber was much excited and evidently drunk when he returned.
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-1-06-tobias-greg.quote: He was much excited, and evidently the worse for drink.

1887-a-study-in-scarlet-1-06-tobias-greg.subject: Madame Charpentier
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-1-06-tobias-greg.statement: Madame Charpentier says Arthur returned after she had gone to bed and let himself in with a latch-key.
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-1-06-tobias-greg.quote: ‘No; he has a latch-key, and he let himself in.’

1887-a-study-in-scarlet-1-06-tobias-greg.subject: Madame Charpentier
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-1-06-tobias-greg.statement: Madame Charpentier says she went to bed about eleven.
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-1-06-tobias-greg.quote: ‘About eleven.’

1887-a-study-in-scarlet-1-06-tobias-greg.subject: Gregson
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-1-06-tobias-greg.statement: Gregson treats the unexplained hours after Arthur left as suspicious and arrests him.
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-1-06-tobias-greg.quote:
‘What was he doing during that time?’

‘“I do not know,” she answered, turning white to her very lips.’

Of course after that there was nothing more to be done.

1887-a-study-in-scarlet-1-07-light-in-th.subject: Lestrade
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-1-07-light-in-th.statement: Lestrade says he was the first to discover what had happened to Stangerson.
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-1-07-light-in-th.quote: I was the first to discover what had occurred.

1887-a-study-in-scarlet-1-07-light-in-th.subject: Lestrade
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-1-07-light-in-th.value: Stangerson was concerned in Drebber's death
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-1-07-light-in-th.statement: Lestrade had believed Stangerson was involved in Drebber's death.
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-1-07-light-in-th.quote: I freely confess that I was of the opinion that Stangerson was concerned in the death of Drebber.

1887-a-study-in-scarlet-1-07-light-in-th.subject: Lestrade
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-1-07-light-in-th.statement: Lestrade telegraphs Liverpool a description of Stangerson and warns them to watch the American boats.
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-1-07-light-in-th.quote: I telegraphed to Liverpool, giving a description of the man, and warning them to keep a watch upon the American boats.

1887-a-study-in-scarlet-1-07-light-in-th.subject: Lestrade
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-1-07-light-in-th.statement: Lestrade calls at hotels and lodging-houses near Euston to look for Stangerson.
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-1-07-light-in-th.quote: I then set to work calling upon all the hotels and lodging-houses in the vicinity of Euston.

1887-a-study-in-scarlet-1-07-light-in-th.subject: Lestrade
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-1-07-light-in-th.statement: Lestrade reaches Halliday’s Private Hotel while searching for Stangerson.
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-1-07-light-in-th.quote: This morning I began very early, and at eight o’clock I reached Halliday’s Private Hotel, in Little George Street.

1887-a-study-in-scarlet-1-07-light-in-th.subject: Stangerson
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-1-07-light-in-th.statement: Stangerson had been waiting for a gentleman for two days.
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-1-07-light-in-th.quote: He has been waiting for a gentleman for two days.

1887-a-study-in-scarlet-1-07-light-in-th.subject: Lestrade
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-1-07-light-in-th.statement: Lestrade finds Stangerson dead in his hotel room.
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-1-07-light-in-th.quote: The window of the room was open, and beside the window, all huddled up, lay the body of a man in his nightdress.

1887-a-study-in-scarlet-1-07-light-in-th.subject: Stangerson
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-1-07-light-in-th.statement: Stangerson was using the name Joseph Stangerson.
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-1-07-light-in-th.quote: the same gentleman who had engaged the room under the name of Joseph Stangerson.

1887-a-study-in-scarlet-1-07-light-in-th.subject: Stangerson
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-1-07-light-in-th.statement: Stangerson is dead when Lestrade finds him.
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-1-07-light-in-th.quote: He was quite dead, and had been for some time, for his limbs were rigid and cold.

1887-a-study-in-scarlet-1-07-light-in-th.subject: Stangerson
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-1-07-light-in-th.statement: Stangerson has a deep stab wound in his left side.
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-1-07-light-in-th.quote: The cause of death was a deep stab in the left side, which must have penetrated the heart.

1887-a-study-in-scarlet-1-07-light-in-th.subject: Stangerson
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-1-07-light-in-th.statement: Jefferson Hope murdered Stangerson.
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-1-07-light-in-th.quote: let me introduce you to Mr. Jefferson Hope, the murderer of Enoch Drebber and of Joseph Stangerson.

1887-a-study-in-scarlet-1-07-light-in-th.subject: unknown assassin
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-1-07-light-in-th.statement: The assassin writes RACHE above Stangerson’s body in blood.
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-1-07-light-in-th.quote: The word RACHE, written in letters of blood,

1887-a-study-in-scarlet-1-07-light-in-th.subject: milk boy
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-1-07-light-in-th.statement: A milk boy sees a man descend a ladder at the hotel after Stangerson’s murder.
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-1-07-light-in-th.quote: After passing, he looked back and saw a man descend the ladder.

1887-a-study-in-scarlet-1-07-light-in-th.subject: milk boy
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-1-07-light-in-th.value: tall, reddish-faced, wearing a long brownish coat
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-1-07-light-in-th.statement: The milk boy recalls the man as tall, reddish-faced, and dressed in a long brownish coat.
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-1-07-light-in-th.quote: He has an impression that the man was tall, had a reddish face, and was dressed in a long, brownish coat.

1887-a-study-in-scarlet-1-07-light-in-th.subject: Jefferson Hope
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-1-07-light-in-th.statement: After the murder, Jefferson Hope washes his hands in the room’s basin.
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-1-07-light-in-th.quote: we found blood-stained water in the basin, where he had washed his hands,

1887-a-study-in-scarlet-1-07-light-in-th.subject: Jefferson Hope
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-1-07-light-in-th.statement: Jefferson Hope deliberately wipes his knife on the sheets after the murder.
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-1-07-light-in-th.quote: and marks on the sheets where he had deliberately wiped his knife.

1887-a-study-in-scarlet-1-07-light-in-th.subject: Holmes
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-1-07-light-in-th.statement: Holmes says he knows the assassin’s name and expects to capture him shortly.
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-1-07-light-in-th.quote: You have asked me if I know the name of the assassin. I do.

1887-a-study-in-scarlet-1-07-light-in-th.subject: Holmes
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-1-07-light-in-th.value: There will be no more murders
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-1-07-light-in-th.statement: Holmes says there will be no more murders.
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-1-07-light-in-th.quote: There will be no more murders,

1887-a-study-in-scarlet-1-07-light-in-th.subject: Lestrade
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-1-07-light-in-th.statement: Lestrade takes the pills, purse, and telegram from Stangerson’s room for safekeeping at the police station.
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-1-07-light-in-th.quote: I took them and the purse and the telegram, intending to have them put in a place of safety at the Police Station.

1887-a-study-in-scarlet-1-07-light-in-th.subject: pills
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-1-07-light-in-th.value: one deadly poison pill and one harmless pill
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-1-07-light-in-th.statement: The box contains one deadly poison pill and one entirely harmless pill.
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-1-07-light-in-th.quote: Of the two pills in that box one was of the most deadly poison, and the other was entirely harmless.

1887-a-study-in-scarlet-1-07-light-in-th.subject: Holmes
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-1-07-light-in-th.statement: Holmes dissolves half a pill in water, adds milk, and gives it to the terrier, which remains alive.
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-1-07-light-in-th.quote: The dog continued to lie stretched upon the cushion, breathing in a laboured way, but apparently neither the better nor the worse for its draught.

1887-a-study-in-scarlet-1-07-light-in-th.subject: Holmes
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-1-07-light-in-th.statement: Holmes dissolves the other half-pill, adds milk, and gives it to the terrier, which dies.
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-1-07-light-in-th.quote: The unfortunate creature’s tongue seemed hardly to have been moistened in it before it gave a convulsive shiver in every limb, and lay as rigid and lifeless as if it had been struck by lightning.

1887-a-study-in-scarlet-1-07-light-in-th.subject: terrier
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-1-07-light-in-th.statement: The terrier dies after drinking the second pill mixture.
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-1-07-light-in-th.quote: and lay as rigid and lifeless as if it had been struck by lightning.

1887-a-study-in-scarlet-1-07-light-in-th.subject: Holmes
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-1-07-light-in-th.statement: Holmes refuses to reveal the assassin’s name until he can do so without endangering his plans.
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-1-07-light-in-th.quote: At present I am ready to promise that the instant that I can communicate with you without endangering my own combinations, I shall do so.

1887-a-study-in-scarlet-1-07-light-in-th.subject: Wiggins
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-1-07-light-in-th.statement: Wiggins tells Holmes that he has the cab downstairs.
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-1-07-light-in-th.quote: “Please, sir,” he said, touching his forelock, “I have the cab downstairs.”

1887-a-study-in-scarlet-1-07-light-in-th.subject: Holmes
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-1-07-light-in-th.statement: Holmes handcuffs the cabman and identifies him as Jefferson Hope, murderer of Drebber and Stangerson.
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-1-07-light-in-th.quote: “Gentlemen,” he cried, with flashing eyes, “let me introduce you to Mr. Jefferson Hope, the murderer of Enoch Drebber and of Joseph Stangerson.”

1887-a-study-in-scarlet-1-07-light-in-th.subject: Jefferson Hope
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-1-07-light-in-th.statement: After being handcuffed, Hope breaks through the window in an attempt to escape.
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-1-07-light-in-th.quote: Then, with an inarticulate roar of fury, the prisoner wrenched himself free from Holmes’s grasp, and hurled himself through the window.

1887-a-study-in-scarlet-1-07-light-in-th.subject: Holmes
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-1-07-light-in-th.statement: Holmes, Gregson, and Lestrade help seize Hope after he jumps through the window.
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-1-07-light-in-th.quote: but before he got quite through, Gregson, Lestrade, and Holmes sprang upon him like so many staghounds.

1887-a-study-in-scarlet-1-07-light-in-th.subject: Lestrade
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-1-07-light-in-th.statement: Lestrade half-strangles Hope until he stops resisting.
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-1-07-light-in-th.quote: It was not until Lestrade succeeded in getting his hand inside his neckcloth and half-strangling him that we made him realize that his struggles were of no avail;

1887-a-study-in-scarlet-1-07-light-in-th.subject: Holmes
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-1-07-light-in-th.statement: Holmes says the cab will take Hope to Scotland Yard.
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-1-07-light-in-th.quote: “We have his cab,” said Sherlock Holmes. “It will serve to take him to Scotland Yard.”

1887-a-study-in-scarlet-1-07-light-in-th.subject: Jefferson Hope
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-1-07-light-in-th.statement: Jefferson Hope murdered Enoch Drebber.
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-1-07-light-in-th.quote: the murderer of Enoch Drebber and of Joseph Stangerson.

1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-01-on-the-grea.subject: Sierra Blanco
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-01-on-the-grea.statement: Sierra Blanco is a mountain overlooking the alkali plain.
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-01-on-the-grea.quote: Looking down from the Sierra Blanco, one sees a pathway traced out across the desert, which winds away and is lost in the extreme distance.

1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-01-on-the-grea.subject: John Ferrier
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-01-on-the-grea.statement: On May 4, 1847, John Ferrier stood on the northern slope of Sierra Blanco.
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-01-on-the-grea.quote: Looking down on this very scene, there stood upon the fourth of May, eighteen hundred and forty-seven, a solitary traveller.

1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-01-on-the-grea.subject: John Ferrier
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-01-on-the-grea.statement: John Ferrier is a solitary traveller.
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-01-on-the-grea.quote: My name is John Ferrier,” the wanderer explained;

1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-01-on-the-grea.subject: John Ferrier
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-01-on-the-grea.value: nearer to forty or to sixty
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-01-on-the-grea.statement: John Ferrier's age is unclear, but he appears to be somewhere between forty and sixty.
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-01-on-the-grea.quote: An observer would have found it difficult to say whether he was nearer to forty or to sixty.

1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-01-on-the-grea.subject: John Ferrier
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-01-on-the-grea.value: dying from hunger and from thirst
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-01-on-the-grea.statement: John Ferrier is dying from hunger and thirst.
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-01-on-the-grea.quote: The man was dying—dying from hunger and from thirst.

1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-01-on-the-grea.subject: Lucy
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-01-on-the-grea.statement: Lucy is about five years old.
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-01-on-the-grea.quote: a pretty little girl of about five years of age

1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-01-on-the-grea.subject: Lucy
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-01-on-the-grea.statement: Lucy's eyes are brown.
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-01-on-the-grea.quote: a small, scared face, with very bright brown eyes

1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-01-on-the-grea.subject: John Ferrier
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-01-on-the-grea.statement: John Ferrier carried Lucy slung over his right shoulder in a grey shawl.
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-01-on-the-grea.quote: a large bundle tied up in a grey shawl, which he had carried slung over his right shoulder.

1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-01-on-the-grea.subject: John Ferrier
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-01-on-the-grea.statement: John Ferrier lowered Lucy's bundle onto the ground, and the impact hurt her.
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-01-on-the-grea.quote: Before sitting down, he had deposited upon the ground his useless rifle, and also a large bundle tied up in a grey shawl, which he had carried slung over his right shoulder.

1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-01-on-the-grea.subject: Lucy
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-01-on-the-grea.statement: Lucy reproached John Ferrier for hurting her.
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-01-on-the-grea.quote: “You’ve hurt me!” said a childish voice reproachfully.

1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-01-on-the-grea.subject: John Ferrier
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-01-on-the-grea.statement: John Ferrier penitently told Lucy he had not meant to hurt her.
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-01-on-the-grea.quote: “Have I though,” the man answered penitently, “I didn’t go for to do it.”

1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-01-on-the-grea.subject: Lucy
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-01-on-the-grea.statement: Lucy asked where her mother was.
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-01-on-the-grea.quote: “Where’s mother?”

1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-01-on-the-grea.subject: John Ferrier
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-01-on-the-grea.statement: John Ferrier told Lucy that her mother was gone and that she would see her before long.
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-01-on-the-grea.quote: “Mother’s gone. I guess you’ll see her before long.”

1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-01-on-the-grea.subject: Lucy
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-01-on-the-grea.statement: Lucy asked whether there was water or food.
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-01-on-the-grea.quote: Say, it’s awful dry, ain’t it? Ain’t there no water, nor nothing to eat?

1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-01-on-the-grea.subject: John Ferrier
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-01-on-the-grea.statement: John Ferrier told Lucy they had no food or water and that she must be patient.
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-01-on-the-grea.quote: “No, there ain’t nothing, dearie. You’ll just need to be patient awhile, and then you’ll be all right.”

1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-01-on-the-grea.subject: John Ferrier
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-01-on-the-grea.statement: John Ferrier explained that their party had expected to find another river but had failed to find it because something was wrong with their compass or map.
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-01-on-the-grea.quote: “Well, we reckoned we’d strike another river soon, d’ye see. But there was somethin’ wrong; compasses, or map, or somethin’, and it didn’t turn up.”

1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-01-on-the-grea.subject: John Ferrier
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-01-on-the-grea.statement: After the water ran out, John Ferrier carried Lucy over his shoulder as they travelled toward possible water.
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-01-on-the-grea.quote: Then I thought there was some chance of water in this direction, so I heaved you over my shoulder and we tramped it together.

1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-01-on-the-grea.subject: John Ferrier
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-01-on-the-grea.statement: John Ferrier asked Lucy to say the prayers she used to say in the wagon, and said he would join in the choruses.
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-01-on-the-grea.quote: You say them out, and I’ll stand by and come in on the choruses.

1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-01-on-the-grea.subject: Lucy
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-01-on-the-grea.statement: Lucy knelt with John Ferrier and prayed with him.
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-01-on-the-grea.quote: Side by side on the narrow shawl knelt the two wanderers, the little prattling child and the reckless, hardened adventurer.

1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-01-on-the-grea.subject: Lucy
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-01-on-the-grea.statement: Lucy fell asleep nestled against John Ferrier's breast.
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-01-on-the-grea.quote: until the child fell asleep, nestling upon the broad breast of her protector.

1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-01-on-the-grea.subject: John Ferrier
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-01-on-the-grea.statement: After watching Lucy sleep, John Ferrier fell asleep beside her.
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-01-on-the-grea.quote: Slowly the eyelids drooped over the tired eyes, and the head sunk lower and lower upon the breast, until the man’s grizzled beard was mixed with the gold tresses of his companion, and both slept the same deep and dreamless slumber.

1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-01-on-the-grea.subject: Mormon caravan
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-01-on-the-grea.statement: A large Mormon caravan arrived at the bluff where John Ferrier and Lucy were sleeping.
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-01-on-the-grea.quote: As the whirl of dust drew nearer to the solitary bluff upon which the two castaways were reposing, the canvas-covered tilts of waggons and the figures of armed horsemen began to show up through the haze, and the apparition revealed itself as being a great caravan upon its journey for the West.

1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-01-on-the-grea.subject: Brigham Young
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-01-on-the-grea.statement: Brigham Young is the Prophet of the Mormon caravan.
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-01-on-the-grea.quote: The hand of God is leading us under the person of our Prophet.

1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-01-on-the-grea.subject: Brother Stangerson
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-01-on-the-grea.statement: Brother Stangerson and the other men at the head of the caravan halted at the base of the bluff and held a short council.
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-01-on-the-grea.quote: On reaching the base of the bluff they halted, and held a short council among themselves.

1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-01-on-the-grea.subject: Mormon scouts
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-01-on-the-grea.statement: A group of young Mormon scouts climbed the slope toward the pink object on the crag.
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-01-on-the-grea.quote: In a moment the young fellows had dismounted, fastened their horses, and were ascending the precipitous slope which led up to the object which had excited their curiosity.

1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-01-on-the-grea.subject: Mormon scouts
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-01-on-the-grea.statement: The scouts found John Ferrier and Lucy asleep beside a boulder on the plateau.
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-01-on-the-grea.quote: On the little plateau which crowned the barren hill there stood a single giant boulder, and against this boulder there lay a tall man, long-bearded and hard-featured, but of an excessive thinness.

1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-01-on-the-grea.subject: John Ferrier
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-01-on-the-grea.statement: The cries of the buzzards woke John Ferrier and Lucy.
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-01-on-the-grea.quote: The cries of the foul birds awoke the two sleepers who stared about them in bewilderment.

1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-01-on-the-grea.subject: John Ferrier
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-01-on-the-grea.statement: John Ferrier mistook the caravan for delirium.
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-01-on-the-grea.quote: “This is what they call delirium, I guess,” he muttered.

1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-01-on-the-grea.subject: Mormon rescuers
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-01-on-the-grea.statement: One of the rescuers lifted Lucy onto his shoulder.
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-01-on-the-grea.quote: One of them seized the little girl, and hoisted her upon his shoulder, while two others supported her gaunt companion, and assisted him towards the waggons.

1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-01-on-the-grea.subject: Mormon rescuers
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-01-on-the-grea.statement: Two rescuers supported John Ferrier and helped him toward the wagons.
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-01-on-the-grea.quote: One of them seized the little girl, and hoisted her upon his shoulder, while two others supported her gaunt companion, and assisted him towards the waggons.

1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-01-on-the-grea.subject: John Ferrier
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-01-on-the-grea.statement: John Ferrier identified himself to the rescuers and said he and the child were the only survivors of a party of twenty-one.
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-01-on-the-grea.quote: “My name is John Ferrier,” the wanderer explained; “me and that little un are all that’s left o’ twenty-one people.”

1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-01-on-the-grea.subject: John Ferrier
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-01-on-the-grea.statement: John Ferrier declared that Lucy was his because he had saved her and that no one would take her from him.
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-01-on-the-grea.quote: “I guess she is now,” the other cried, defiantly; “she’s mine ’cause I saved her. No man will take her from me.”

1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-01-on-the-grea.subject: Lucy
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-01-on-the-grea.statement: Lucy's first name is Lucy.
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-01-on-the-grea.quote: She’s Lucy Ferrier from this day on.

1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-01-on-the-grea.subject: Lucy
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-01-on-the-grea.statement: Lucy's surname is Ferrier.
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-01-on-the-grea.quote: She’s Lucy Ferrier from this day on.

1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-01-on-the-grea.subject: Mormon caravan
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-01-on-the-grea.statement: The Mormon caravan numbers nearly ten thousand people.
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-01-on-the-grea.quote: “Nigh upon ten thousand,” said one of the young men;

1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-01-on-the-grea.subject: Mormon caravan
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-01-on-the-grea.value: Nauvoo, in the State of Illinois
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-01-on-the-grea.statement: The Mormon caravan came from Nauvoo, Illinois.
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-01-on-the-grea.quote: We have come from Nauvoo, in the State of Illinois, where we had founded our temple.

1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-01-on-the-grea.subject: Mormon caravan
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-01-on-the-grea.statement: The Mormon caravan was travelling westward to seek refuge and was commanded to continue on toward Zion.
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-01-on-the-grea.quote: Forward! On, on to Zion!

1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-01-on-the-grea.subject: Mormon leader
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-01-on-the-grea.statement: The Mormon leader offered to take John Ferrier and Lucy with the caravan only if they accepted the Mormon creed.
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-01-on-the-grea.quote: “If we take you with us,” he said, in solemn words, “it can only be as believers in our own creed.”

1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-01-on-the-grea.subject: John Ferrier
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-01-on-the-grea.statement: John Ferrier agreed to travel with the Mormons on any terms.
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-01-on-the-grea.quote: “Guess I’ll come with you on any terms,” said Ferrier,

1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-01-on-the-grea.subject: Mormon leader
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-01-on-the-grea.statement: The Mormon leader assigned John Ferrier and Lucy to Brother Stangerson's care.
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-01-on-the-grea.quote: “Take him, Brother Stangerson,” he said, “give him food and drink, and the child likewise.”

1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-01-on-the-grea.subject: Brother Stangerson
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-01-on-the-grea.statement: Brother Stangerson was instructed to give John Ferrier food and drink.
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-01-on-the-grea.quote: “Take him, Brother Stangerson,” he said, “give him food and drink, and the child likewise.”

1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-01-on-the-grea.subject: Brother Stangerson
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-01-on-the-grea.statement: Brother Stangerson was instructed to give Lucy food and drink.
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-01-on-the-grea.quote: “Take him, Brother Stangerson,” he said, “give him food and drink, and the child likewise.”

1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-01-on-the-grea.subject: Brother Stangerson
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-01-on-the-grea.statement: Brother Stangerson was tasked with teaching John Ferrier the Mormon creed.
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-01-on-the-grea.quote: Let it be your task also to teach him our holy creed.

1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-01-on-the-grea.subject: Brother Stangerson
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-01-on-the-grea.statement: Brother Stangerson led John Ferrier and Lucy to his wagon, where a meal was waiting.
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-01-on-the-grea.quote: The Elder to whose care the two waifs had been committed, led them to his waggon, where a meal was already awaiting them.

1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-01-on-the-grea.subject: John Ferrier
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-01-on-the-grea.statement: Brother Stangerson declared that John Ferrier and Lucy were now of the Mormon religion.
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-01-on-the-grea.quote: In the meantime, remember that now and for ever you are of our religion.

1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-02-the-flower-.subject: Lucy
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-02-the-flower-.statement: Lucy was adopted as John Ferrier's daughter.
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-02-the-flower-.quote: the little girl who had shared his fortunes and had been adopted as his daughter

1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-02-the-flower-.subject: John Ferrier
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-02-the-flower-.statement: John Ferrier is Lucy's adoptive father.
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-02-the-flower-.quote: the little girl who had shared his fortunes and had been adopted as his daughter

1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-02-the-flower-.subject: Lucy
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-02-the-flower-.statement: Lucy grew up in John Ferrier's log-house.
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-02-the-flower-.quote: Lucy Ferrier grew up within the log-house

1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-02-the-flower-.subject: John Ferrier
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-02-the-flower-.value: to set up a female establishment
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-02-the-flower-.statement: John Ferrier persistently refused to set up a female establishment.
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-02-the-flower-.quote: No argument or persuasion could ever induce him to set up a female establishment after the manner of his companions.

1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-02-the-flower-.subject: John Ferrier
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-02-the-flower-.statement: John Ferrier remained strictly celibate.
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-02-the-flower-.quote: Whatever the reason, Ferrier remained strictly celibate.

1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-02-the-flower-.subject: Lucy
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-02-the-flower-.statement: Lucy rode into Salt Lake City on an errand from her father.
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-02-the-flower-.quote: She had a commission from her father in the City, and was dashing in as she had done many a time before

1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-02-the-flower-.subject: Lucy
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-02-the-flower-.statement: Lucy became trapped among a moving drove of cattle.
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-02-the-flower-.quote: she found herself completely imbedded in the moving stream of fierce-eyed, long-horned bullocks.

1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-02-the-flower-.subject: Jefferson Hope
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-02-the-flower-.statement: Jefferson Hope caught Lucy's frightened horse and led her out of the cattle drove.
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-02-the-flower-.quote: At the same moment a sinewy brown hand caught the frightened horse by the curb, and forcing a way through the drove, soon brought her to the outskirts.

1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-02-the-flower-.subject: Lucy
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-02-the-flower-.statement: Lucy invited Jefferson Hope to visit her and her father.
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-02-the-flower-.quote: You must come and see us.

1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-02-the-flower-.subject: Jefferson Hope
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-02-the-flower-.statement: Jefferson Hope asked Lucy to find out whether John Ferrier remembered the Jefferson Hopes of St. Louis.
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-02-the-flower-.quote: When you see him, ask him if he remembers the Jefferson Hopes of St. Louis.

1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-02-the-flower-.subject: Jefferson Hope
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-02-the-flower-.value: a friend of John Ferrier from St. Louis
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-02-the-flower-.statement: Jefferson Hope said his father and John Ferrier had been close in St. Louis.
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-02-the-flower-.quote: If he’s the same Ferrier, my father and he were pretty thick.

1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-02-the-flower-.subject: Jefferson Hope
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-02-the-flower-.statement: Jefferson Hope visited John Ferrier that night and returned many times.
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-02-the-flower-.quote: He called on John Ferrier that night, and many times again, until his face was a familiar one at the farm-house.

1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-02-the-flower-.subject: Jefferson Hope
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-02-the-flower-.statement: Jefferson Hope told John Ferrier and Lucy stories about his experiences and the outside world.
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-02-the-flower-.quote: All this Jefferson Hope was able to tell him, and in a style which interested Lucy as well as her father.

1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-02-the-flower-.subject: Jefferson Hope
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-02-the-flower-.statement: Jefferson Hope fell in love with Lucy.
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-02-the-flower-.quote: The love which had sprung up in his heart was not the sudden, changeable fancy of a boy

1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-02-the-flower-.subject: Jefferson Hope
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-02-the-flower-.statement: Lucy returned Jefferson Hope's affection.
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-02-the-flower-.quote: her young heart was no longer her own.

1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-02-the-flower-.subject: Jefferson Hope
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-02-the-flower-.statement: Jefferson Hope asked Lucy to be ready to go with him when he returned.
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-02-the-flower-.quote: I won’t ask you to come with me now, but will you be ready to come when I am here again?

1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-02-the-flower-.subject: John Ferrier
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-02-the-flower-.value: Lucy and Jefferson Hope marrying if their mines worked successfully
