1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-02-the-flower-.statement: John Ferrier consented to Lucy and Jefferson Hope's marriage on the condition that their mines worked successfully.
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-02-the-flower-.quote: He has given his consent, provided we get these mines working all right.

1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-02-the-flower-.subject: Jefferson Hope
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-02-the-flower-.statement: Jefferson Hope promised to return within two months and claim Lucy.
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-02-the-flower-.quote: A couple of months at the outside. I will come and claim you then, my darling.

1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-02-the-flower-.subject: Jefferson Hope
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-02-the-flower-.statement: Jefferson Hope kissed Lucy before leaving.
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-02-the-flower-.quote: Thank God!” he said, hoarsely, stooping and kissing her.

1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-02-the-flower-.subject: Jefferson Hope
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-02-the-flower-.statement: Jefferson Hope left to join the people waiting for him at the cañon.
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-02-the-flower-.quote: They are waiting for me at the cañon.

1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-02-the-flower-.subject: Lucy
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-02-the-flower-.statement: Lucy watched Jefferson Hope ride away until he disappeared from sight.
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-02-the-flower-.quote: She stood at the gate, gazing after him until he vanished from her sight.

1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-03-john-ferrie.subject: John Ferrier
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-03-john-ferrie.statement: John Ferrier is Lucy’s adoptive father.
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-03-john-ferrie.quote: John Ferrier’s heart was sore within him when he thought of the young man’s return, and of the impending loss of his adopted child.

1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-03-john-ferrie.subject: John Ferrier
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-03-john-ferrie.statement: John Ferrier is Lucy’s adoptive parent.
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-03-john-ferrie.quote: John Ferrier’s heart was sore within him when he thought of the young man’s return, and of the impending loss of his adopted child.

1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-03-john-ferrie.subject: John Ferrier
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-03-john-ferrie.statement: John Ferrier has always been determined not to allow Lucy to marry a Mormon.
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-03-john-ferrie.quote: He had always determined, deep down in his resolute heart, that nothing would ever induce him to allow his daughter to wed a Mormon.

1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-03-john-ferrie.subject: Danite Band
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-03-john-ferrie.statement: The Danite Band is also known as the Avenging Angels.
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-03-john-ferrie.quote: To this day, in the lonely ranches of the West, the name of the Danite Band, or the Avenging Angels, is a sinister and an ill-omened one.

1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-03-john-ferrie.subject: Danite Band
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-03-john-ferrie.value: masked armed men raid camps and murder immigrants
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-03-john-ferrie.statement: The Danite Band is associated with masked armed men and rumours of murdered immigrants and rifled camps.
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-03-john-ferrie.quote: Strange rumours began to be bandied about—rumours of murdered immigrants and rifled camps in regions where Indians had never been seen.

1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-03-john-ferrie.subject: Brigham Young
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-03-john-ferrie.statement: Brigham Young visits John Ferrier at his home.
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-03-john-ferrie.quote: One fine morning, John Ferrier was about to set out to his wheatfields, when he heard the click of the latch, and, looking through the window, saw a stout, sandy-haired, middle-aged man coming up the pathway.

1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-03-john-ferrie.subject: Brigham Young
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-03-john-ferrie.statement: Brigham Young accuses John Ferrier of neglecting his promise to embrace the Mormon faith and conform to its usages.
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-03-john-ferrie.quote: This you promised to do, and this, if common report says truly, you have neglected.

1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-03-john-ferrie.subject: John Ferrier
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-03-john-ferrie.statement: John Ferrier tells Brigham Young that he has not married.
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-03-john-ferrie.quote: “It is true that I have not married,” Ferrier answered.

1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-03-john-ferrie.subject: Brigham Young
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-03-john-ferrie.statement: Brigham Young demands to know where John Ferrier’s wives are and asks him to call them in.
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-03-john-ferrie.quote: “Where are your wives?” asked Young, looking round him. “Call them in, that I may greet them.”

1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-03-john-ferrie.subject: Brigham Young
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-03-john-ferrie.statement: Brigham Young tells John Ferrier that Lucy must marry a man of the true faith rather than a Gentile.
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-03-john-ferrie.quote: This being so, it is impossible that you, who profess the holy creed, should suffer your daughter to violate it.

1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-03-john-ferrie.subject: Mormon faith
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-03-john-ferrie.statement: The code of the Mormon faith says that a maiden of the true faith must marry one of the elect and commits a grievous sin if she marries a Gentile.
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-03-john-ferrie.quote: ‘Let every maiden of the true faith marry one of the elect; for if she wed a Gentile, she commits a grievous sin.’

1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-03-john-ferrie.subject: Sacred Council of Four
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-03-john-ferrie.object: John Ferrier’s faith will be tested over Lucy’s marriage
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-03-john-ferrie.statement: The Sacred Council of Four decides that John Ferrier’s faith will be tested over Lucy’s marriage.
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-03-john-ferrie.quote: “Upon this one point your whole faith shall be tested—so it has been decided in the Sacred Council of Four.”

1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-03-john-ferrie.subject: Brigham Young
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-03-john-ferrie.value: choose between Stangerson’s son and Drebber’s son
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-03-john-ferrie.statement: Brigham Young tells Ferrier that Lucy may choose between Stangerson’s son and Drebber’s son.
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-03-john-ferrie.quote: Stangerson has a son, and Drebber has a son, and either of them would gladly welcome your daughter to their house.

1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-03-john-ferrie.subject: John Ferrier
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-03-john-ferrie.statement: John Ferrier asks Brigham Young to give them time because Lucy is very young.
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-03-john-ferrie.quote: “You will give us time,” he said at last. “My daughter is very young—she is scarce of an age to marry.”

1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-03-john-ferrie.subject: Brigham Young
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-03-john-ferrie.statement: Brigham Young gives Lucy a month to choose and says she must give her answer at the end of it.
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-03-john-ferrie.quote: “She shall have a month to choose,” said Young, rising from his seat. “At the end of that time she shall give her answer.”

1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-03-john-ferrie.subject: Brigham Young
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-03-john-ferrie.statement: Brigham Young threatens John Ferrier for opposing the orders of the Holy Four.
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-03-john-ferrie.quote: “It were better for you, John Ferrier,” he thundered, “that you and she were now lying blanched skeletons upon the Sierra Blanco, than that you should put your weak wills against the orders of the Holy Four!”

1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-03-john-ferrie.subject: Lucy
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-03-john-ferrie.statement: Lucy overhears Brigham Young’s conversation with John Ferrier.
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-03-john-ferrie.quote: “I could not help it,” she said, in answer to his look. “His voice rang through the house.”

1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-03-john-ferrie.subject: Lucy
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-03-john-ferrie.statement: Lucy asks her father what they should do after hearing Brigham Young’s demand.
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-03-john-ferrie.quote: “Oh, father, father, what shall we do?”

1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-03-john-ferrie.subject: John Ferrier
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-03-john-ferrie.statement: John Ferrier reassures Lucy that they will find a way to resolve their predicament.
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-03-john-ferrie.quote: “Don’t you scare yourself,” he answered, drawing her to him, and passing his broad, rough hand caressingly over her chestnut hair. “We’ll fix it up somehow or another.”

1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-03-john-ferrie.subject: John Ferrier
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-03-john-ferrie.statement: John Ferrier plans to send Jefferson Hope a message about their predicament with a party leaving for Nevada the next day.
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-03-john-ferrie.quote: There’s a party starting for Nevada to-morrow, and I’ll manage to send him a message letting him know the hole we are in.

1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-03-john-ferrie.subject: John Ferrier
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-03-john-ferrie.statement: John Ferrier plans for himself and Lucy to leave Utah after the month they have been given.
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-03-john-ferrie.quote: We have a clear month before us; at the end of that, I guess we had best shin out of Utah.

1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-03-john-ferrie.subject: John Ferrier
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-03-john-ferrie.statement: John Ferrier plans to raise as much money as he can from the farm and leave the rest behind.
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-03-john-ferrie.quote: “We will raise as much as we can in money, and let the rest go.”

1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-03-john-ferrie.subject: John Ferrier
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-03-john-ferrie.statement: John Ferrier says Brigham Young might meet a shotgun charge if he comes to the farm.
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-03-john-ferrie.quote: If he comes browsing about this farm, he might chance to run up against a charge of buckshot travelling in the opposite direction.

1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-03-john-ferrie.subject: John Ferrier
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-03-john-ferrie.statement: John Ferrier tells Lucy that there is no danger and that she should not fret.
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-03-john-ferrie.quote: “In the meantime, don’t you fret yourself, my dearie, and don’t get your eyes swelled up, else he’ll be walking into me when he sees you. There’s nothing to be afeared about, and there’s no danger at all.”

1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-03-john-ferrie.subject: John Ferrier
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-03-john-ferrie.statement: John Ferrier carefully cleans and loads the shotgun hanging in his bedroom.
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-03-john-ferrie.quote: he carefully cleaned and loaded the rusty old shotgun which hung upon the wall of his bedroom.

1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-04-a-flight-fo.subject: John Ferrier
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-04-a-flight-fo.statement: John Ferrier went to Salt Lake City the morning after his interview with the Mormon Prophet.
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-04-a-flight-fo.quote: On the morning which followed his interview with the Mormon Prophet, John Ferrier went in to Salt Lake City

1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-04-a-flight-fo.subject: John Ferrier
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-04-a-flight-fo.object: acquaintance bound for the Nevada Mountains
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-04-a-flight-fo.statement: John Ferrier entrusted his message to Jefferson Hope to an acquaintance bound for the Nevada Mountains.
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-04-a-flight-fo.quote: he entrusted him with his message to Jefferson Hope.

1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-04-a-flight-fo.subject: John Ferrier
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-04-a-flight-fo.statement: John Ferrier warned Jefferson Hope of the imminent danger and urged him to return.
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-04-a-flight-fo.quote: In it he told the young man of the imminent danger which threatened them, and how necessary it was that he should return.

1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-04-a-flight-fo.subject: Joseph Stangerson
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-04-a-flight-fo.statement: Joseph Stangerson identifies the other visitor as the son of Elder Drebber.
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-04-a-flight-fo.quote: This here is the son of Elder Drebber, and I’m Joseph Stangerson

1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-04-a-flight-fo.subject: Joseph Stangerson
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-04-a-flight-fo.statement: Joseph Stangerson says that he has four wives.
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-04-a-flight-fo.quote: As I have but four wives

1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-04-a-flight-fo.subject: Drebber
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-04-a-flight-fo.statement: Drebber says that he has seven wives.
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-04-a-flight-fo.quote: Brother Drebber here has seven

1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-04-a-flight-fo.subject: Joseph Stangerson
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-04-a-flight-fo.statement: Joseph Stangerson came to solicit Lucy Ferrier's hand in marriage for himself or Drebber.
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-04-a-flight-fo.quote: We have come,” continued Stangerson, “at the advice of our fathers to solicit the hand of your daughter for whichever of us may seem good to you and to her.

1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-04-a-flight-fo.subject: Drebber
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-04-a-flight-fo.statement: Drebber came to solicit Lucy Ferrier's hand in marriage for himself or Stangerson.
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-04-a-flight-fo.quote: We have come,” continued Stangerson, “at the advice of our fathers to solicit the hand of your daughter for whichever of us may seem good to you and to her.

1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-04-a-flight-fo.subject: John Ferrier
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-04-a-flight-fo.statement: John Ferrier told the two visitors he did not want to see them again until Lucy summoned them.
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-04-a-flight-fo.quote: when my daughter summons you, you can come, but until then I don’t want to see your faces again.

1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-04-a-flight-fo.subject: Joseph Stangerson
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-04-a-flight-fo.statement: Joseph Stangerson threatened that John Ferrier would rue defying the Prophet and Council of Four.
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-04-a-flight-fo.quote: You have defied the Prophet and the Council of Four. You shall rue it to the end of your days.

1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-04-a-flight-fo.subject: Drebber
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-04-a-flight-fo.statement: Drebber threatened that the Lord would arise and smite John Ferrier.
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-04-a-flight-fo.quote: He will arise and smite you!

1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-04-a-flight-fo.subject: Lucy Ferrier
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-04-a-flight-fo.statement: Lucy restrained John Ferrier when he was about to rush upstairs for his gun.
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-04-a-flight-fo.quote: would have rushed upstairs for his gun had not Lucy seized him by the arm and restrained him.

1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-04-a-flight-fo.subject: John Ferrier
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-04-a-flight-fo.statement: John Ferrier said he would sooner see Lucy in her grave than married to either visitor.
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-04-a-flight-fo.quote: I would sooner see you in your grave, my girl, than the wife of either of them.

1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-04-a-flight-fo.subject: Lucy Ferrier
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-04-a-flight-fo.statement: Lucy said she would sooner die than marry either visitor.
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-04-a-flight-fo.quote: “And so should I, father,” she answered, with spirit;

1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-04-a-flight-fo.subject: John Ferrier
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-04-a-flight-fo.value: Twenty-nine days are given for amendment
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-04-a-flight-fo.statement: John Ferrier found a warning granting him twenty-nine days to amend his conduct.
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-04-a-flight-fo.quote: “Twenty-nine days are given you for amendment, and then——”

1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-04-a-flight-fo.subject: John Ferrier
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-04-a-flight-fo.statement: John Ferrier found the number 28 scrawled on the ceiling the next morning.
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-04-a-flight-fo.quote: In the centre of the ceiling was scrawled, with a burned stick apparently, the number 28.

1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-04-a-flight-fo.subject: John Ferrier
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-04-a-flight-fo.statement: John Ferrier stayed up that night with his gun and kept watch.
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-04-a-flight-fo.quote: That night he sat up with his gun and kept watch and ward.

1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-04-a-flight-fo.subject: John Ferrier
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-04-a-flight-fo.statement: John Ferrier found the number 27 painted on the outside of his door the following morning.
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-04-a-flight-fo.quote: and yet in the morning a great 27 had been painted upon the outside of his door.

1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-04-a-flight-fo.subject: John Ferrier
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-04-a-flight-fo.statement: John Ferrier saw the figure 2 on his house wall that morning.
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-04-a-flight-fo.quote: That morning had shown the figure 2 upon the wall of his house

1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-04-a-flight-fo.subject: Jefferson Hope
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-04-a-flight-fo.statement: Jefferson Hope says Lucy is the reason he came to share the danger.
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-04-a-flight-fo.quote: It’s Lucy that brings me here

1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-04-a-flight-fo.subject: Jefferson Hope
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-04-a-flight-fo.statement: Jefferson Hope crawled into John Ferrier's house at night.
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-04-a-flight-fo.quote: Once within the house the man sprang to his feet, closed the door, and revealed to the astonished farmer the fierce face and resolute expression of Jefferson Hope.

1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-04-a-flight-fo.subject: Jefferson Hope
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-04-a-flight-fo.statement: Jefferson Hope ate the cold meat and bread left on the table.
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-04-a-flight-fo.quote: He flung himself upon the cold meat and bread which were still lying upon the table from his host’s supper, and devoured it voraciously.

1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-04-a-flight-fo.subject: Jefferson Hope
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-04-a-flight-fo.statement: Jefferson Hope said he had gone without food for forty-eight hours.
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-04-a-flight-fo.quote: I have had no time for bite or sup for eight-and-forty hours.

1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-04-a-flight-fo.subject: Jefferson Hope
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-04-a-flight-fo.statement: Jefferson Hope planned to take John and Lucy Ferrier through the mountains toward Carson City.
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-04-a-flight-fo.quote: We must push for Carson City through the mountains.

1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-04-a-flight-fo.subject: Jefferson Hope
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-04-a-flight-fo.statement: Jefferson Hope had a mule and two horses waiting in Eagle Ravine.
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-04-a-flight-fo.quote: I have a mule and two horses waiting in the Eagle Ravine.

1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-04-a-flight-fo.subject: John Ferrier
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-04-a-flight-fo.statement: John Ferrier prepared Lucy for the journey while Jefferson Hope packed provisions and water.
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-04-a-flight-fo.quote: While Ferrier was absent, preparing his daughter for the approaching journey

1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-04-a-flight-fo.subject: Jefferson Hope
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-04-a-flight-fo.statement: Jefferson Hope packed the available food and filled a stoneware jar with water.
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-04-a-flight-fo.quote: Jefferson Hope packed all the eatables that he could find into a small parcel, and filled a stoneware jar with water

1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-04-a-flight-fo.subject: Jefferson Hope
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-04-a-flight-fo.statement: Jefferson Hope led John and Lucy Ferrier out through a side window and across the fields.
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-04-a-flight-fo.quote: The front and back entrances are watched, but with caution we may get away through the side window and across the fields.

1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-04-a-flight-fo.subject: Jefferson Hope
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-04-a-flight-fo.statement: Jefferson Hope carried a revolver in the front of his tunic.
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-04-a-flight-fo.quote: the revolver butt which protruded from the front of his tunic.

1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-04-a-flight-fo.subject: Jefferson Hope
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-04-a-flight-fo.statement: Jefferson Hope seized his companions and pulled them down into the shadow when he heard the owl signal.
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-04-a-flight-fo.quote: the young man seized his two companions and dragged them down into the shadow

1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-04-a-flight-fo.subject: sentinel
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-04-a-flight-fo.statement: A sentinel used the mountain owl's hoot as a signal, which a second man answered.
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-04-a-flight-fo.quote: the melancholy hooting of a mountain owl was heard within a few yards of them, which was immediately answered by another hoot at a small distance.

1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-04-a-flight-fo.subject: sentinel
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-04-a-flight-fo.statement: The first man said the meeting would be tomorrow at midnight when the Whip-poor-Will calls three times.
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-04-a-flight-fo.quote: “To-morrow at midnight,” said the first who appeared to be in authority. “When the Whip-poor-Will calls three times.”

1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-04-a-flight-fo.subject: Jefferson Hope
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-04-a-flight-fo.statement: After the two men left, Jefferson Hope helped his companions through the gap and led them across the fields at speed.
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-04-a-flight-fo.quote: The instant that their footsteps had died away in the distance, Jefferson Hope sprang to his feet, and helping his companions through the gap, led the way across the fields at the top of his speed

1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-04-a-flight-fo.subject: Jefferson Hope
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-04-a-flight-fo.statement: Jefferson Hope supported and half-carried Lucy when her strength failed.
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-04-a-flight-fo.quote: supporting and half-carrying the girl when her strength appeared to fail her.

1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-04-a-flight-fo.subject: Jefferson Hope
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-04-a-flight-fo.statement: Jefferson Hope and his companions slipped into a field to avoid recognition when they met someone.
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-04-a-flight-fo.quote: Only once did they meet anyone, and then they managed to slip into a field, and so avoid recognition.

1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-04-a-flight-fo.subject: Jefferson Hope
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-04-a-flight-fo.statement: Jefferson Hope led the fugitives along a rugged footpath toward Eagle Cañon.
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-04-a-flight-fo.quote: the hunter branched away into a rugged and narrow footpath which led to the mountains.

1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-04-a-flight-fo.subject: Jefferson Hope
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-04-a-flight-fo.statement: Jefferson Hope found the animals waiting in a screened corner of Eagle Cañon.
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-04-a-flight-fo.quote: where the faithful animals had been picketed.

1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-04-a-flight-fo.subject: Jefferson Hope
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-04-a-flight-fo.statement: Jefferson Hope led one of the horses while Lucy rode the mule and Ferrier rode another horse.
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-04-a-flight-fo.quote: The girl was placed upon the mule, and old Ferrier upon one of the horses, with his money-bag, while Jefferson Hope led the other along the precipitous and dangerous path.

1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-04-a-flight-fo.subject: sentinel
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-04-a-flight-fo.statement: A sentinel challenged the fugitives from a rock overlooking the track.
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-04-a-flight-fo.quote: his military challenge of “Who goes there?” rang through the silent ravine.

1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-04-a-flight-fo.subject: Jefferson Hope
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-04-a-flight-fo.statement: Jefferson Hope told the sentinel they were travellers for Nevada.
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-04-a-flight-fo.quote: “Travellers for Nevada,” said Jefferson Hope

1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-04-a-flight-fo.subject: John Ferrier
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-04-a-flight-fo.statement: John Ferrier told the sentinel they were travelling with the permission of the Holy Four.
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-04-a-flight-fo.quote: “The Holy Four,” answered Ferrier.

1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-04-a-flight-fo.subject: sentinel
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-04-a-flight-fo.statement: The sentinel gave the challenge phrase “Nine from seven.”
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-04-a-flight-fo.quote: “Nine from seven,” cried the sentinel.

1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-04-a-flight-fo.subject: Jefferson Hope
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-04-a-flight-fo.statement: Jefferson Hope answered the sentinel with “Seven from five.”
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-04-a-flight-fo.quote: “Seven from five,” returned Jefferson Hope promptly

1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-04-a-flight-fo.subject: sentinel
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-04-a-flight-fo.statement: The sentinel allowed the fugitives to pass and wished them the Lord's protection.
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-04-a-flight-fo.quote: “Pass, and the Lord go with you,” said the voice from above.

1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-05-the-avengin.subject: Hope
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-05-the-avengin.statement: Jefferson Hope is a hunter.
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-05-the-avengin.quote: the spruce young hunter of former days

1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-05-the-avengin.subject: Hope
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-05-the-avengin.statement: Hope flees with Lucy and her father through the mountains on horseback.
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-05-the-avengin.quote: All night their course lay through intricate defiles and over irregular and rock-strewn paths.

1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-05-the-avengin.subject: Hope
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-05-the-avengin.statement: Hope halts with Lucy and her father at a torrent so they can water their horses and eat breakfast.
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-05-the-avengin.quote: At a wild torrent which swept out of a ravine they called a halt and watered their horses, while they partook of a hasty breakfast.

1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-05-the-avengin.subject: Hope
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-05-the-avengin.statement: Hope refuses to let Lucy and her father rest longer because he believes their pursuers are close.
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-05-the-avengin.quote: Lucy and her father would fain have rested longer, but Jefferson Hope was inexorable.

1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-05-the-avengin.subject: Hope
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-05-the-avengin.value: Once safe in Carson they may rest for the remainder of their lives.
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-05-the-avengin.statement: Hope says they can rest for the remainder of their lives once they reach Carson safely.
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-05-the-avengin.quote: Once safe in Carson we may rest for the remainder of our lives.

1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-05-the-avengin.subject: Hope
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-05-the-avengin.statement: Hope, Lucy, and her father continue through the mountain defiles for the day and sleep beneath a crag at night.
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-05-the-avengin.quote: During the whole of that day they struggled on through the defiles, and by evening they calculated that they were more than thirty miles from their enemies.

1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-05-the-avengin.subject: Hope
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-05-the-avengin.statement: Hope leaves Lucy and her father by a fire and goes hunting with his rifle.
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-05-the-avengin.quote: Having tethered the horses, and bade Lucy adieu, he threw his gun over his shoulder, and set out in search of whatever chance might throw in his way.

1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-05-the-avengin.subject: Hope
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-05-the-avengin.statement: Hope shoots a big-horn with his rifle.
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-05-the-avengin.quote: Lying on his face, he rested his rifle upon a rock, and took a long and steady aim before drawing the trigger.

1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-05-the-avengin.subject: Hope
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-05-the-avengin.statement: Hope cuts away a haunch and part of the flank from the big-horn and carries them back as food.
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-05-the-avengin.quote: The creature was too unwieldy to lift, so the hunter contented himself with cutting away one haunch and part of the flank.

1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-05-the-avengin.subject: Hope
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-05-the-avengin.statement: After nearly five hours away, Hope returns to the camp and finds Lucy, her father, and the animals gone.
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-05-the-avengin.quote: There was no living creature near the remains of the fire: animals, man, maiden, all were gone.

1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-05-the-avengin.subject: Hope
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-05-the-avengin.statement: Hope uses a burning piece of wood to examine the camp.
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-05-the-avengin.quote: Seizing a half-consumed piece of wood from the smouldering fire, he blew it into a flame, and proceeded with its help to examine the little camp.

1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-05-the-avengin.subject: Hope
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-05-the-avengin.value: A large party of mounted men overtook the fugitives and returned toward Salt Lake City.
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-05-the-avengin.statement: Hope infers from the horse tracks that a large mounted party overtook the fugitives and turned back toward Salt Lake City.
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-05-the-avengin.quote: The ground was all stamped down by the feet of horses, showing that a large party of mounted men had overtaken the fugitives, and the direction of their tracks proved that they had afterwards turned back to Salt Lake City.

1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-05-the-avengin.subject: John Ferrier
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-05-the-avengin.statement: John Ferrier dies on August 4th, 1860.
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-05-the-avengin.quote: JOHN FERRIER, FORMERLY OF SALT LAKE CITY, Died August 4th, 1860.

1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-05-the-avengin.subject: Hope
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-05-the-avengin.statement: Hope finds John Ferrier’s newly dug grave at the camp.
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-05-the-avengin.quote: There was no mistaking it for anything but a newly-dug grave.

1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-05-the-avengin.subject: Hope
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-05-the-avengin.value: Lucy has been taken back to become one of the Elder’s son’s harem.
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-05-the-avengin.statement: Hope concludes that Lucy was carried back by their pursuers to become one of the Elder’s son’s harem.
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-05-the-avengin.quote: Lucy had been carried back by their terrible pursuers to fulfil her original destiny, by becoming one of the harem of the Elder’s son.

1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-05-the-avengin.subject: Hope
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-05-the-avengin.statement: Hope resolves to devote his life to revenge against his enemies.
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-05-the-avengin.quote: If there was nothing else left to him, he could at least devote his life to revenge.

1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-05-the-avengin.subject: Hope
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-05-the-avengin.statement: Hope cooks enough food to last him a few days and packs it.
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-05-the-avengin.quote: With a grim, white face, he retraced his steps to where he had dropped the food, and having stirred up the smouldering fire, he cooked enough to last him for a few days.

1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-05-the-avengin.subject: Hope
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-05-the-avengin.statement: Hope walks back through the mountains on the trail of the men he calls the avenging angels.
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-05-the-avengin.quote: This he made up into a bundle, and, tired as he was, he set himself to walk back through the mountains upon the track of the avenging angels.

1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-05-the-avengin.subject: Hope
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-05-the-avengin.statement: After five days of walking, Hope reaches Eagle Cañon on the sixth day.
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-05-the-avengin.quote: On the sixth day, he reached the Eagle Cañon, from which they had commenced their ill-fated flight.

1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-05-the-avengin.subject: Hope
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-05-the-avengin.statement: Hope meets Cowper near Eagle Cañon and asks about Lucy’s fate.
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-05-the-avengin.quote: As he approached, he recognized him as a Mormon named Cowper, to whom he had rendered services at different times.

1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-05-the-avengin.subject: Cowper
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-05-the-avengin.value: There is a warrant against Hope from the Holy Four for helping the Ferriers escape.
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-05-the-avengin.statement: Cowper tells Hope that the Holy Four have issued a warrant against him for assisting the Ferriers’ escape.
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-05-the-avengin.quote: There is a warrant against you from the Holy Four for assisting the Ferriers away.

1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-05-the-avengin.subject: Hope
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-05-the-avengin.statement: Hope asks Cowper what has become of Lucy Ferrier.
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-05-the-avengin.quote: “What has become of Lucy Ferrier?”

1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-05-the-avengin.subject: Cowper
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-05-the-avengin.statement: Cowper tells Hope that Lucy married young Drebber the previous day.
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-05-the-avengin.quote: “She was married yesterday to young Drebber.”

1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-05-the-avengin.subject: Cowper
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-05-the-avengin.statement: Cowper says Stangerson shot Lucy’s father, John Ferrier.
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-05-the-avengin.quote: Stangerson had shot her father, which seemed to give him the best claim

1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-05-the-avengin.subject: Cowper
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-05-the-avengin.value: The Prophet gave Lucy to Drebber because Drebber’s party was stronger in council.
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-05-the-avengin.statement: Cowper says the Prophet awarded Lucy to Drebber after Drebber’s party prevailed in council.
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-05-the-avengin.quote: Drebber’s party was the stronger, so the Prophet gave her over to him.

1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-05-the-avengin.subject: Hope
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-05-the-avengin.statement: Hope leaves Cowper and goes into the mountains.
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-05-the-avengin.quote: “Yes, I am off,” said Jefferson Hope, who had risen from his seat.

1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-05-the-avengin.subject: Lucy
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-05-the-avengin.value: within a month of her marriage
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-05-the-avengin.statement: Lucy dies within a month of her marriage to Drebber.
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-05-the-avengin.quote: poor Lucy never held up her head again, but pined away and died within a month.

1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-05-the-avengin.subject: Drebber
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-05-the-avengin.statement: Drebber marries Lucy principally to obtain John Ferrier’s property.
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-05-the-avengin.quote: Her sottish husband, who had married her principally for the sake of John Ferrier’s property, did not affect any great grief at her bereavement;

1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-05-the-avengin.subject: Hope
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-05-the-avengin.statement: Hope removes Lucy’s wedding ring from her finger before her burial.
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-05-the-avengin.quote: Stooping over her, he pressed his lips reverently to her cold forehead, and then, snatching up her hand, he took the wedding-ring from her finger.

1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-05-the-avengin.subject: Hope
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-05-the-avengin.value: Lucy shall not be buried wearing the wedding ring.
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-05-the-avengin.statement: Hope says Lucy shall not be buried wearing the wedding ring.
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-05-the-avengin.quote: “She shall not be buried in that,” he cried with a fierce snarl,

1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-05-the-avengin.subject: Drebber
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-05-the-avengin.statement: Drebber is married to Lucy before her death.
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-05-the-avengin.quote: Her sottish husband, who had married her principally for the sake of John Ferrier’s property,

1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-05-the-avengin.subject: Hope
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-05-the-avengin.statement: Hope fires a bullet through Stangerson’s window, and it strikes the wall close to him.
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-05-the-avengin.quote: Once a bullet whistled through Stangerson’s window and flattened itself upon the wall within a foot of him.

1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-05-the-avengin.subject: Hope
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-05-the-avengin.statement: Hope causes a boulder to crash down on Drebber, who narrowly avoids death.
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-05-the-avengin.quote: On another occasion, as Drebber passed under a cliff a great boulder crashed down on him, and he only escaped a terrible death by throwing himself upon his face.

1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-05-the-avengin.subject: Drebber
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-05-the-avengin.statement: Drebber and Stangerson lead repeated expeditions into the mountains to capture or kill Hope.
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-05-the-avengin.quote: The two young Mormons were not long in discovering the reason of these attempts upon their lives, and led repeated expeditions into the mountains in the hope of capturing or killing their enemy, but always without success.

1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-05-the-avengin.subject: Drebber
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-05-the-avengin.value: He and Stangerson avoid going out alone or after nightfall and have their houses guarded.
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-05-the-avengin.statement: Drebber and Stangerson avoid going out alone or after dark and arrange for their houses to be guarded.
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-05-the-avengin.quote: Then they adopted the precaution of never going out alone or after nightfall, and of having their houses guarded.

1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-05-the-avengin.subject: Hope
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-05-the-avengin.statement: Hope returns to the Nevada mines to recover his health and earn money for his pursuit.
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-05-the-avengin.quote: He felt that that was to play his enemy’s game, so he reluctantly returned to the old Nevada mines, there to recruit his health and to amass money enough to allow him to pursue his object without privation.

1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-05-the-avengin.subject: Hope
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-05-the-avengin.statement: Hope remains at the mines for nearly five years, although he intended to be away for at most one year.
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-05-the-avengin.quote: His intention had been to be absent a year at the most, but a combination of unforeseen circumstances prevented his leaving the mines for nearly five.

1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-05-the-avengin.subject: Hope
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-05-the-avengin.statement: After nearly five years, Hope returns to Salt Lake City in disguise and under an assumed name.
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-05-the-avengin.quote: Disguised, and under an assumed name, he returned to Salt Lake City, careless what became of his own life, as long as he obtained what he knew to be justice.

1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-05-the-avengin.subject: Drebber
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-05-the-avengin.statement: Drebber and Stangerson leave Utah after a schism among the Chosen People.
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-05-the-avengin.quote: Among these had been Drebber and Stangerson; and no one knew whither they had gone.

1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-05-the-avengin.subject: Drebber
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-05-the-avengin.statement: Drebber reportedly converts a large part of his property into money before leaving.
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-05-the-avengin.quote: Rumour reported that Drebber had managed to convert a large part of his property into money, and that he had departed a wealthy man, while his companion, Stangerson, was comparatively poor.

1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-05-the-avengin.subject: Hope
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-05-the-avengin.statement: Hope travels from town to town across the United States in search of Drebber and Stangerson.
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-05-the-avengin.quote: With the small competence he possessed, eked out by such employment as he could pick up, he travelled from town to town through the United States in quest of his enemies.

1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-05-the-avengin.subject: Hope
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-05-the-avengin.statement: Hope recognizes Drebber in a window in Cleveland, Ohio.
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-05-the-avengin.quote: It was but a glance of a face in a window, but that one glance told him that Cleveland in Ohio possessed the men whom he was in pursuit of.

1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-05-the-avengin.subject: Stangerson
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-05-the-avengin.statement: Stangerson has become Drebber’s private secretary.
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-05-the-avengin.quote: Stangerson, who had become his private secretary,

1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-05-the-avengin.subject: Drebber
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-05-the-avengin.statement: Drebber reports to a justice of the peace that he and Stangerson face danger from an old rival.
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-05-the-avengin.quote: He hurried before a justice of the peace, accompanied by Stangerson, who had become his private secretary, and represented to him that they were in danger of their lives from the jealousy and hatred of an old rival.

1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-05-the-avengin.subject: Hope
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-05-the-avengin.statement: Hope is taken into custody that evening and detained for weeks because he cannot find sureties.
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-05-the-avengin.quote: That evening Jefferson Hope was taken into custody, and not being able to find sureties, was detained for some weeks.

1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-05-the-avengin.subject: Drebber
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-05-the-avengin.statement: Drebber and Stangerson leave Cleveland for Europe while Hope is detained.
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-05-the-avengin.quote: When at last he was liberated, it was only to find that Drebber’s house was deserted, and that he and his secretary had departed for Europe.

1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-05-the-avengin.subject: Hope
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-05-the-avengin.statement: Hope follows Drebber and Stangerson across Europe, working menial jobs along the way.
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-05-the-avengin.quote: At last, having collected enough to keep life in him, he departed for Europe, and tracked his enemies from city to city, working his way in any menial capacity, but never overtaking the fugitives.

1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-05-the-avengin.subject: Drebber
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-05-the-avengin.statement: Drebber and Stangerson travel from St. Petersburg to Paris, then Copenhagen, and finally London.
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-05-the-avengin.quote: When he reached St. Petersburg they had departed for Paris; and when he followed them there he learned that they had just set off for Copenhagen.

1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-06-a-continuat.subject: Jefferson Hope
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-06-a-continuat.statement: Jefferson Hope has an aortic aneurism.
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-06-a-continuat.quote: “Why,” I cried, “you have an aortic aneurism!”

1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-06-a-continuat.subject: Jefferson Hope
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-06-a-continuat.value: his aortic aneurism is bound to burst before many days pass
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-06-a-continuat.statement: Jefferson Hope says his aortic aneurism is bound to burst before many days pass.
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-06-a-continuat.quote: he told me that it is bound to burst before many days passed.

1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-06-a-continuat.subject: Jefferson Hope
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-06-a-continuat.statement: Jefferson Hope tells the Inspector and detectives his account of the murders.
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-06-a-continuat.quote: “I want to tell you gentlemen all about it.”

1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-06-a-continuat.subject: Jefferson Hope
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-06-a-continuat.value: to be judge, jury, and executioner
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-06-a-continuat.statement: Jefferson Hope decides to punish Drebber and Stangerson himself because he believes they caused the deaths of a father and daughter.
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-06-a-continuat.quote: I knew of their guilt though, and I determined that I should be judge, jury, and executioner all rolled into one.

1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-06-a-continuat.subject: Jefferson Hope
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-06-a-continuat.statement: Jefferson Hope was to marry Lucy Ferrier twenty years earlier.
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-06-a-continuat.quote: That girl that I spoke of was to have married me twenty years ago.

1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-06-a-continuat.subject: Jefferson Hope
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-06-a-continuat.statement: Jefferson Hope takes Lucy Ferrier's marriage ring from her dead finger.
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-06-a-continuat.quote: I took the marriage ring from her dead finger,

1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-06-a-continuat.subject: Jefferson Hope
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-06-a-continuat.value: to make Drebber see Lucy's ring as he dies
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-06-a-continuat.statement: Jefferson Hope vows that Drebber will see Lucy's ring as he dies.
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-06-a-continuat.quote: I vowed that his dying eyes should rest upon that very ring,

1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-06-a-continuat.subject: Jefferson Hope
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-06-a-continuat.statement: Jefferson Hope follows Drebber and his accomplice across two continents.
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-06-a-continuat.quote: I have carried it about with me, and have followed him and his accomplice over two continents until I caught them.

1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-06-a-continuat.subject: Jefferson Hope
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-06-a-continuat.statement: Jefferson Hope gets work as a cabdriver in London.
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-06-a-continuat.quote: Driving and riding are as natural to me as walking, so I applied at a cabowner’s office, and soon got employment.

1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-06-a-continuat.subject: Jefferson Hope
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-06-a-continuat.statement: Jefferson Hope discovers that Drebber and Stangerson are living at a boarding-house in Camberwell.
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-06-a-continuat.quote: They were at a boarding-house at Camberwell, over on the other side of the river.

1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-06-a-continuat.subject: Jefferson Hope
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-06-a-continuat.statement: Jefferson Hope follows Drebber and Stangerson around London for two weeks.
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-06-a-continuat.quote: During two weeks I drove behind them every day, and never once saw them separate.

1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-06-a-continuat.subject: Enoch Drebber
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-06-a-continuat.statement: Drebber leaves Torquay Terrace with Stangerson after luggage is brought out.
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-06-a-continuat.quote: Presently some luggage was brought out, and after a time Drebber and Stangerson followed it, and drove off.

1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-06-a-continuat.subject: Enoch Drebber
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-06-a-continuat.statement: Drebber leaves Euston Station alone while Stangerson waits for him at Halliday’s Private Hotel.
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-06-a-continuat.quote: Drebber answered that the matter was a delicate one, and that he must go alone.

1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-06-a-continuat.subject: Jefferson Hope
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-06-a-continuat.statement: Jefferson Hope makes a duplicate of a key to a house on Brixton Road.
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-06-a-continuat.quote: I had taken a moulding of it, and had a duplicate constructed.

1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-06-a-continuat.subject: Enoch Drebber
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-06-a-continuat.statement: Drebber becomes drunk after spending nearly half an hour in a liquor shop.
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-06-a-continuat.quote: When he came out he staggered in his walk, and was evidently pretty well on.

1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-06-a-continuat.subject: Enoch Drebber
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-06-a-continuat.statement: Drebber enters Jefferson Hope’s cab after a young man throws him out of a house.
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-06-a-continuat.quote: He ran as far as the corner, and then, seeing my cab, he hailed me and jumped in.

1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-06-a-continuat.subject: Jefferson Hope
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-06-a-continuat.statement: Jefferson Hope drives Drebber to the house on Brixton Road.
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-06-a-continuat.quote: I drove along slowly, weighing in my own mind what it was best to do.

1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-06-a-continuat.subject: Jefferson Hope
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-06-a-continuat.value: a choice between a poisoned pill and a harmless pill
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-06-a-continuat.statement: Jefferson Hope makes Drebber choose and eat one of two pills, one poisonous and one harmless.
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-06-a-continuat.quote: ‘Choose and eat. There is death in one and life in the other.

1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-06-a-continuat.subject: Jefferson Hope
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-06-a-continuat.statement: Jefferson Hope kills Drebber with a poisoned pill.
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-06-a-continuat.quote: A spasm of pain contorted his features; he threw his hands out in front of him, staggered, and then, with a hoarse cry, fell heavily upon the floor.

1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-06-a-continuat.subject: Enoch Drebber
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-06-a-continuat.statement: Enoch Drebber is dead.
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-06-a-continuat.quote: There was no movement. He was dead!

1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-06-a-continuat.subject: Jefferson Hope
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-06-a-continuat.statement: Jefferson Hope writes “RACHE” on the wall in his own blood.
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-06-a-continuat.quote: I dipped my finger in my own blood and printed it on a convenient place on the wall.

1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-06-a-continuat.subject: Jefferson Hope
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-06-a-continuat.statement: Jefferson Hope returns to the house to look for Lucy’s ring after discovering it is missing.
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-06-a-continuat.quote: Thinking that I might have dropped it when I stooped over Drebber’s body, I drove back,

1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-06-a-continuat.subject: Jefferson Hope
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-06-a-continuat.statement: Jefferson Hope pretends to be hopelessly drunk to disarm a police-officer’s suspicions.
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-06-a-continuat.quote: and only managed to disarm his suspicions by pretending to be hopelessly drunk.

1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-06-a-continuat.subject: Jefferson Hope
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-06-a-continuat.statement: Jefferson Hope waits outside Halliday’s Private Hotel for Stangerson, who does not come out.
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-06-a-continuat.quote: I knew that he was staying at Halliday’s Private Hotel, and I hung about all day, but he never came out.

1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-06-a-continuat.subject: Jefferson Hope
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-06-a-continuat.statement: Jefferson Hope uses ladders to enter Stangerson’s bedroom.
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-06-a-continuat.quote: early next morning I took advantage of some ladders which were lying in the lane behind the hotel, and so made my way into his room in the grey of the dawn.

1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-06-a-continuat.subject: Jefferson Hope
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-06-a-continuat.statement: Jefferson Hope gives Stangerson the same choice of poisoned pills he gave Drebber.
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-06-a-continuat.quote: I described Drebber’s death to him, and I gave him the same choice of the poisoned pills.

1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-06-a-continuat.subject: Stangerson
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-06-a-continuat.statement: Stangerson springs from his bed and attacks Jefferson Hope.
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-06-a-continuat.quote: Instead of grasping at the chance of safety which that offered him, he sprang from his bed and flew at my throat.

1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-06-a-continuat.subject: Jefferson Hope
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-06-a-continuat.statement: Jefferson Hope stabs Stangerson in the heart in self-defence.
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-06-a-continuat.quote: In self-defence I stabbed him to the heart.

1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-06-a-continuat.subject: Stangerson
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-06-a-continuat.statement: Stangerson is dead after Jefferson Hope stabs him.
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-06-a-continuat.quote: In self-defence I stabbed him to the heart.

1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-06-a-continuat.subject: Jefferson Hope
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-06-a-continuat.statement: After killing Stangerson, Jefferson Hope continues working as a cabdriver for a day or so.
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-06-a-continuat.quote: I went on cabbing it for a day or so, intending to keep at it until I could save enough to take me back to America.

1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-06-a-continuat.subject: Jefferson Hope
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-06-a-continuat.statement: Jefferson Hope goes to 221B Baker Street after a boy says a gentleman wants his cab.
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-06-a-continuat.quote: I went round, suspecting no harm,

1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-06-a-continuat.subject: Sherlock Holmes
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-06-a-continuat.statement: Sherlock Holmes arrests Jefferson Hope at 221B Baker Street.
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-06-a-continuat.quote: and the next thing I knew, this young man here had the bracelets on my wrists,

1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-06-a-continuat.subject: Jefferson Hope
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-06-a-continuat.statement: Jefferson Hope refuses to reveal his accomplice’s identity.
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-06-a-continuat.quote: I can tell my own secrets, but I don’t get other people into trouble.

1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-06-a-continuat.subject: Jefferson Hope
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-06-a-continuat.statement: Jefferson Hope is taken to the police-station after his arrest.
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-06-a-continuat.quote: We were ushered into a small chamber where a police Inspector noted down our prisoner’s name

1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-06-a-continuat.subject: Jefferson Hope
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-06-a-continuat.value: he has a good deal to say about the case
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-06-a-continuat.statement: Jefferson Hope tells the Inspector that he wants to give his account.
1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-06-a-continuat.quote: “I’ve got a good deal to say,” our prisoner said slowly.

1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-06-a-continuat.subject: Inspector

1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-07-the-conclus.subject: Jefferson Hope

1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-07-the-conclus.quote: On the very night after his capture the aneurism burst, and he was found in the morning stretched upon the floor of the cell, with a placid smile upon his face, as though he had been able in his dying moments to look back upon a useful life, and on work well done.

1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-07-the-conclus.subject: Jefferson Hope

1887-a-study-in-scarlet-2-07-the-conclus.quote: The answer was conclusive. It told me that Drebber had already applied for the protection of the law against an old rival in love, named Jefferson Hope, and that this same Hope was at present in Europe.

1890-the-sign-of-the-four-02-the-stateme.quote: my father, who was senior captain of his regiment

1890-the-sign-of-the-four-02-the-stateme.subject: Captain Morstan
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-02-the-stateme.statement: Captain Morstan was staying at the Langham Hotel when he disappeared.
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-02-the-stateme.quote: Captain Morstan was staying there

1890-the-sign-of-the-four-02-the-stateme.subject: Captain Morstan
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-02-the-stateme.statement: Captain Morstan disappeared on 3 December 1878.
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-02-the-stateme.quote: He disappeared upon the 3rd of December, 1878

1890-the-sign-of-the-four-02-the-stateme.subject: Captain Morstan
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-02-the-stateme.statement: Captain Morstan’s luggage remained at the Langham Hotel after his disappearance.
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-02-the-stateme.quote: Remained at the hotel.

1890-the-sign-of-the-four-02-the-stateme.subject: Captain Morstan
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-02-the-stateme.statement: Captain Morstan served in the 34th Bombay Infantry.
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-02-the-stateme.quote: of his own regiment, the 34th Bombay Infantry.

1890-the-sign-of-the-four-02-the-stateme.subject: Captain Morstan
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-02-the-stateme.statement: Captain Morstan had served in charge of the convict guard in the Andaman Islands.
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-02-the-stateme.quote: He had been one of the officers in charge of the convict-guard there.

1890-the-sign-of-the-four-02-the-stateme.subject: Mary
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-02-the-stateme.statement: After Captain Morstan disappeared, Mary and others advertised in newspapers for information about him.
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-02-the-stateme.quote: next morning we advertised in all the papers.

1890-the-sign-of-the-four-02-the-stateme.subject: Mary
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-02-the-stateme.statement: Mary has heard no word from her father since his disappearance.
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-02-the-stateme.quote: from that day to this no word has ever been heard of my unfortunate father.

1890-the-sign-of-the-four-02-the-stateme.subject: Major Sholto
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-02-the-stateme.object: retired officer of the 34th Bombay Infantry
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-02-the-stateme.statement: Major Sholto was a retired officer of the 34th Bombay Infantry.
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-02-the-stateme.quote: The major had retired some little time before

1890-the-sign-of-the-four-02-the-stateme.subject: Major Sholto
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-02-the-stateme.statement: Major Sholto lived at Upper Norwood.
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-02-the-stateme.quote: lived at Upper Norwood.

1890-the-sign-of-the-four-02-the-stateme.subject: Captain Morstan
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-02-the-stateme.statement: Captain Morstan and Major Sholto were brother officers in the same regiment.
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-02-the-stateme.quote: Only one that we know of,—Major Sholto, of his own regiment

1890-the-sign-of-the-four-02-the-stateme.subject: Mary
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-02-the-stateme.statement: Mary saw an advertisement in the Times asking for her address and inviting her to come forward to her advantage.
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-02-the-stateme.quote: an advertisement appeared in the _Times_ asking for the address of Miss Mary Morstan and stating that it would be to her advantage to come forward.

1890-the-sign-of-the-four-02-the-stateme.subject: Mary
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-02-the-stateme.statement: On Mrs. Cecil Forrester’s advice, Mary published her address in the advertisement column.
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-02-the-stateme.quote: By her advice I published my address in the advertisement column.

1890-the-sign-of-the-four-02-the-stateme.subject: Mary
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-02-the-stateme.statement: Mary received a large, lustrous pearl in an unmarked box through the post.
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-02-the-stateme.quote: there arrived through the post a small card-board box addressed to me, which I found to contain a very large and lustrous pearl.

1890-the-sign-of-the-four-02-the-stateme.subject: Mary
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-02-the-stateme.statement: Mary has received a similar pearl in a box every year on the same date since the first one arrived.
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-02-the-stateme.quote: Since then every year upon the same date there has always appeared a similar box, containing a similar pearl, without any clue as to the sender.

1890-the-sign-of-the-four-02-the-stateme.subject: Mary
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-02-the-stateme.statement: Mary receives a letter inviting her to meet an unknown friend outside the Lyceum Theatre at seven that evening.
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-02-the-stateme.quote: This morning I received this letter

1890-the-sign-of-the-four-02-the-stateme.subject: Mary
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-02-the-stateme.statement: Mary intends to meet the unknown friend with Holmes and Watson.
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-02-the-stateme.quote: That is exactly what I want to ask you.

1890-the-sign-of-the-four-02-the-stateme.subject: Mary
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-02-the-stateme.statement: Mary brings her pearl-box to the meeting with Holmes and Watson and shows them the pearls.
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-02-the-stateme.quote: She opened a flat box as she spoke, and showed me six of the finest pearls that I had ever seen.

1890-the-sign-of-the-four-02-the-stateme.subject: Sherlock Holmes
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-02-the-stateme.statement: Sherlock Holmes works as a consulting detective.
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-02-the-stateme.quote: State your case

1890-the-sign-of-the-four-02-the-stateme.subject: Sherlock Holmes
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-02-the-stateme.statement: Holmes agrees to go with Mary to meet her correspondent.
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-02-the-stateme.quote: Then we shall most certainly go.

1890-the-sign-of-the-four-02-the-stateme.subject: Sherlock Holmes
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-02-the-stateme.statement: Holmes asks Watson to accompany him and Mary.
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-02-the-stateme.quote: He and I have worked together before.

1890-the-sign-of-the-four-02-the-stateme.subject: Sherlock Holmes
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-02-the-stateme.statement: Holmes asks to keep Mary’s papers so he can examine them.
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-02-the-stateme.quote: Pray allow me to keep the papers.

1890-the-sign-of-the-four-02-the-stateme.subject: Sherlock Holmes
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-02-the-stateme.statement: Holmes concludes that the letter and pearl-box addresses were written by the same person.
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-02-the-stateme.quote: They are undoubtedly by the same person.

1890-the-sign-of-the-four-02-the-stateme.subject: Sherlock Holmes
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-02-the-stateme.statement: Holmes says he never makes exceptions to his rule of avoiding judgment biased by personal qualities.
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-02-the-stateme.quote: I never make exceptions.

1890-the-sign-of-the-four-02-the-stateme.subject: Dr. Watson
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-02-the-stateme.statement: Watson is an army surgeon.
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-02-the-stateme.quote: What was I, an army surgeon with a weak leg and a weaker banking-account

1890-the-sign-of-the-four-02-the-stateme.subject: Dr. Watson
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-02-the-stateme.statement: Watson has a weakness in his leg.
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-02-the-stateme.quote: an army surgeon with a weak leg

1890-the-sign-of-the-four-02-the-stateme.subject: Dr. Watson
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-02-the-stateme.statement: Watson says he would be proud and happy to help Mary.
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-02-the-stateme.quote: I should be proud and happy, said I, fervently, if I can be of any service.

1890-the-sign-of-the-four-02-the-stateme.subject: Sherlock Holmes
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-02-the-stateme.statement: Holmes leaves to make some references and says he will return in an hour.
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-02-the-stateme.quote: I am going out now. I have some few references to make.

1890-the-sign-of-the-four-02-the-stateme.subject: Mary
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-02-the-stateme.statement: Mary is blonde.
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-02-the-stateme.quote: She was a blonde young lady

1890-the-sign-of-the-four-02-the-stateme.subject: Mary
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-02-the-stateme.statement: Mary has blue eyes.
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-02-the-stateme.quote: her large blue eyes

1890-the-sign-of-the-four-03-in-quest-of.subject: Major Sholto
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-03-in-quest-of.statement: Major Sholto died on the 28th of April, 1882.
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-03-in-quest-of.quote: Major Sholto, of Upper Norwood, late of the 34th Bombay Infantry, died upon the 28th of April, 1882.

1890-the-sign-of-the-four-03-in-quest-of.subject: Captain Morstan
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-03-in-quest-of.statement: Captain Morstan disappeared.
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-03-in-quest-of.quote: Captain Morstan disappears.

1890-the-sign-of-the-four-03-in-quest-of.subject: Captain Morstan
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-03-in-quest-of.statement: Captain Morstan and Major Sholto were particular friends.
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-03-in-quest-of.quote: Major Sholto was a very particular friend of papa’s,

1890-the-sign-of-the-four-03-in-quest-of.subject: Miss Morstan
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-03-in-quest-of.value: a valuable present, repeated from year to year
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-03-in-quest-of.statement: Miss Morstan received a valuable present within a week of Major Sholto’s death, and it was repeated from year to year.
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-03-in-quest-of.quote: Within a week of his death Captain Morstan’s daughter receives a valuable present, which is repeated from year to year,

1890-the-sign-of-the-four-03-in-quest-of.subject: Miss Morstan
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-03-in-quest-of.statement: Miss Morstan is Captain Morstan’s daughter.
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-03-in-quest-of.quote: Captain Morstan’s daughter receives a valuable present,

1890-the-sign-of-the-four-03-in-quest-of.subject: Captain Morstan
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-03-in-quest-of.statement: Captain Morstan and Major Sholto were in command of the troops at the Andaman Islands.
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-03-in-quest-of.quote: He and papa were in command of the troops at the Andaman Islands,

1890-the-sign-of-the-four-03-in-quest-of.subject: Miss Morstan
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-03-in-quest-of.statement: Miss Morstan brought a curious paper found in her father’s desk.
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-03-in-quest-of.quote: a curious paper was found in papa’s desk which no one could understand.

1890-the-sign-of-the-four-03-in-quest-of.subject: paper
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-03-in-quest-of.value: a plan of part of a large building
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-03-in-quest-of.statement: The paper’s diagram appears to depict part of a large building.
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-03-in-quest-of.quote: The diagram upon it appears to be a plan of part of a large building with numerous halls, corridors, and passages.

1890-the-sign-of-the-four-03-in-quest-of.subject: paper
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-03-in-quest-of.value: Jonathan Small, Mahomet Singh, Abdullah Khan, Dost Akbar
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-03-in-quest-of.statement: The paper bears the names Jonathan Small, Mahomet Singh, Abdullah Khan, and Dost Akbar beside the sign of the four.
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-03-in-quest-of.quote: Beside it is written, in very rough and coarse characters, ‘The sign of the four,—Jonathan Small, Mahomet Singh, Abdullah Khan, Dost Akbar.’

1890-the-sign-of-the-four-03-in-quest-of.subject: Holmes
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-03-in-quest-of.statement: Holmes asked Miss Morstan to preserve the paper carefully.
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-03-in-quest-of.quote: Preserve it carefully, then, Miss Morstan, for it may prove to be of use to us.

1890-the-sign-of-the-four-03-in-quest-of.subject: Holmes
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-03-in-quest-of.statement: Holmes took his revolver from his drawer and put it in his pocket before the expedition.
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-03-in-quest-of.quote: Holmes took his revolver from his drawer and slipped it into his pocket.

1890-the-sign-of-the-four-03-in-quest-of.subject: Miss Morstan
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-03-in-quest-of.statement: Miss Morstan gave her word that neither companion was a police officer.
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-03-in-quest-of.quote: “I give you my word on that,” she answered.

1890-the-sign-of-the-four-03-in-quest-of.subject: Holmes
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-03-in-quest-of.statement: Holmes identified that the cab was making for the Surrey side.
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-03-in-quest-of.quote: We are making for the Surrey side, apparently.

1890-the-sign-of-the-four-03-in-quest-of.subject: Holmes
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-03-in-quest-of.statement: Holmes named Rochester Row as the cab passed through it.
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-03-in-quest-of.quote: “Rochester Row,” said he.

1890-the-sign-of-the-four-03-in-quest-of.subject: Holmes
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-03-in-quest-of.statement: Holmes named Vincent Square as the cab passed through it.
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-03-in-quest-of.quote: Now Vincent Square.

1890-the-sign-of-the-four-03-in-quest-of.subject: Holmes
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-03-in-quest-of.statement: Holmes named Vauxhall Bridge Road as the cab reached it.
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-03-in-quest-of.quote: Now we come out on the Vauxhall Bridge Road.

1890-the-sign-of-the-four-03-in-quest-of.subject: Holmes
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-03-in-quest-of.statement: Holmes named Wordsworth Road as the cab passed through it.
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-03-in-quest-of.quote: “Wordsworth Road,” said my companion.

1890-the-sign-of-the-four-03-in-quest-of.subject: Holmes
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-03-in-quest-of.statement: Holmes named Priory Road as the cab passed through it.
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-03-in-quest-of.quote: Priory Road.

1890-the-sign-of-the-four-03-in-quest-of.subject: Holmes
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-03-in-quest-of.statement: Holmes named Lark Hall Lane as the cab passed through it.
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-03-in-quest-of.quote: Lark Hall Lane.

1890-the-sign-of-the-four-03-in-quest-of.subject: Holmes
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-03-in-quest-of.statement: Holmes named Stockwell Place as the cab passed through it.
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-03-in-quest-of.quote: Stockwell Place.

1890-the-sign-of-the-four-03-in-quest-of.subject: Holmes
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-03-in-quest-of.statement: Holmes named Robert Street as the cab passed through it.
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-03-in-quest-of.quote: Robert Street.

1890-the-sign-of-the-four-03-in-quest-of.subject: Holmes
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-03-in-quest-of.statement: Holmes named Cold Harbor Lane as the cab passed through it.
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-03-in-quest-of.quote: Cold Harbor Lane.

1890-the-sign-of-the-four-03-in-quest-of.subject: Holmes
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-03-in-quest-of.object: third house in a new terrace
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-03-in-quest-of.statement: Holmes and his companions arrived at the third house in a new terrace.
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-03-in-quest-of.quote: At last the cab drew up at the third house in a new terrace.

1890-the-sign-of-the-four-03-in-quest-of.subject: Hindoo servant
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-03-in-quest-of.statement: The Hindoo servant opened the door and said that the Sahib awaited them.
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-03-in-quest-of.quote: “The Sahib awaits you,” said he,

1890-the-sign-of-the-four-03-in-quest-of.subject: Hindoo servant
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-03-in-quest-of.statement: The Hindoo servant was told to show the visitors straight in.
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-03-in-quest-of.quote: “Show them in to me, khitmutgar,” it cried.

1890-the-sign-of-the-four-04-the-story-o.subject: Thaddeus
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-04-the-story-o.statement: Thaddeus's first name is Thaddeus.
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-04-the-story-o.quote: “Mr. Thaddeus Sholto,” said the little man, still jerking and smiling. “That is my name.

1890-the-sign-of-the-four-04-the-story-o.subject: Thaddeus
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-04-the-story-o.statement: Thaddeus has just turned thirty.
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-04-the-story-o.quote: In point of fact he had just turned his thirtieth year.

1890-the-sign-of-the-four-04-the-story-o.subject: Thaddeus
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-04-the-story-o.statement: Thaddeus is Major John Sholto's son.
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-04-the-story-o.quote: My father was, as you may have guessed, Major John Sholto, once of the Indian army.

1890-the-sign-of-the-four-04-the-story-o.subject: Bartholomew
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-04-the-story-o.statement: Bartholomew and Thaddeus are twin brothers.
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-04-the-story-o.quote: My twin-brother Bartholomew and I were the only children.

1890-the-sign-of-the-four-04-the-story-o.subject: Bartholomew
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-04-the-story-o.statement: Bartholomew is Major John Sholto's son.
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-04-the-story-o.quote: My twin-brother Bartholomew and I were the only children.

1890-the-sign-of-the-four-04-the-story-o.subject: Thaddeus
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-04-the-story-o.statement: Thaddeus is Major John Sholto's son.
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-04-the-story-o.quote: My twin-brother Bartholomew and I were the only children.

1890-the-sign-of-the-four-04-the-story-o.subject: Thaddeus
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-04-the-story-o.statement: Thaddeus invites Miss Morstan and her companions into his room.
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-04-the-story-o.quote: Pray step into my little sanctum.

1890-the-sign-of-the-four-04-the-story-o.subject: Thaddeus
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-04-the-story-o.statement: Thaddeus asks Dr. Watson to examine his heart.
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-04-the-story-o.quote: I have grave doubts as to my mitral valve, if you would be so very good.

1890-the-sign-of-the-four-04-the-story-o.subject: Dr. Watson
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-04-the-story-o.statement: Dr. Watson listens to Thaddeus's heart and finds nothing amiss.
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-04-the-story-o.quote: I listened to his heart, as requested, but was unable to find anything amiss

1890-the-sign-of-the-four-04-the-story-o.subject: Thaddeus
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-04-the-story-o.value: his mitral valve may be diseased
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-04-the-story-o.statement: Thaddeus says he has long suspected a problem with his mitral valve.
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-04-the-story-o.quote: I am a great sufferer, and I have long had suspicions as to that valve.

1890-the-sign-of-the-four-04-the-story-o.subject: Thaddeus
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-04-the-story-o.statement: Thaddeus asks that no police or officials be involved.
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-04-the-story-o.quote: But let us have no outsiders,—no police or officials.

1890-the-sign-of-the-four-04-the-story-o.subject: Thaddeus
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-04-the-story-o.statement: Thaddeus says that Miss Morstan's father might have lived if he had not strained his heart.
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-04-the-story-o.quote: Had your father, Miss Morstan, refrained from throwing a strain upon his heart, he might have been alive now.

1890-the-sign-of-the-four-04-the-story-o.subject: Major John Sholto
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-04-the-story-o.statement: Major John Sholto was a major in the Indian army and retired from it.
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-04-the-story-o.quote: My father was, as you may have guessed, Major John Sholto, once of the Indian army. He retired some eleven years ago

1890-the-sign-of-the-four-04-the-story-o.subject: Major John Sholto
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-04-the-story-o.statement: Major John Sholto came to live at Pondicherry Lodge after retiring.
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-04-the-story-o.quote: He retired some eleven years ago, and came to live at Pondicherry Lodge in Upper Norwood.

1890-the-sign-of-the-four-04-the-story-o.subject: Major John Sholto
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-04-the-story-o.statement: Major John Sholto bought a house at Pondicherry Lodge.
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-04-the-story-o.quote: With these advantages he bought himself a house, and lived in great luxury.

1890-the-sign-of-the-four-04-the-story-o.subject: Major John Sholto
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-04-the-story-o.statement: Major John Sholto was very fearful of going out alone.
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-04-the-story-o.quote: He was very fearful of going out alone

1890-the-sign-of-the-four-04-the-story-o.subject: Major John Sholto
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-04-the-story-o.statement: Major John Sholto employed two prize-fighters as porters at Pondicherry Lodge.
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-04-the-story-o.quote: he always employed two prize-fighters to act as porters at Pondicherry Lodge.

1890-the-sign-of-the-four-04-the-story-o.subject: Major John Sholto
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-04-the-story-o.statement: Major John Sholto had a marked aversion to men with wooden legs.
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-04-the-story-o.quote: he had a most marked aversion to men with wooden legs.

1890-the-sign-of-the-four-04-the-story-o.subject: Major John Sholto
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-04-the-story-o.statement: Major John Sholto once fired his revolver at a wooden-legged tradesman.
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-04-the-story-o.quote: On one occasion he actually fired his revolver at a wooden-legged man, who proved to be a harmless tradesman canvassing for orders.

1890-the-sign-of-the-four-04-the-story-o.subject: Major John Sholto
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-04-the-story-o.statement: Major John Sholto received a letter from India that shocked him.
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-04-the-story-o.quote: Early in 1882 my father received a letter from India which was a great shock to him.

1890-the-sign-of-the-four-04-the-story-o.subject: Major John Sholto
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-04-the-story-o.statement: Major John Sholto died after becoming rapidly worse following receipt of the letter.
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-04-the-story-o.quote: He had suffered for years from an enlarged spleen, but he now became rapidly worse, and towards the end of April we were informed that he was beyond all hope

1890-the-sign-of-the-four-04-the-story-o.subject: Major John Sholto
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-04-the-story-o.statement: Major John Sholto told his sons that Morstan's orphan was owed at least half of the Agra treasure.
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-04-the-story-o.quote: The cursed greed which has been my besetting sin through life has withheld from her the treasure, half at least of which should have been hers.

1890-the-sign-of-the-four-04-the-story-o.subject: Major John Sholto
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-04-the-story-o.statement: Major John Sholto ordered his sons to give Miss Morstan a fair share of the Agra treasure after he died.
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-04-the-story-o.quote: You, my sons, will give her a fair share of the Agra treasure.

1890-the-sign-of-the-four-04-the-story-o.subject: Major John Sholto
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-04-the-story-o.statement: Major John Sholto could not bear to part with the pearl chaplet he had taken out to send to Miss Morstan.
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-04-the-story-o.quote: Even that I could not bear to part with, although I had got it out with the design of sending it to her.

1890-the-sign-of-the-four-04-the-story-o.subject: Arthur Morstan
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-04-the-story-o.statement: Arthur Morstan had suffered for years from a weak heart.
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-04-the-story-o.quote: He had suffered for years from a weak heart, but he concealed it from every one.

1890-the-sign-of-the-four-04-the-story-o.subject: Arthur Morstan
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-04-the-story-o.statement: Arthur Morstan went to Pondicherry Lodge to claim his share of the treasure.
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-04-the-story-o.quote: on the night of Morstan’s arrival he came straight over here to claim his share.

1890-the-sign-of-the-four-04-the-story-o.subject: Arthur Morstan
