1890-the-sign-of-the-four-04-the-story-o.statement: Arthur Morstan and Major John Sholto argued over how to divide the treasure.
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-04-the-story-o.quote: Morstan and I had a difference of opinion as to the division of the treasure, and we came to heated words.

1890-the-sign-of-the-four-04-the-story-o.subject: Arthur Morstan
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-04-the-story-o.statement: Arthur Morstan died after pressing his hand to his side and falling against the treasure-chest.
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-04-the-story-o.quote: Morstan had sprung out of his chair in a paroxysm of anger, when he suddenly pressed his hand to his side, his face turned a dusky hue, and he fell backwards, cutting his head against the corner of the treasure-chest.

1890-the-sign-of-the-four-04-the-story-o.subject: Major John Sholto
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-04-the-story-o.statement: Major John Sholto and Lal Chowdar hid Arthur Morstan's body that night.
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-04-the-story-o.quote: Lal Chowdar and I disposed of the body that night

1890-the-sign-of-the-four-04-the-story-o.subject: Major John Sholto
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-04-the-story-o.statement: Major John Sholto concealed the treasure along with Arthur Morstan's body.
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-04-the-story-o.quote: My fault lies in the fact that we concealed not only the body, but also the treasure

1890-the-sign-of-the-four-04-the-story-o.subject: Major John Sholto
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-04-the-story-o.statement: Major John Sholto saw a face looking in through his window as he told his sons where the treasure was hidden.
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-04-the-story-o.quote: A face was looking in at us out of the darkness.

1890-the-sign-of-the-four-04-the-story-o.subject: Bartholomew
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-04-the-story-o.statement: Bartholomew and Thaddeus searched the garden for the intruder but found only one footprint.
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-04-the-story-o.quote: We searched the garden that night, but found no sign of the intruder, save that just under the window a single footmark was visible in the flower-bed.

1890-the-sign-of-the-four-04-the-story-o.subject: intruder
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-04-the-story-o.statement: The intruder left a torn piece of paper bearing the words “The sign of the four” on Major John Sholto's chest.
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-04-the-story-o.quote: upon his chest was fixed a torn piece of paper, with the words ‘The sign of the four’ scrawled across it.

1890-the-sign-of-the-four-04-the-story-o.subject: Thaddeus
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-04-the-story-o.statement: Thaddeus and Bartholomew searched the garden for the treasure for weeks and months without finding it.
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-04-the-story-o.quote: For weeks and for months we dug and delved in every part of the garden, without discovering its whereabouts.

1890-the-sign-of-the-four-04-the-story-o.subject: Thaddeus
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-04-the-story-o.statement: Thaddeus persuaded Bartholomew to let him send Miss Morstan a pearl at fixed intervals.
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-04-the-story-o.quote: It was all that I could do to persuade him to let me find out Miss Morstan’s address and send her a detached pearl at fixed intervals

1890-the-sign-of-the-four-04-the-story-o.subject: Bartholomew
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-04-the-story-o.statement: Bartholomew and Thaddeus are twin brothers.
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-04-the-story-o.quote: My brother Bartholomew and I had some little discussion.

1890-the-sign-of-the-four-04-the-story-o.subject: Thaddeus
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-04-the-story-o.statement: Thaddeus left Pondicherry Lodge and took the old khitmutgar and Williams with him.
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-04-the-story-o.quote: so I left Pondicherry Lodge, taking the old khitmutgar and Williams with me.

1890-the-sign-of-the-four-04-the-story-o.subject: Bartholomew
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-04-the-story-o.statement: Bartholomew discovered the treasure indoors in a sealed garret above the highest room.
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-04-the-story-o.quote: there, sure enough, he came upon another little garret above it, which had been sealed up and was known to no one.

1890-the-sign-of-the-four-04-the-story-o.subject: Bartholomew
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-04-the-story-o.value: not less than half a million sterling
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-04-the-story-o.statement: Bartholomew estimated the jewels to be worth at least half a million sterling.
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-04-the-story-o.quote: He computes the value of the jewels at not less than half a million sterling.

1890-the-sign-of-the-four-04-the-story-o.subject: Thaddeus
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-04-the-story-o.statement: Thaddeus contacted Miss Morstan after learning the treasure had been discovered.
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-04-the-story-o.quote: Yesterday, however, I learn that an event of extreme importance has occurred. The treasure has been discovered. I instantly communicated with Miss Morstan

1890-the-sign-of-the-four-04-the-story-o.subject: Thaddeus
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-04-the-story-o.statement: Thaddeus proposed that they drive to Norwood and demand their share of the treasure.
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-04-the-story-o.quote: it only remains for us to drive out to Norwood and demand our share.

1890-the-sign-of-the-four-04-the-story-o.subject: Thaddeus
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-04-the-story-o.statement: Thaddeus travels with Miss Morstan, Holmes, and Watson to Pondicherry Lodge.
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-04-the-story-o.quote: “This, Miss Morstan, is Pondicherry Lodge,” said Mr. Thaddeus Sholto, as he handed her out.

1890-the-sign-of-the-four-04-the-story-o.subject: Miss Morstan
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-04-the-story-o.statement: Miss Morstan tells Thaddeus that she wants the interview to be as short as possible.
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-04-the-story-o.quote: It is very late, and I should desire the interview to be as short as possible.

1890-the-sign-of-the-four-04-the-story-o.subject: Holmes
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-04-the-story-o.statement: Holmes agrees that Thaddeus's account will go no further.
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-04-the-story-o.quote: whatever you may choose to say will go no further.

1890-the-sign-of-the-four-04-the-story-o.subject: Miss Morstan
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-04-the-story-o.statement: Miss Morstan drinks water and rallies after appearing close to fainting.
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-04-the-story-o.quote: She rallied however, on drinking a glass of water which I quietly poured out for her from a Venetian carafe upon the side-table.

1890-the-sign-of-the-four-05-the-tragedy.subject: Pondicherry Lodge
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-05-the-tragedy.value: a very high stone wall topped with broken glass
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-05-the-tragedy.statement: Pondicherry Lodge is surrounded by a very high stone wall topped with broken glass.
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-05-the-tragedy.quote: Pondicherry Lodge stood in its own grounds, and was girt round with a very high stone wall topped with broken glass.

1890-the-sign-of-the-four-05-the-tragedy.subject: Pondicherry Lodge
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-05-the-tragedy.statement: Pondicherry Lodge has a single narrow iron-clamped door as its only entrance.
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-05-the-tragedy.quote: A single narrow iron-clamped door formed the only means of entrance.

1890-the-sign-of-the-four-05-the-tragedy.subject: McMurdo
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-05-the-tragedy.statement: McMurdo is the porter at Pondicherry Lodge.
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-05-the-tragedy.quote: A short, deep-chested man stood in the opening

1890-the-sign-of-the-four-05-the-tragedy.subject: McMurdo
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-05-the-tragedy.statement: McMurdo initially refuses to let Thaddeus's friends into Pondicherry Lodge because he has no orders about them.
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-05-the-tragedy.quote: I can let you in, but your friends must just stop where they are.

1890-the-sign-of-the-four-05-the-tragedy.subject: Sherlock Holmes
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-05-the-tragedy.statement: Sherlock Holmes once fought three rounds with McMurdo as an amateur prize-fighter.
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-05-the-tragedy.quote: Don’t you remember the amateur who fought three rounds with you at Alison’s rooms on the night of your benefit four years back?

1890-the-sign-of-the-four-05-the-tragedy.subject: Sherlock Holmes
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-05-the-tragedy.statement: After McMurdo recognises Holmes, he lets Holmes and his friends enter Pondicherry Lodge.
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-05-the-tragedy.quote: “In you come, sir, in you come,—you and your friends,” he answered.

1890-the-sign-of-the-four-05-the-tragedy.subject: Thaddeus Sholto
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-05-the-tragedy.statement: Thaddeus Sholto and Bartholomew Sholto are twins.
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-05-the-tragedy.quote: Then I recalled to mind that he had mentioned to us that his brother and he were twins.

1890-the-sign-of-the-four-05-the-tragedy.subject: Bartholomew Sholto
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-05-the-tragedy.statement: Bartholomew Sholto and Thaddeus Sholto are twins.
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-05-the-tragedy.quote: Then I recalled to mind that he had mentioned to us that his brother and he were twins.

1890-the-sign-of-the-four-05-the-tragedy.subject: Bartholomew Sholto
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-05-the-tragedy.statement: Bartholomew Sholto was his father’s favourite son.
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-05-the-tragedy.quote: He was the favourite son, you know, and I sometimes think that my father may have told him more than he ever told me.

1890-the-sign-of-the-four-05-the-tragedy.subject: Bartholomew Sholto
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-05-the-tragedy.statement: Bartholomew Sholto guards Pondicherry Lodge, following his father’s custom.
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-05-the-tragedy.quote: Yes; he has followed my father’s custom.

1890-the-sign-of-the-four-05-the-tragedy.subject: Mrs. Bernstone
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-05-the-tragedy.statement: Mrs. Bernstone is the housekeeper at Pondicherry Lodge.
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-05-the-tragedy.quote: Ah, that is the housekeeper’s room. That is where old Mrs. Bernstone sits.

1890-the-sign-of-the-four-05-the-tragedy.subject: Thaddeus Sholto
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-05-the-tragedy.statement: Thaddeus goes to the house to check on Bartholomew after hearing a frightened woman whimpering.
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-05-the-tragedy.quote: “It is Mrs. Bernstone,” said Sholto. “She is the only woman in the house. Wait here. I shall be back in a moment.”

1890-the-sign-of-the-four-05-the-tragedy.subject: Mrs. Bernstone
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-05-the-tragedy.statement: Mrs. Bernstone admits Thaddeus into the house and is glad to see him.
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-05-the-tragedy.quote: We could see a tall old woman admit him, and sway with pleasure at the very sight of him.

1890-the-sign-of-the-four-05-the-tragedy.subject: Treasure-seekers
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-05-the-tragedy.statement: Treasure-seekers searched the grounds for six years, leaving them looking like a gravel-pit.
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-05-the-tragedy.quote: You must remember that they were six years looking for it.

1890-the-sign-of-the-four-05-the-tragedy.subject: Thaddeus Sholto
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-05-the-tragedy.statement: Thaddeus runs from the house and tells the others that something is wrong with Bartholomew.
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-05-the-tragedy.quote: “There is something amiss with Bartholomew!” he cried.

1890-the-sign-of-the-four-05-the-tragedy.subject: Sherlock Holmes
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-05-the-tragedy.statement: Holmes examines marks on the stair carpet with his lens while going upstairs.
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-05-the-tragedy.quote: Twice as we ascended Holmes whipped his lens out of his pocket and carefully examined marks which appeared to me to be mere shapeless smudges of dust upon the cocoa-nut matting which served as a stair-carpet.

1890-the-sign-of-the-four-05-the-tragedy.subject: Sherlock Holmes
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-05-the-tragedy.statement: Holmes and Watson force open the locked door to Bartholomew’s chamber.
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-05-the-tragedy.quote: Together we flung ourselves upon it once more, and this time it gave way with a sudden snap, and we found ourselves within Bartholomew Sholto’s chamber.

1890-the-sign-of-the-four-05-the-tragedy.subject: Bartholomew Sholto’s chamber
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-05-the-tragedy.statement: Bartholomew Sholto’s chamber is fitted up as a chemical laboratory.
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-05-the-tragedy.quote: It appeared to have been fitted up as a chemical laboratory.

1890-the-sign-of-the-four-05-the-tragedy.subject: Sherlock Holmes
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-05-the-tragedy.statement: Holmes and the others find Bartholomew dead in a chair in his chamber.
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-05-the-tragedy.quote: By the table, in a wooden arm-chair, the master of the house was seated all in a heap, with his head sunk upon his left shoulder, and that ghastly, inscrutable smile upon his face.

1890-the-sign-of-the-four-05-the-tragedy.subject: Bartholomew Sholto
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-05-the-tragedy.statement: Bartholomew Sholto is dead when the others find him.
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-05-the-tragedy.quote: He was stiff and cold, and had clearly been dead many hours.

1890-the-sign-of-the-four-05-the-tragedy.subject: Bartholomew Sholto
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-05-the-tragedy.statement: A torn note bearing the words “The sign of the four” lies beside Bartholomew Sholto.
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-05-the-tragedy.quote: In the light of the lantern I read, with a thrill of horror, “The sign of the four.”

1890-the-sign-of-the-four-05-the-tragedy.subject: Sherlock Holmes
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-05-the-tragedy.statement: Holmes says that Bartholomew’s death is murder.
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-05-the-tragedy.quote: “It means murder,” said he, stooping over the dead man.

1890-the-sign-of-the-four-05-the-tragedy.subject: the thorn
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-05-the-tragedy.statement: The thorn found in Bartholomew’s skin is poisoned.
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-05-the-tragedy.quote: It is a thorn. You may pick it out. But be careful, for it is poisoned.

1890-the-sign-of-the-four-05-the-tragedy.subject: Watson
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-05-the-tragedy.statement: Watson removes the poisoned thorn from Bartholomew’s skin.
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-05-the-tragedy.quote: I took it up between my finger and thumb.

1890-the-sign-of-the-four-05-the-tragedy.subject: Thaddeus Sholto
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-05-the-tragedy.statement: Thaddeus says the treasure has been stolen from Bartholomew’s chamber.
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-05-the-tragedy.quote: “The treasure is gone!” he said. “They have robbed him of the treasure!”

1890-the-sign-of-the-four-05-the-tragedy.subject: Thaddeus Sholto
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-05-the-tragedy.statement: Thaddeus helped Bartholomew lower the treasure through the opening in the ceiling.
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-05-the-tragedy.quote: There is the hole through which we lowered it. I helped him to do it!

1890-the-sign-of-the-four-05-the-tragedy.subject: Thaddeus Sholto
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-05-the-tragedy.statement: Thaddeus says he was the last person to see Bartholomew alive.
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-05-the-tragedy.quote: I was the last person who saw him!

1890-the-sign-of-the-four-05-the-tragedy.subject: Thaddeus Sholto
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-05-the-tragedy.statement: Thaddeus says he left Bartholomew in his chamber the previous night and heard him lock the door.
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-05-the-tragedy.quote: I left him here last night, and I heard him lock the door as I came downstairs.

1890-the-sign-of-the-four-05-the-tragedy.subject: Thaddeus Sholto
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-05-the-tragedy.statement: Thaddeus says he heard Bartholomew lock the door at ten o’clock.
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-05-the-tragedy.quote: “It was ten o’clock.

1890-the-sign-of-the-four-05-the-tragedy.subject: Sherlock Holmes
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-05-the-tragedy.statement: Holmes advises Thaddeus to report Bartholomew’s death to the police and offer his assistance.
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-05-the-tragedy.quote: Take my advice, and drive down to the station to report this matter to the police.

1890-the-sign-of-the-four-05-the-tragedy.subject: Thaddeus Sholto
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-05-the-tragedy.statement: Thaddeus obeys Holmes’s advice and goes to the station.
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-05-the-tragedy.quote: The little man obeyed in a half-stupefied fashion, and we heard him stumbling down the stairs in the dark.

1890-the-sign-of-the-four-06-sherlock-ho.subject: Holmes
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-06-sherlock-ho.statement: Holmes examines the window and observes that it is snibbed on the inner side and has a solid framework.
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-06-sherlock-ho.quote: Window is snibbed on the inner side. Framework is solid.

1890-the-sign-of-the-four-06-sherlock-ho.subject: Holmes
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-06-sherlock-ho.value: A wooden-legged man entered and left through the window with an ally's help.
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-06-sherlock-ho.statement: Holmes infers that a wooden-legged man entered and left through the window with an ally's help.
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-06-sherlock-ho.quote: You would depart, of course, in the same fashion, and your ally would draw up the rope, untie it from the hook, shut the window, snib it on the inside, and get away in the way that he originally came.

1890-the-sign-of-the-four-06-sherlock-ho.subject: Holmes
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-06-sherlock-ho.value: The wooden-legged man slipped on the rope and injured his hand.
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-06-sherlock-ho.statement: Holmes infers that the wooden-legged man slipped down the rope and took skin off his hand.
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-06-sherlock-ho.quote: My lens discloses more than one blood-mark, especially towards the end of the rope, from which I gather that he slipped down with such velocity that he took the skin off his hand.

1890-the-sign-of-the-four-06-sherlock-ho.subject: Holmes
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-06-sherlock-ho.statement: Holmes concludes that the ally entered through a hole in the roof.
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-06-sherlock-ho.quote:
He came through the hole in the roof,” I cried.

“Of course he did.

1890-the-sign-of-the-four-06-sherlock-ho.subject: Holmes
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-06-sherlock-ho.statement: Holmes climbs into the garret to investigate the room above.
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-06-sherlock-ho.quote: He mounted the steps, and, seizing a rafter with either hand, he swung himself up into the garret.

1890-the-sign-of-the-four-06-sherlock-ho.subject: Watson
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-06-sherlock-ho.statement: Watson follows Holmes into the garret.
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-06-sherlock-ho.quote: Then, lying on his face, he reached down for the lamp and held it while I followed him.

1890-the-sign-of-the-four-06-sherlock-ho.subject: garret
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-06-sherlock-ho.value: the secret room in which the treasure was found
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-06-sherlock-ho.statement: The garret is the secret room in which the treasure was found.
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-06-sherlock-ho.quote: the secret room in which the treasure was found.

1890-the-sign-of-the-four-06-sherlock-ho.subject: Holmes
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-06-sherlock-ho.statement: Holmes identifies a trap-door in the garret that leads onto the roof.
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-06-sherlock-ho.quote: This is a trap-door which leads out on to the roof.

1890-the-sign-of-the-four-06-sherlock-ho.subject: Holmes
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-06-sherlock-ho.value: Number One entered through the trap-door onto the roof.
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-06-sherlock-ho.statement: Holmes concludes that Number One entered through the trap-door onto the roof.
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-06-sherlock-ho.quote: This, then, is the way by which Number One entered.

1890-the-sign-of-the-four-06-sherlock-ho.subject: Holmes
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-06-sherlock-ho.value: The garret floor bears clear prints of a naked foot about half the size of an ordinary man's foot.
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-06-sherlock-ho.statement: Holmes and Watson find small naked-foot prints across the garret floor.
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-06-sherlock-ho.quote: The floor was covered thickly with the prints of a naked foot,—clear, well defined, perfectly formed, but scarce half the size of those of an ordinary man.

1890-the-sign-of-the-four-06-sherlock-ho.subject: Holmes
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-06-sherlock-ho.statement: Holmes searches the room with a lens and tape measure.
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-06-sherlock-ho.quote: He whipped out his lens and a tape measure, and hurried about the room on his knees, measuring, comparing, examining, with his long thin nose only a few inches from the planks

1890-the-sign-of-the-four-06-sherlock-ho.subject: Holmes
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-06-sherlock-ho.statement: Holmes finds that Number One stepped in creosote.
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-06-sherlock-ho.quote: Number One has had the misfortune to tread in the creosote.

1890-the-sign-of-the-four-06-sherlock-ho.subject: Holmes
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-06-sherlock-ho.statement: Holmes says Toby can follow the creosote scent over a great distance.
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-06-sherlock-ho.quote: I know a dog that would follow that scent to the world’s end.

1890-the-sign-of-the-four-06-sherlock-ho.subject: Holmes
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-06-sherlock-ho.statement: Holmes asks Watson to feel the dead man's arm and leg.
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-06-sherlock-ho.quote: Before they come,” said Holmes, “just put your hand here on this poor fellow’s arm, and here on his leg.

1890-the-sign-of-the-four-06-sherlock-ho.subject: Holmes
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-06-sherlock-ho.value: The dead man's muscles are in extreme contraction, beyond ordinary rigor mortis.
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-06-sherlock-ho.statement: Holmes observes extreme muscular contraction in the dead man.
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-06-sherlock-ho.quote: They are in a state of extreme contraction, far exceeding the usual _rigor mortis_.

1890-the-sign-of-the-four-06-sherlock-ho.subject: Holmes
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-06-sherlock-ho.value: The man died from a powerful vegetable alkaloid.
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-06-sherlock-ho.statement: Holmes and Watson infer that the man died from a powerful vegetable alkaloid.
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-06-sherlock-ho.quote: “Death from some powerful vegetable alkaloid,” I answered,—“some strychnine-like substance which would produce tetanus.”

1890-the-sign-of-the-four-06-sherlock-ho.subject: Holmes
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-06-sherlock-ho.statement: Holmes finds a thorn driven or shot into the dead man's scalp as the means by which poison entered his system.
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-06-sherlock-ho.quote: As you saw, I discovered a thorn which had been driven or shot with no great force into the scalp.

1890-the-sign-of-the-four-06-sherlock-ho.subject: Watson
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-06-sherlock-ho.statement: Watson picks up the thorn and examines it in the lantern light.
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-06-sherlock-ho.quote: I took it up gingerly and held it in the light of the lantern.

1890-the-sign-of-the-four-06-sherlock-ho.subject: Watson
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-06-sherlock-ho.statement: Watson says the thorn is not English.
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-06-sherlock-ho.quote: “No, it certainly is not.”

1890-the-sign-of-the-four-06-sherlock-ho.subject: Athelney Jones
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-06-sherlock-ho.statement: Athelney Jones enters the room with an inspector and Thaddeus Sholto.
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-06-sherlock-ho.quote: He was closely followed by an inspector in uniform, and by the still palpitating Thaddeus Sholto.

1890-the-sign-of-the-four-06-sherlock-ho.subject: Athelney Jones
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-06-sherlock-ho.statement: Athelney Jones proposes that Thaddeus took the treasure after his brother died.
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-06-sherlock-ho.quote: The brother died in a fit, on which Sholto walked off with the treasure.

1890-the-sign-of-the-four-06-sherlock-ho.subject: Holmes
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-06-sherlock-ho.statement: Holmes challenges Jones's theory by pointing out that it would require the dead man to lock the door from inside.
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-06-sherlock-ho.quote: On which the dead man very considerately got up and locked the door on the inside.

1890-the-sign-of-the-four-06-sherlock-ho.subject: Holmes
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-06-sherlock-ho.statement: Holmes presents Jones with the poisoned splinter, the card, and a stone-headed instrument as evidence.
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-06-sherlock-ho.quote: This splinter of wood, which I have every reason to believe to be poisoned, was in the man’s scalp where you still see the mark; this card, inscribed as you see it, was on the table; and beside it lay this rather curious stone-headed instrument.

1890-the-sign-of-the-four-06-sherlock-ho.subject: Athelney Jones
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-06-sherlock-ho.statement: Athelney Jones climbs into the garret and finds the trap-door.
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-06-sherlock-ho.quote: With great activity, considering his bulk, he sprang up the steps and squeezed through into the garret, and immediately afterwards we heard his exulting voice proclaiming that he had found the trap-door.

1890-the-sign-of-the-four-06-sherlock-ho.subject: Athelney Jones
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-06-sherlock-ho.statement: Athelney Jones arrests Thaddeus Sholto for being concerned in his brother's death.
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-06-sherlock-ho.quote: I arrest you in the Queen’s name as being concerned in the death of your brother.

1890-the-sign-of-the-four-06-sherlock-ho.subject: Holmes
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-06-sherlock-ho.statement: Holmes tells Thaddeus that he can clear him of the charge.
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-06-sherlock-ho.quote: I think that I can engage to clear you of the charge.

1890-the-sign-of-the-four-06-sherlock-ho.subject: Holmes
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-06-sherlock-ho.statement: Holmes identifies Jonathan Small as one of the two people who were in the room the previous night.
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-06-sherlock-ho.quote: His name, I have every reason to believe, is Jonathan Small.

1890-the-sign-of-the-four-06-sherlock-ho.subject: Jonathan Small
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-06-sherlock-ho.statement: Jonathan Small's right leg is off.
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-06-sherlock-ho.quote: with his right leg off

1890-the-sign-of-the-four-06-sherlock-ho.subject: Jonathan Small
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-06-sherlock-ho.statement: Jonathan Small wears a wooden stump that is worn away on the inner side.
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-06-sherlock-ho.quote: wearing a wooden stump which is worn away upon the inner side.

1890-the-sign-of-the-four-06-sherlock-ho.subject: Jonathan Small
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-06-sherlock-ho.value: a coarse, square-toed sole, with an iron band round the heel
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-06-sherlock-ho.statement: Jonathan Small's left boot has a coarse, square-toed sole and an iron band around the heel.
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-06-sherlock-ho.quote: His left boot has a coarse, square-toed sole, with an iron band round the heel.

1890-the-sign-of-the-four-06-sherlock-ho.subject: Jonathan Small
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-06-sherlock-ho.statement: Jonathan Small has been a convict.
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-06-sherlock-ho.quote: and has been a convict.

1890-the-sign-of-the-four-06-sherlock-ho.subject: Holmes
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-06-sherlock-ho.statement: Holmes says he will give Jones the name and description of one of the two people in the room.
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-06-sherlock-ho.quote: I will make you a free present of the name and description of one of the two people who were in this room last night.

1890-the-sign-of-the-four-06-sherlock-ho.subject: Holmes
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-06-sherlock-ho.statement: Holmes plans to question Mrs. Bernstone and the Indian servant.
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-06-sherlock-ho.quote: I,” said Holmes, “shall see what I can learn from Mrs. Bernstone, and from the Indian servant, who, Mr. Thaddeus tell me, sleeps in the next garret.

1890-the-sign-of-the-four-06-sherlock-ho.subject: Holmes
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-06-sherlock-ho.statement: Holmes asks Watson to escort Miss Morstan home to Mrs. Cecil Forrester in Lower Camberwell.
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-06-sherlock-ho.quote: You must escort her home. She lives with Mrs. Cecil Forrester, in Lower Camberwell: so it is not very far.

1890-the-sign-of-the-four-06-sherlock-ho.subject: Watson
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-06-sherlock-ho.statement: Watson agrees to escort Miss Morstan home and return to the investigation.
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-06-sherlock-ho.quote: I should like, however, to see the matter through with you, now that I have got so far.

1890-the-sign-of-the-four-06-sherlock-ho.subject: Holmes
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-06-sherlock-ho.statement: Holmes directs Watson to go to No. 3, Pinchin Lane, after dropping Miss Morstan, and fetch Toby from Sherman.
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-06-sherlock-ho.quote: When you have dropped Miss Morstan I wish you to go on to No. 3, Pinchin Lane, down near the water’s edge at Lambeth.

1890-the-sign-of-the-four-06-sherlock-ho.subject: Sherman's shop
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-06-sherlock-ho.statement: Sherman's bird-stuffing shop is the third house on the right-hand side at No. 3, Pinchin Lane.
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-06-sherlock-ho.quote: The third house on the right-hand side is a bird-stuffer’s: Sherman is the name.

1890-the-sign-of-the-four-06-sherlock-ho.subject: Watson
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-06-sherlock-ho.statement: Watson agrees to fetch Toby and bring him back in the cab.
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-06-sherlock-ho.quote: “I shall bring him, then,” said I.

1890-the-sign-of-the-four-06-sherlock-ho.subject: Toby
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-06-sherlock-ho.statement: Toby is a queer mongrel with an exceptional sense of smell.
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-06-sherlock-ho.quote: Yes,—a queer mongrel, with a most amazing power of scent.

1890-the-sign-of-the-four-07-the-episode.subject: Watson
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-07-the-episode.statement: Watson escorted Miss Morstan home in a cab.
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-07-the-episode.quote: The police had brought a cab with them, and in this I escorted Miss Morstan back to her home.

1890-the-sign-of-the-four-07-the-episode.subject: Miss Morstan
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-07-the-episode.statement: Miss Morstan turned faint and then wept in the cab.
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-07-the-episode.quote: In the cab, however, she first turned faint, and then burst into a passion of weeping,—so sorely had she been tried by the adventures of the night.

1890-the-sign-of-the-four-07-the-episode.subject: Miss Morstan
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-07-the-episode.statement: Watson loved Miss Morstan.
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-07-the-episode.quote: My sympathies and my love went out to her, even as my hand had in the garden.

1890-the-sign-of-the-four-07-the-episode.subject: Watson
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-07-the-episode.statement: Watson withheld a confession of love because he feared taking advantage of Miss Morstan and being seen as a fortune-seeker.
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-07-the-episode.quote: Yet there were two thoughts which sealed the words of affection upon my lips.

1890-the-sign-of-the-four-07-the-episode.subject: Watson
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-07-the-episode.statement: Watson and Miss Morstan reached Mrs. Cecil Forrester’s shortly before two o’clock.
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-07-the-episode.quote: It was nearly two o’clock when we reached Mrs. Cecil Forrester’s.

1890-the-sign-of-the-four-07-the-episode.subject: Mrs. Forrester
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-07-the-episode.statement: Mrs. Forrester opened the door and greeted Miss Morstan warmly.
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-07-the-episode.quote: She opened the door herself, a middle-aged, graceful woman, and it gave me joy to see how tenderly her arm stole round the other’s waist and how motherly was the voice in which she greeted her.

1890-the-sign-of-the-four-07-the-episode.subject: Mrs. Forrester
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-07-the-episode.statement: Mrs. Forrester is an honoured friend of Miss Morstan, not merely a paid dependant.
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-07-the-episode.quote: She was clearly no mere paid dependant, but an honoured friend.

1890-the-sign-of-the-four-07-the-episode.subject: Mrs. Forrester
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-07-the-episode.statement: Mrs. Forrester asked Watson to come in and tell her about their adventures.
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-07-the-episode.quote: Mrs. Forrester earnestly begged me to step in and tell her our adventures.

1890-the-sign-of-the-four-07-the-episode.subject: Watson
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-07-the-episode.statement: Watson declined to go in because his errand was important and promised to report progress later.
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-07-the-episode.quote: I explained, however, the importance of my errand, and promised faithfully to call and report any progress which we might make with the case.

1890-the-sign-of-the-four-07-the-episode.subject: Watson
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-07-the-episode.statement: Watson reviewed the events of the case as he travelled away.
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-07-the-episode.quote: I reviewed the whole extraordinary sequence of events as I rattled on through the silent gas-lit streets.

1890-the-sign-of-the-four-07-the-episode.subject: Pinchin Lane
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-07-the-episode.object: row of shabby two-storied brick houses in Lambeth
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-07-the-episode.statement: Pinchin Lane is a row of shabby two-storied brick houses in the lower quarter of Lambeth.
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-07-the-episode.quote: Pinchin Lane was a row of shabby two-storied brick houses in the lower quarter of Lambeth.

1890-the-sign-of-the-four-07-the-episode.subject: Watson
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-07-the-episode.statement: Watson knocked for some time at No. 3 Pinchin Lane.
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-07-the-episode.quote: I had to knock for some time at No. 3 before I could make my impression.

1890-the-sign-of-the-four-07-the-episode.subject: Sherman
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-07-the-episode.statement: Sherman threatened to drop a wiper on Watson if he did not leave.
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-07-the-episode.quote: So help me gracious, I have a wiper in the bag, an’ I’ll drop it on your ’ead if you don’t hook it.

1890-the-sign-of-the-four-07-the-episode.subject: Watson
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-07-the-episode.statement: Watson told Sherman that he wanted a dog.
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-07-the-episode.quote: “But I want a dog,” I cried.

1890-the-sign-of-the-four-07-the-episode.subject: Watson
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-07-the-episode.statement: Watson began to identify himself by mentioning Sherlock Holmes, and Sherman immediately opened the door.
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-07-the-episode.quote: “Mr. Sherlock Holmes—” I began, but the words had a most magical effect, for the window instantly slammed down, and within a minute the door was unbarred and open.

1890-the-sign-of-the-four-07-the-episode.subject: Sherman
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-07-the-episode.statement: Sherman keeps a collection of animals.
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-07-the-episode.quote: He moved slowly forward with his candle among the queer animal family which he had gathered round him.

1890-the-sign-of-the-four-07-the-episode.subject: Sherman
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-07-the-episode.statement: Sherman said that the dog Holmes wanted was Toby.
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-07-the-episode.quote: “Ah! that would be Toby.”

1890-the-sign-of-the-four-07-the-episode.subject: Toby
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-07-the-episode.statement: Toby lives at No. 7 on the left of Sherman’s house.
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-07-the-episode.quote: “Toby lives at No. 7 on the left here.”

1890-the-sign-of-the-four-07-the-episode.subject: Toby
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-07-the-episode.statement: Toby is half spaniel and half lurcher.
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-07-the-episode.quote: Toby proved to be an ugly, long-haired, lop-eared creature, half spaniel and half lurcher, brown-and-white in colour, with a very clumsy waddling gait.

1890-the-sign-of-the-four-07-the-episode.subject: Toby
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-07-the-episode.statement: Toby is brown-and-white.
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-07-the-episode.quote: Toby proved to be an ugly, long-haired, lop-eared creature, half spaniel and half lurcher, brown-and-white in colour, with a very clumsy waddling gait.

1890-the-sign-of-the-four-07-the-episode.subject: Toby
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-07-the-episode.statement: After accepting sugar, Toby followed Watson to the cab.
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-07-the-episode.quote: It accepted after some hesitation a lump of sugar which the old naturalist handed to me, and, having thus sealed an alliance, it followed me to the cab, and made no difficulties about accompanying me.

1890-the-sign-of-the-four-07-the-episode.subject: Watson
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-07-the-episode.statement: Watson returned to Pondicherry Lodge just after three o’clock with Toby.
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-07-the-episode.quote: It had just struck three on the Palace clock when I found myself back once more at Pondicherry Lodge.

1890-the-sign-of-the-four-07-the-episode.subject: McMurdo
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-07-the-episode.statement: McMurdo had been arrested as an accessory.
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-07-the-episode.quote: The ex-prize-fighter McMurdo had, I found, been arrested as an accessory, and both he and Mr. Sholto had been marched off to the station.

1890-the-sign-of-the-four-07-the-episode.subject: Watson
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-07-the-episode.statement: Two constables let Watson pass into Pondicherry Lodge with Toby after he mentioned the detective’s name.
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-07-the-episode.quote: Two constables guarded the narrow gate, but they allowed me to pass with the dog on my mentioning the detective’s name.

1890-the-sign-of-the-four-07-the-episode.subject: Holmes
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-07-the-episode.statement: Holmes told Watson that Athelney Jones had arrested Thaddeus Sholto, the gatekeeper, the housekeeper, and the Indian servant.
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-07-the-episode.quote: He has arrested not only friend Thaddeus, but the gatekeeper, the housekeeper, and the Indian servant.

1890-the-sign-of-the-four-07-the-episode.subject: Holmes
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-07-the-episode.statement: Holmes told Watson to leave Toby and come upstairs.
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-07-the-episode.quote: Leave the dog here, and come up.

1890-the-sign-of-the-four-07-the-episode.subject: Watson
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-07-the-episode.statement: Watson and Holmes tied Toby to the hall table before going upstairs.
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-07-the-episode.quote: We tied Toby to the hall table, and re-ascended the stairs.

1890-the-sign-of-the-four-07-the-episode.subject: Holmes
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-07-the-episode.statement: Holmes directed Watson to examine the footprints in the dust.
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-07-the-episode.quote: “I wish you particularly to notice these footmarks,” he said.

1890-the-sign-of-the-four-07-the-episode.subject: Watson
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-07-the-episode.statement: Watson said the footprints belonged to a child or small woman.
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-07-the-episode.quote: “They belong,” I said, “to a child or a small woman.”

1890-the-sign-of-the-four-07-the-episode.subject: Holmes
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-07-the-episode.statement: Holmes observed that the other footprint had each toe distinctly divided, unlike his own cramped toes.
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-07-the-episode.quote: “Quite so. That is the point.”

1890-the-sign-of-the-four-07-the-episode.subject: Holmes
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-07-the-episode.statement: Holmes asked Watson to smell the edge of the flap-window’s woodwork.
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-07-the-episode.quote: “Now, would you kindly step over to that flap-window and smell the edge of the wood-work? I shall stay here, as I have this handkerchief in my hand.”

1890-the-sign-of-the-four-07-the-episode.subject: Watson
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-07-the-episode.statement: Watson smelled a strong tarry odour at the flap-window.
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-07-the-episode.quote: I did as he directed, and was instantly conscious of a strong tarry smell.

1890-the-sign-of-the-four-07-the-episode.subject: Holmes
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-07-the-episode.statement: Holmes inferred that the suspect had put his foot on the flap-window’s woodwork while escaping.
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-07-the-episode.quote: “That is where he put his foot in getting out.”

1890-the-sign-of-the-four-07-the-episode.subject: Holmes
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-07-the-episode.statement: Holmes ordered Watson to loose Toby and look for Blondin.
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-07-the-episode.quote: “Now run downstairs, loose the dog, and look out for Blondin.”

1890-the-sign-of-the-four-07-the-episode.subject: Holmes
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-07-the-episode.statement: Holmes crawled along the roof ridge of Pondicherry Lodge.
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-07-the-episode.quote: By the time that I got out into the grounds Sherlock Holmes was on the roof, and I could see him like an enormous glow-worm crawling very slowly along the ridge.

1890-the-sign-of-the-four-07-the-episode.subject: Holmes
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-07-the-episode.statement: Holmes descended the wall and landed on the water-barrel.
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-07-the-episode.quote: Then with a light spring he came on to the barrel, and from there to the earth.

1890-the-sign-of-the-four-07-the-episode.subject: Holmes
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-07-the-episode.statement: Holmes found a small pouch containing six dark wooden spines.
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-07-the-episode.quote: Inside were half a dozen spines of dark wood, sharp at one end and rounded at the other, like that which had struck Bartholomew Sholto.

1890-the-sign-of-the-four-07-the-episode.subject: Holmes
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-07-the-episode.statement: Holmes put the creasote handkerchief under Toby’s nose to give the dog the scent.
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-07-the-episode.quote: He pushed the creasote handkerchief under the dog’s nose, while the creature stood with its fluffy legs separated, and with a most comical cock to its head, like a connoisseur sniffing the _bouquet_ of a famous vintage.

1890-the-sign-of-the-four-07-the-episode.subject: Holmes
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-07-the-episode.statement: Holmes fastened a cord to Toby’s collar and led him to the water-barrel.
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-07-the-episode.quote: Holmes then threw the handkerchief to a distance, fastened a stout cord to the mongrel’s collar, and led him to the foot of the water-barrel.

1890-the-sign-of-the-four-07-the-episode.subject: Toby
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-07-the-episode.statement: Toby followed the scent trail at a pace that kept Holmes and Watson running to keep up.
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-07-the-episode.quote: The creature instantly broke into a succession of high, tremulous yelps, and, with his nose on the ground, and his tail in the air, pattered off upon the trail at a pace which strained his leash and kept us at the top of our speed.

1890-the-sign-of-the-four-07-the-episode.subject: Toby
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-07-the-episode.object: trail beyond Pondicherry Lodge boundary wall
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-07-the-episode.statement: Toby followed the scent along the boundary wall and stopped at a corner screened by a young beech.
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-07-the-episode.quote: On reaching the boundary wall Toby ran along, whining eagerly, underneath its shadow, and stopped finally in a corner screened by a young beech.

1890-the-sign-of-the-four-07-the-episode.subject: Holmes
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-07-the-episode.statement: Holmes climbed over the boundary wall and dropped Toby onto the other side.
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-07-the-episode.quote: Holmes clambered up, and, taking the dog from me, he dropped it over upon the other side.

1890-the-sign-of-the-four-07-the-episode.subject: Holmes
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-07-the-episode.statement: Holmes concluded that the wooden-legged man was Jonathan Small.
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-07-the-episode.quote: Therefore we may say with confidence that the wooden-legged man is identical with Jonathan Small.

1890-the-sign-of-the-four-07-the-episode.subject: Jonathan Small
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-07-the-episode.statement: Holmes hypothesized that Jonathan Small and his associates were convicts and could not get away to obtain the treasure.
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-07-the-episode.quote: Jonathan Small did not get the treasure because he and his associates were themselves convicts and could not get away.

1890-the-sign-of-the-four-07-the-episode.subject: Jonathan Small
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-07-the-episode.statement: Holmes theorized that Jonathan Small came to England seeking his rights and revenge on Major Sholto.
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-07-the-episode.quote: He comes to England with the double idea of regaining what he would consider to be his rights and of having his revenge upon the man who had wronged him.

1890-the-sign-of-the-four-07-the-episode.subject: Jonathan Small
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-07-the-episode.statement: Holmes theorized that Jonathan Small left an inscription on the card after searching Major Sholto’s papers.
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-07-the-episode.quote: Mad with hate, however, against the dead man, he enters the room that night, searches his private papers in the hope of discovering some memorandum relating to the treasure, and finally leaves a momento of his visit in the short inscription upon the card.

1890-the-sign-of-the-four-07-the-episode.subject: Jonathan Small
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-07-the-episode.statement: Holmes theorized that Jonathan Small brought an associate who could reach Bartholomew Sholto’s lofty room.
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-07-the-episode.quote: He takes with him, however, a rather curious associate, who gets over this difficulty, but dips his naked foot into creasote, whence comes Toby, and a six-mile limp for a half-pay officer with a damaged tendo Achillis.

1890-the-sign-of-the-four-07-the-episode.subject: associate
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-07-the-episode.statement: Holmes said the associate committed the crime and killed Bartholomew Sholto with poison.
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-07-the-episode.quote: But it was the associate, and not Jonathan, who committed the crime.

1890-the-sign-of-the-four-07-the-episode.subject: Jonathan Small
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-07-the-episode.statement: Holmes theorized that Jonathan Small lowered the treasure-box to the ground and followed it himself.
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-07-the-episode.quote: so Jonathan Small left his record, lowered the treasure-box to the ground, and followed it himself.

1890-the-sign-of-the-four-07-the-episode.subject: Holmes
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-07-the-episode.statement: Holmes loaded two chambers of his revolver before continuing the pursuit.
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-07-the-episode.quote: He took out his revolver as he spoke, and, having loaded two of the chambers, he put it back into the right-hand pocket of his jacket.

1890-the-sign-of-the-four-07-the-episode.subject: Holmes
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-07-the-episode.statement: Holmes asked Watson if he was ready for a six-mile walk.
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-07-the-episode.quote: “Are you game for a six-mile trudge, Watson?”

1890-the-sign-of-the-four-07-the-episode.subject: Watson
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-07-the-episode.statement: Watson agreed to the six-mile walk.
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-07-the-episode.quote: “Certainly,” I answered.

1890-the-sign-of-the-four-07-the-episode.subject: Holmes
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-07-the-episode.statement: Holmes and Watson followed Toby through Streatham, Brixton, Camberwell, and Kennington Lane.
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-07-the-episode.quote: We had traversed Streatham, Brixton, Camberwell, and now found ourselves in Kennington Lane, having borne away through the side-streets to the east of the Oval.

1890-the-sign-of-the-four-07-the-episode.subject: Toby
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-07-the-episode.statement: Toby stopped advancing at Knight’s Place and ran back and forth uncertainly.
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-07-the-episode.quote: Where the latter street turns into Knight’s Place, Toby ceased to advance, but began to run backwards and forwards with one ear cocked and the other drooping, the very picture of canine indecision.

1890-the-sign-of-the-four-07-the-episode.subject: Toby
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-07-the-episode.statement: After sniffing around, Toby made up his mind and darted away along the scent.
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-07-the-episode.quote: He was indeed off, for after sniffing round again he suddenly made up his mind, and darted away with an energy and determination such as he had not yet shown.

1890-the-sign-of-the-four-07-the-episode.subject: Toby
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-07-the-episode.statement: Toby turned through the side-gate into Broderick and Nelson’s timber-yard.
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-07-the-episode.quote: Here the dog, frantic with excitement, turned down through the side-gate into the enclosure, where the sawyers were already at work.

1890-the-sign-of-the-four-07-the-episode.subject: Toby
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-07-the-episode.statement: Toby tracked the scent to a large barrel on a hand-trolley and sprang onto it.
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-07-the-episode.quote: On the dog raced through sawdust and shavings, down an alley, round a passage, between two wood-piles, and finally, with a triumphant yelp, sprang upon a large barrel which still stood upon the hand-trolley on which it had been brought.

1890-the-sign-of-the-four-07-the-episode.subject: barrel
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-07-the-episode.statement: The barrel and its trolley were smeared with a dark liquid, and the air smelled strongly of creasote.
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-07-the-episode.quote: The staves of the barrel and the wheels of the trolley were smeared with a dark liquid, and the whole air was heavy with the smell of creasote.

1890-the-sign-of-the-four-07-the-episode.subject: Holmes
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-07-the-episode.statement: Holmes and Watson laughed when they realized Toby had led them to the creasote barrel.
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-07-the-episode.quote: Sherlock Holmes and I looked blankly at each other, and then burst simultaneously into an uncontrollable fit of laughter.

1890-the-sign-of-the-four-08-the-baker-s.subject: Holmes
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-08-the-baker-s.statement: Holmes walks Toby out of the timber-yard after lifting him down from a barrel.
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-08-the-baker-s.quote: Holmes, lifting him down from the barrel and walking him out of the timber-yard.

1890-the-sign-of-the-four-08-the-baker-s.subject: Holmes
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-08-the-baker-s.statement: Holmes says Toby is not to blame because creosote trails can cross.
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-08-the-baker-s.quote: Poor Toby is not to blame.

1890-the-sign-of-the-four-08-the-baker-s.subject: Holmes
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-08-the-baker-s.statement: Holmes and Watson lead Toby back to where he lost the scent, and Toby finds a fresh direction.
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-08-the-baker-s.quote: On leading Toby to the place where he had committed his fault, he cast about in a wide circle and finally dashed off in a fresh direction.

1890-the-sign-of-the-four-08-the-baker-s.subject: Holmes
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-08-the-baker-s.statement: Holmes concludes that they are following the true scent because it stays on the pavement while the barrel travelled in the roadway.
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-08-the-baker-s.quote: But you notice that he keeps on the pavement, whereas the barrel passed down the roadway. No, we are on the true scent now.

1890-the-sign-of-the-four-08-the-baker-s.subject: Toby
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-08-the-baker-s.statement: Toby follows the trail through Belmont Place and Prince’s Street to the water’s edge at the small wharf at the end of Broad Street.
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-08-the-baker-s.quote: At the end of Broad Street it ran right down to the water’s edge, where there was a small wooden wharf. Toby led us to the very edge of this, and there stood whining, looking out on the dark current beyond.

1890-the-sign-of-the-four-08-the-baker-s.subject: Holmes
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-08-the-baker-s.statement: Holmes concludes that the fugitives took a boat from the wharf.
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-08-the-baker-s.quote: “We are out of luck,” said Holmes. “They have taken to a boat here.”

1890-the-sign-of-the-four-08-the-baker-s.subject: Holmes
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-08-the-baker-s.statement: Holmes and Watson take Toby around the nearby punts and skiffs, but Toby does not identify any of them.
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-08-the-baker-s.quote: We took Toby round to each in turn, but, though he sniffed earnestly, he made no sign.

1890-the-sign-of-the-four-08-the-baker-s.subject: Jack
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-08-the-baker-s.statement: Jack runs out of the house, followed by Mrs. Smith, who calls him back to be washed.
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-08-the-baker-s.quote: and a little, curly-headed lad of six came running out, followed by a stoutish, red-faced woman with a large sponge in her hand.

1890-the-sign-of-the-four-08-the-baker-s.subject: Jack
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-08-the-baker-s.statement: Jack is six years old.
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-08-the-baker-s.quote: a little, curly-headed lad of six came running out

1890-the-sign-of-the-four-08-the-baker-s.subject: Holmes
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-08-the-baker-s.statement: Holmes gives Jack two shillings after asking what he would like.
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-08-the-baker-s.quote:
“I’d like two shillin’ better,” the prodigy answered, after some thought.

“Here you are, then! Catch!—A fine child, Mrs. Smith!”

1890-the-sign-of-the-four-08-the-baker-s.subject: Mrs. Smith
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-08-the-baker-s.statement: Mrs. Smith says her husband has been away since the previous morning and that she is frightened about him.
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-08-the-baker-s.quote: “He’s been away since yesterday mornin’, sir, and, truth to tell, I am beginnin’ to feel frightened about him.”

1890-the-sign-of-the-four-08-the-baker-s.subject: Mrs. Smith
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-08-the-baker-s.statement: Mrs. Smith says Mordecai Smith left in the Aurora, which did not have enough coal to reach farther than about Woolwich and back.
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-08-the-baker-s.quote: “Why, bless you, sir, it is in the steam launch that he has gone. That’s what puzzles me; for I know there ain’t more coals in her than would take her to about Woolwich and back.”

1890-the-sign-of-the-four-08-the-baker-s.subject: Mrs. Smith
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-08-the-baker-s.statement: Mrs. Smith says a wooden-legged man had called for her husband more than once and roused him the previous night.
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-08-the-baker-s.quote: “Yes, sir, a brown, monkey-faced chap that’s called more’n once for my old man. It was him that roused him up yesternight, and, what’s more, my man knew he was comin’, for he had steam up in the launch.”

1890-the-sign-of-the-four-08-the-baker-s.subject: Mrs. Smith
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-08-the-baker-s.statement: Mrs. Smith identifies the wooden-legged man by his thick, foggy voice and says he tapped at the window at about three.
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-08-the-baker-s.quote: “His voice, sir. I knew his voice, which is kind o’ thick and foggy. He tapped at the winder,—about three it would be.”

1890-the-sign-of-the-four-08-the-baker-s.subject: Mrs. Smith
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-08-the-baker-s.statement: Mrs. Smith says Mordecai Smith woke Jim and left with the wooden-legged man without saying anything to her.
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-08-the-baker-s.quote: “My old man woke up Jim,—that’s my eldest,—and away they went, without so much as a word to me.”

1890-the-sign-of-the-four-08-the-baker-s.subject: Jim
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-08-the-baker-s.statement: Jim is Mordecai Smith’s eldest child.
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-08-the-baker-s.quote: that’s my eldest

1890-the-sign-of-the-four-08-the-baker-s.subject: Mrs. Smith
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-08-the-baker-s.statement: Mrs. Smith describes the Aurora as black with two red streaks and a black funnel with a white band.
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-08-the-baker-s.quote: “She’s been fresh painted, black with two red streaks.”

1890-the-sign-of-the-four-08-the-baker-s.subject: Mrs. Smith
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-08-the-baker-s.statement: Mrs. Smith says the Aurora’s funnel is black with a white band.
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-08-the-baker-s.quote: “No, sir. Black with a white band.”

1890-the-sign-of-the-four-08-the-baker-s.subject: Holmes
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-08-the-baker-s.statement: Holmes and Watson take a wherry across the river.
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-08-the-baker-s.quote: We shall take it and cross the river.

1890-the-sign-of-the-four-08-the-baker-s.subject: Holmes
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-08-the-baker-s.statement: Holmes says he will not involve the police yet, though he may call Athelney Jones in at the last moment.
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-08-the-baker-s.quote: “No. I shall probably call Athelney Jones in at the last moment.”

1890-the-sign-of-the-four-08-the-baker-s.subject: Holmes
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-08-the-baker-s.statement: Holmes rejects advertising for information because it would warn the fugitives that the chase was close.
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-08-the-baker-s.quote: “Worse and worse! Our men would know that the chase was hot at their heels, and they would be off out of the country.”

1890-the-sign-of-the-four-08-the-baker-s.subject: Holmes
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-08-the-baker-s.statement: Holmes tells Watson to take a hansom home, have breakfast, and sleep for an hour.
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-08-the-baker-s.quote: “Take this hansom, drive home, have some breakfast, and get an hour’s sleep.”

1890-the-sign-of-the-four-08-the-baker-s.subject: Holmes
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-08-the-baker-s.statement: Holmes sends a telegram to Wiggins to summon him and his gang.
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-08-the-baker-s.quote: That wire was to my dirty little lieutenant, Wiggins, and I expect that he and his gang will be with us before we have finished our breakfast.

1890-the-sign-of-the-four-08-the-baker-s.subject: Wiggins
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-08-the-baker-s.statement: Wiggins is Holmes’s lieutenant.
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-08-the-baker-s.quote: my dirty little lieutenant, Wiggins

1890-the-sign-of-the-four-08-the-baker-s.subject: Watson
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-08-the-baker-s.statement: Watson says he is ready to devote his life to recovering the treasure because it rightfully belongs, or partly belongs, to Miss Morstan.
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-08-the-baker-s.quote: That, or part of it, belonged rightfully to Miss Morstan. While there was a chance of recovering it I was ready to devote my life to the one object.

1890-the-sign-of-the-four-08-the-baker-s.subject: Watson
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-08-the-baker-s.statement: Watson says finding the treasure would probably put Mary Morstan forever beyond his reach, but that selfish love would be influenced by this.
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-08-the-baker-s.quote: True, if I found it it would probably put her forever beyond my reach. Yet it would be a petty and selfish love which would be influenced by such a thought as that.

1890-the-sign-of-the-four-08-the-baker-s.subject: newspaper
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-08-the-baker-s.statement: The newspaper reports that Athelney Jones arrested Thaddeus Sholto, Mrs. Bernstone, Lal Rao, and McMurdo.
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-08-the-baker-s.quote: the brother, Thaddeus Sholto, has already been arrested, together with the housekeeper, Mrs. Bernstone, an Indian butler named Lal Rao, and a porter, or gatekeeper, named McMurdo.

1890-the-sign-of-the-four-08-the-baker-s.subject: newspaper
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-08-the-baker-s.statement: The newspaper reports that Bartholomew Sholto was found dead in his room and that a collection of Indian gems was stolen.
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-08-the-baker-s.quote: Mr. Bartholomew Sholto, of Pondicherry Lodge, Upper Norwood, was found dead in his room under circumstances which point to foul play.

1890-the-sign-of-the-four-08-the-baker-s.subject: Holmes
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-08-the-baker-s.statement: Holmes summons the Baker Street Irregulars to help find the Aurora.
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-08-the-baker-s.quote: This is just the case where they might be invaluable.

1890-the-sign-of-the-four-08-the-baker-s.subject: Holmes
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-08-the-baker-s.statement: Holmes instructs Wiggins to have the boys search both banks of the river for the Aurora and report as soon as they find news.
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-08-the-baker-s.quote: I want one boy to be at Mordecai Smith’s landing-stage opposite Millbank to say if the boat comes back. You must divide it out among yourselves, and do both banks thoroughly. Let me know the moment you have news.

1890-the-sign-of-the-four-08-the-baker-s.subject: Holmes
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-08-the-baker-s.statement: Holmes offers a guinea to the boy who finds the Aurora and pays the boys a shilling each in advance.
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-08-the-baker-s.quote: “The old scale of pay, and a guinea to the boy who finds the boat. Here’s a day in advance. Now off you go!” He handed them a shilling each

1890-the-sign-of-the-four-08-the-baker-s.subject: Holmes
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-08-the-baker-s.statement: Holmes concludes that the small-footed companion is from the Andaman Islands.
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-08-the-baker-s.quote: Since, however, we had already determined that Small had come from the Andamans, it is not so very wonderful that this islander should be with him.

1890-the-sign-of-the-four-08-the-baker-s.subject: Holmes
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-08-the-baker-s.statement: Holmes deduces that the small poisoned darts can only be shot from a blow-pipe.
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-08-the-baker-s.quote: These little darts, too, could only be shot in one way. They are from a blow-pipe.

1890-the-sign-of-the-four-08-the-baker-s.subject: Andaman Islanders
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-08-the-baker-s.statement: The cited gazetteer says Andaman Islanders have remarkably small feet and hands and have attacked shipwreck survivors with stone-headed clubs or poisoned arrows.
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-08-the-baker-s.quote: They have always been a terror to shipwrecked crews, braining the survivors with their stone-headed clubs, or shooting them with their poisoned arrows.

1890-the-sign-of-the-four-08-the-baker-s.subject: Holmes
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-08-the-baker-s.statement: Holmes plays a low, dreamy melody on his violin to help Watson fall asleep.
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-08-the-baker-s.quote: he began to play some low, dreamy, melodious air,—his own, no doubt, for he had a remarkable gift for improvisation.

1890-the-sign-of-the-four-09-a-break-in-.subject: Holmes
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-09-a-break-in-.statement: Holmes is named Sherlock Holmes.
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-09-a-break-in-.quote: Sherlock Holmes still sat exactly as I had left him

1890-the-sign-of-the-four-09-a-break-in-.subject: Holmes
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-09-a-break-in-.statement: Holmes was at Baker Street while Watson woke late in the afternoon.
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-09-a-break-in-.quote: Sherlock Holmes still sat exactly as I had left him

1890-the-sign-of-the-four-09-a-break-in-.subject: Watson
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-09-a-break-in-.statement: Watson said he would go to Camberwell to visit Mrs. Cecil Forrester and Miss Morstan.
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-09-a-break-in-.quote: Then I shall run over to Camberwell and call upon Mrs. Cecil Forrester.

1890-the-sign-of-the-four-09-a-break-in-.subject: Watson
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-09-a-break-in-.statement: Watson said he expected to return in an hour or two.
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-09-a-break-in-.quote: I shall be back in an hour or two,

1890-the-sign-of-the-four-09-a-break-in-.subject: Watson
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-09-a-break-in-.statement: Watson took Toby with him when he left.
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-09-a-break-in-.quote: I took our mongrel accordingly,

1890-the-sign-of-the-four-09-a-break-in-.subject: Watson
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-09-a-break-in-.statement: Watson left Toby and a half-sovereign at the old naturalist's in Pinchin Lane.
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-09-a-break-in-.quote: I took our mongrel accordingly, and left him, together with a half-sovereign, at the old naturalist’s in Pinchin Lane.

1890-the-sign-of-the-four-09-a-break-in-.subject: Watson
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-09-a-break-in-.statement: Watson was at Camberwell when he visited Miss Morstan and Mrs. Forrester.
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-09-a-break-in-.quote: At Camberwell I found Miss Morstan a little weary after her night’s adventures,

1890-the-sign-of-the-four-09-a-break-in-.subject: Watson
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-09-a-break-in-.statement: Watson told Miss Morstan and Mrs. Forrester what they had done, withholding the more dreadful parts of the tragedy.
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-09-a-break-in-.quote: I told them all that we had done, suppressing, however, the more dreadful parts of the tragedy.

1890-the-sign-of-the-four-09-a-break-in-.subject: Watson
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-09-a-break-in-.statement: Watson did not tell Miss Morstan and Mrs. Forrester the exact manner and method of Mr. Sholto's death.
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-09-a-break-in-.quote: Thus, although I spoke of Mr. Sholto’s death, I said nothing of the exact manner and method of it.

1890-the-sign-of-the-four-09-a-break-in-.subject: Miss Morstan
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-09-a-break-in-.statement: Miss Morstan said she was anxious for Thaddeus Sholto and considered it their duty to clear him of the charge.
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-09-a-break-in-.quote: It is for Mr. Thaddeus Sholto that I am anxious,” she said.

1890-the-sign-of-the-four-09-a-break-in-.subject: Mary Morstan
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-09-a-break-in-.statement: Mary Morstan and Mrs. Cecil Forrester were together at Camberwell.
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-09-a-break-in-.quote: At Camberwell I found Miss Morstan a little weary after her night’s adventures, but very eager to hear the news. Mrs. Forrester, too, was full of curiosity.

1890-the-sign-of-the-four-09-a-break-in-.subject: Holmes
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-09-a-break-in-.statement: Holmes was at Baker Street when Watson returned from Camberwell in the evening.
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-09-a-break-in-.quote: My companion’s book and pipe lay by his chair, but he had disappeared.

1890-the-sign-of-the-four-09-a-break-in-.subject: Holmes
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-09-a-break-in-.statement: Holmes walked repeatedly and muttered to himself after Watson left.
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-09-a-break-in-.quote: After you was gone he walked and he walked, up and down, and up and down, until I was weary of the sound of his footstep.

1890-the-sign-of-the-four-09-a-break-in-.subject: Holmes
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-09-a-break-in-.statement: Holmes turned on Mrs. Hudson when she mentioned cooling medicine.
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-09-a-break-in-.quote: I ventured to say something to him about cooling medicine, but he turned on me, sir, with such a look that I don’t know how ever I got out of the room.

1890-the-sign-of-the-four-09-a-break-in-.subject: Holmes
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-09-a-break-in-.statement: Holmes said he could not sleep because the problem was consuming him.
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-09-a-break-in-.quote: “No, I could not sleep,” he answered.

1890-the-sign-of-the-four-09-a-break-in-.subject: Holmes
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-09-a-break-in-.statement: Holmes said a search party would search upriver as far as Richmond.
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-09-a-break-in-.quote: there is a search-party who will work up as far as Richmond.

1890-the-sign-of-the-four-09-a-break-in-.subject: Watson
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-09-a-break-in-.statement: Watson walked to Camberwell in the evening to report their lack of success to the ladies.
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-09-a-break-in-.quote: I walked over to Camberwell in the evening to report our ill success to the ladies,

1890-the-sign-of-the-four-09-a-break-in-.subject: Holmes
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-09-a-break-in-.statement: Holmes spent the evening conducting a chemical analysis.
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-09-a-break-in-.quote: busied himself all evening in an abstruse chemical analysis

1890-the-sign-of-the-four-09-a-break-in-.subject: Holmes
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-09-a-break-in-.statement: Holmes was in Watson's room at early dawn before setting out down the river.
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-09-a-break-in-.quote: In the early dawn I woke with a start, and was surprised to find him standing by my bedside,

1890-the-sign-of-the-four-09-a-break-in-.subject: Holmes
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-09-a-break-in-.statement: Holmes set out disguised as an old sailor.
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-09-a-break-in-.quote: clad in a rude sailor dress with a pea-jacket, and a coarse red scarf round his neck.

1890-the-sign-of-the-four-09-a-break-in-.subject: Holmes
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-09-a-break-in-.statement: Holmes told Watson he was going down the river.
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-09-a-break-in-.quote: “I am off down the river, Watson,” said he.

1890-the-sign-of-the-four-09-a-break-in-.subject: Holmes
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-09-a-break-in-.statement: Holmes asked Watson to remain as his representative while he was away.
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-09-a-break-in-.quote: No; you can be much more useful if you will remain here as my representative.

1890-the-sign-of-the-four-09-a-break-in-.subject: Holmes
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-09-a-break-in-.statement: Holmes instructed Watson to open incoming notes and telegrams and act on his own judgment if news arrived.
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-09-a-break-in-.quote: I want you to open all notes and telegrams, and to act on your own judgment if any news should come.

1890-the-sign-of-the-four-09-a-break-in-.subject: Holmes
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-09-a-break-in-.statement: Holmes placed an advertisement in the Standard seeking information about Mordecai Smith and the Aurora.
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-09-a-break-in-.quote: This was clearly Holmes’s doing.

1890-the-sign-of-the-four-09-a-break-in-.subject: Aurora
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-09-a-break-in-.value: black with two red stripes; black funnel with a white band
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-09-a-break-in-.statement: The Aurora is described as black with two red stripes and a black funnel with a white band.
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-09-a-break-in-.quote: the steam launch _Aurora_, black with two red stripes, funnel black with a white band,

1890-the-sign-of-the-four-09-a-break-in-.subject: Holmes
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-09-a-break-in-.statement: Holmes's telegram was dated from Poplar at noon.
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-09-a-break-in-.quote: It was dated from Poplar at twelve o’clock.

1890-the-sign-of-the-four-09-a-break-in-.subject: Holmes
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-09-a-break-in-.statement: Holmes telegraphed Jones to go to Baker Street and wait if Holmes had not returned.
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-09-a-break-in-.quote: “Go to Baker Street at once,” it said. “If I have not returned, wait for me.

1890-the-sign-of-the-four-09-a-break-in-.subject: Holmes
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-09-a-break-in-.statement: Holmes's telegram invited Jones to join them that night if he wanted to be present at the finish.
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-09-a-break-in-.quote: You can come with us to-night if you want to be in at the finish.”

1890-the-sign-of-the-four-09-a-break-in-.subject: Athelney Jones
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-09-a-break-in-.statement: Athelney Jones arrived at Baker Street at three o'clock in the afternoon.
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-09-a-break-in-.quote: At three o’clock in the afternoon there was a loud peal at the bell, an authoritative voice in the hall, and, to my surprise, no less a person than Mr. Athelney Jones was shown up to me.

1890-the-sign-of-the-four-09-a-break-in-.subject: Athelney Jones
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-09-a-break-in-.statement: Jones said he had been obliged to reconsider his theory about the Norwood case.
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-09-a-break-in-.quote: Well, I have been obliged to reconsider it.

1890-the-sign-of-the-four-09-a-break-in-.subject: Thaddeus Sholto
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-09-a-break-in-.value: from the time he left his brother’s room, he was always in someone’s sight
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-09-a-break-in-.statement: Thaddeus Sholto's alibi was that he was continually in someone's sight after leaving his brother's room.
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-09-a-break-in-.quote: From the time that he left his brother’s room he was never out of sight of some one or other.

1890-the-sign-of-the-four-09-a-break-in-.subject: Thaddeus Sholto
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-09-a-break-in-.statement: Thaddeus Sholto was released the previous evening.
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-09-a-break-in-.quote: He and the housekeeper, Mrs. Bernstone, were both released yesterday evening.

1890-the-sign-of-the-four-09-a-break-in-.subject: Holmes
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-09-a-break-in-.statement: Holmes arrived while Watson and Jones were talking at Baker Street.
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-09-a-break-in-.quote: There was Holmes sitting close to us with an air of quiet amusement.

1890-the-sign-of-the-four-09-a-break-in-.subject: Holmes
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-09-a-break-in-.statement: Holmes revealed that the old sailor was himself in disguise.
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-09-a-break-in-.quote: “Here is the old man,” said he, holding out a heap of white hair.

1890-the-sign-of-the-four-09-a-break-in-.subject: Holmes
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-09-a-break-in-.value: many criminals have begun to recognize him
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-09-a-break-in-.statement: Holmes said he used a simple disguise because many criminals had begun to recognize him.
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-09-a-break-in-.quote: a good many of the criminal classes begin to know me,—especially since our friend here took to publishing some of my cases: so I can only go on the war-path under some simple disguise like this.

1890-the-sign-of-the-four-09-a-break-in-.subject: Holmes
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-09-a-break-in-.statement: Holmes required Jones to act under his orders while allowing Jones to receive the official credit.
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-09-a-break-in-.quote: But you must put yourself under my orders. You are welcome to all the official credit, but you must act on the line that I point out.

1890-the-sign-of-the-four-09-a-break-in-.subject: Holmes
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-09-a-break-in-.statement: Holmes requested a fast police steam launch at Westminster Stairs at seven o'clock.
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-09-a-break-in-.quote: in the first place I shall want a fast police-boat—a steam launch—to be at the Westminster Stairs at seven o’clock.

1890-the-sign-of-the-four-09-a-break-in-.subject: Holmes
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-09-a-break-in-.statement: Holmes requested two sturdy men in case of resistance.
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-09-a-break-in-.quote: Then I shall want two stanch men, in case of resistance.

1890-the-sign-of-the-four-09-a-break-in-.subject: Holmes
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-09-a-break-in-.statement: Holmes said they would obtain the treasure when they secured the men.
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-09-a-break-in-.quote: When we secure the men we shall get the treasure.

1890-the-sign-of-the-four-09-a-break-in-.subject: Holmes
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-09-a-break-in-.statement: Holmes proposed that Watson take the box to Miss Morstan, to whom half the treasure rightfully belonged, and let her open it first.
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-09-a-break-in-.quote: I think that it would be a pleasure to my friend here to take the box round to the young lady to whom half of it rightfully belongs.

1890-the-sign-of-the-four-09-a-break-in-.subject: treasure
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-09-a-break-in-.statement: Jones said the treasure must be handed to the authorities after the young lady opened the box, pending the official investigation.
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-09-a-break-in-.quote: The treasure must afterwards be handed over to the authorities until after the official investigation.

1890-the-sign-of-the-four-09-a-break-in-.subject: Holmes
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-09-a-break-in-.statement: Holmes requested an unofficial interview with Jonathan Small if he was caught and efficiently guarded.
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-09-a-break-in-.quote: I should much like to have a few details about this matter from the lips of Jonathan Small himself.

1890-the-sign-of-the-four-10-the-end-of-.subject: Holmes
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-10-the-end-of-.statement: Holmes tells Watson to take his service revolver on the expedition.
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-10-the-end-of-.quote: “You had best take it, then. It is well to be prepared.

1890-the-sign-of-the-four-10-the-end-of-.subject: Holmes
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-10-the-end-of-.statement: Holmes orders the green lamp removed from the launch so it will not be marked as a police-boat.
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-10-the-end-of-.quote: “Then take it off.”

1890-the-sign-of-the-four-10-the-end-of-.subject: Holmes
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-10-the-end-of-.statement: Holmes directs the launch to the Tower and tells them to stop opposite Jacobson’s Yard.
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-10-the-end-of-.quote: “To the Tower. Tell them to stop opposite Jacobson’s Yard.”

1890-the-sign-of-the-four-10-the-end-of-.subject: Holmes
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-10-the-end-of-.statement: Holmes deduces that Small has hidden the Aurora at a boat-yard after arranging a trivial alteration to it.
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-10-the-end-of-.quote: I might hand the launch over to some boat-builder or repairer, with directions to make a trifling change in her.

1890-the-sign-of-the-four-10-the-end-of-.subject: Holmes
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-10-the-end-of-.statement: Holmes discovers that the Aurora was delivered to Jacobson’s Yard two days earlier by a wooden-legged man.
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-10-the-end-of-.quote: At the sixteenth—Jacobson’s—I learned that the _Aurora_ had been handed over to them two days ago by a wooden-legged man, with some trivial directions as to her rudder.

1890-the-sign-of-the-four-10-the-end-of-.subject: Holmes
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-10-the-end-of-.statement: Holmes stations one of his boys to watch the Aurora and signal when it starts.
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-10-the-end-of-.quote: I stationed him as a sentry over the launch.

1890-the-sign-of-the-four-10-the-end-of-.subject: Holmes
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-10-the-end-of-.statement: Holmes refuses Jones’s suggestion to wait downstream because he cannot be certain the fugitives will go that way.
