1890-the-sign-of-the-four-10-the-end-of-.quote: “We have no right to take anything for granted,” Holmes answered.

1890-the-sign-of-the-four-10-the-end-of-.subject: Holmes
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-10-the-end-of-.statement: Holmes orders the crew to pursue the Aurora at full speed.
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-10-the-end-of-.quote: “Full speed ahead, engineer. Make after that launch with the yellow light.

1890-the-sign-of-the-four-10-the-end-of-.subject: Holmes
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-10-the-end-of-.statement: Holmes tells the others to fire if the man on the Aurora raises his hand.
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-10-the-end-of-.quote: “Fire if he raises his hand,” said Holmes, quietly.

1890-the-sign-of-the-four-10-the-end-of-.subject: Tonga
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-10-the-end-of-.statement: Tonga takes a short wooden blowpipe from beneath his covering and puts it to his lips.
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-10-the-end-of-.quote: Even as we looked he plucked out from under his covering a short, round piece of wood, like a school-ruler, and clapped it to his lips.

1890-the-sign-of-the-four-10-the-end-of-.subject: Holmes
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-10-the-end-of-.statement: Holmes fires his revolver at Tonga as Tonga raises the blowpipe.
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-10-the-end-of-.quote: Our pistols rang out together.

1890-the-sign-of-the-four-10-the-end-of-.subject: Watson
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-10-the-end-of-.statement: Watson fires his revolver at Tonga as Tonga raises the blowpipe.
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-10-the-end-of-.quote: Our pistols rang out together.

1890-the-sign-of-the-four-10-the-end-of-.subject: Tonga
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-10-the-end-of-.statement: Tonga is struck by the gunfire and falls into the Thames.
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-10-the-end-of-.quote: He whirled round, threw up his arms, and with a kind of choking cough fell sideways into the stream.

1890-the-sign-of-the-four-10-the-end-of-.subject: Small
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-10-the-end-of-.statement: After Tonga falls, Small throws himself onto the rudder and steers the Aurora toward the southern bank.
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-10-the-end-of-.quote: At the same moment the wooden-legged man threw himself upon the rudder and put it hard down, so that his boat made straight in for the southern bank, while we shot past her stern, only clearing her by a few feet.

1890-the-sign-of-the-four-10-the-end-of-.subject: Small
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-10-the-end-of-.statement: Small has a wooden stump in place of his right leg below the thigh.
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-10-the-end-of-.quote: I could see that from the thigh downwards there was but a wooden stump upon the right side.

1890-the-sign-of-the-four-10-the-end-of-.subject: Aurora
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-10-the-end-of-.statement: The Aurora runs onto a mud-bank at the southern bank.
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-10-the-end-of-.quote: The launch with a dull thud ran up upon the mud-bank, with her bow in the air and her stern flush with the water.

1890-the-sign-of-the-four-10-the-end-of-.subject: Small
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-10-the-end-of-.statement: Small becomes stuck in the sodden mud and cannot move forward or backward.
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-10-the-end-of-.quote: Not one step could he possibly take either forwards or backwards.

1890-the-sign-of-the-four-10-the-end-of-.subject: Holmes
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-10-the-end-of-.statement: Holmes and the others haul Small out of the mud by throwing a rope over his shoulders.
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-10-the-end-of-.quote: When we brought our launch alongside he was so firmly anchored that it was only by throwing the end of a rope over his shoulders that we were able to haul him out, and to drag him, like some evil fish, over our side.

1890-the-sign-of-the-four-10-the-end-of-.subject: Mordecai Smith
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-10-the-end-of-.statement: Mordecai Smith and his son come aboard the police launch when commanded.
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-10-the-end-of-.quote: The two Smiths, father and son, sat sullenly in their launch, but came aboard meekly enough when commanded.

1890-the-sign-of-the-four-10-the-end-of-.subject: Holmes
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-10-the-end-of-.statement: Holmes and the others haul the Aurora off the bank and secure it to their stern.
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-10-the-end-of-.quote: The _Aurora_ herself we hauled off and made fast to our stern.

1890-the-sign-of-the-four-10-the-end-of-.subject: Holmes
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-10-the-end-of-.statement: Holmes and the others find a solid iron chest of Indian workmanship aboard the Aurora and transfer it to their cabin.
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-10-the-end-of-.quote: There was no key, but it was of considerable weight, so we transferred it carefully to our own little cabin.

1890-the-sign-of-the-four-10-the-end-of-.subject: iron chest
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-10-the-end-of-.statement: The iron chest is identified as the chest that contained the Sholtos’ treasure.
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-10-the-end-of-.quote: This, there could be no question, was the same that had contained the ill-omened treasure of the Sholtos.

1890-the-sign-of-the-four-10-the-end-of-.subject: Tonga
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-10-the-end-of-.statement: Tonga is believed to have drowned in the Thames after falling from the Aurora.
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-10-the-end-of-.quote: Somewhere in the dark ooze at the bottom of the Thames lie the bones of that strange visitor to our shores.

1890-the-sign-of-the-four-10-the-end-of-.subject: Holmes
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-10-the-end-of-.statement: Holmes finds one of the known murderous darts stuck in the wooden hatchway where the pursuers had been standing.
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-10-the-end-of-.quote: There, sure enough, just behind where we had been standing, stuck one of those murderous darts which we knew so well.

1890-the-sign-of-the-four-11-the-great-a.subject: Small
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-11-the-great-a.statement: Small is a captive.
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-11-the-great-a.quote: Our captive sat in the cabin opposite to the iron box which he had done so much and waited so long to gain.

1890-the-sign-of-the-four-11-the-great-a.subject: Small
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-11-the-great-a.statement: Small is fifty or thereabouts.
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-11-the-great-a.quote: His age may have been fifty or thereabouts, for his black, curly hair was thickly shot with grey.

1890-the-sign-of-the-four-11-the-great-a.subject: Small
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-11-the-great-a.statement: Small says he never raised a hand against Mr. Sholto.
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-11-the-great-a.quote: I give you my word on the book that I never raised hand against Mr. Sholto.

1890-the-sign-of-the-four-11-the-great-a.subject: Small
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-11-the-great-a.statement: Small says he beat Tonga with the slack end of the rope for shooting Mr. Sholto.
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-11-the-great-a.quote: I welted the little devil with the slack end of the rope for it, but it was done, and I could not undo it again.

1890-the-sign-of-the-four-11-the-great-a.subject: Small
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-11-the-great-a.statement: Small chose the Aurora because he had heard she was a fast launch.
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-11-the-great-a.quote: I chose his launch because I heard that she was a flier.

1890-the-sign-of-the-four-11-the-great-a.subject: Small
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-11-the-great-a.statement: Small says he and his companions paid Smith well and told him nothing.
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-11-the-great-a.quote: We told him nothing, but we paid him well, and he was to get something handsome if we reached our vessel, the _Esmeralda_, at Gravesend, outward bound for the Brazils.

1890-the-sign-of-the-four-11-the-great-a.subject: Small
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-11-the-great-a.statement: Small says Smith was promised a handsome payment if they reached the Esmeralda at Gravesend.
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-11-the-great-a.quote: We told him nothing, but we paid him well, and he was to get something handsome if we reached our vessel, the _Esmeralda_, at Gravesend, outward bound for the Brazils.

1890-the-sign-of-the-four-11-the-great-a.subject: Small
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-11-the-great-a.statement: Small threw the box key into the river.
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-11-the-great-a.quote: At the bottom of the river,” said Small, shortly.

1890-the-sign-of-the-four-11-the-great-a.subject: Small
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-11-the-great-a.statement: Small claimed a fair claim to nearly half a million pounds of the Agra treasure.
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-11-the-great-a.quote: that I who have a fair claim to nigh upon half a million of money should spend the first half of my life building a breakwater in the Andamans, and am like to spend the other half digging drains at Dartmoor.

1890-the-sign-of-the-four-11-the-great-a.subject: Agra treasure
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-11-the-great-a.statement: Small says the Agra treasure brought a curse upon every man who owned it.
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-11-the-great-a.quote: the Agra treasure, which never brought anything but a curse yet upon the man who owned it.

1890-the-sign-of-the-four-11-the-great-a.subject: Jones
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-11-the-great-a.statement: Jones had Small under his charge.
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-11-the-great-a.quote: You are under the charge of Mr. Athelney Jones, of Scotland Yard.

1890-the-sign-of-the-four-11-the-great-a.subject: Jones
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-11-the-great-a.statement: Jones planned to bring Small to Holmes's rooms.
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-11-the-great-a.quote: He is going to bring you up to my rooms, and I shall ask you for a true account of the matter.

1890-the-sign-of-the-four-11-the-great-a.subject: Holmes
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-11-the-great-a.statement: Holmes planned to ask Small for a true account of the matter.
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-11-the-great-a.quote: He is going to bring you up to my rooms, and I shall ask you for a true account of the matter.

1890-the-sign-of-the-four-11-the-great-a.subject: Holmes
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-11-the-great-a.statement: Holmes believed the poison killed Mr. Sholto before Small reached the room.
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-11-the-great-a.quote: I think I can prove that the poison acts so quickly that the man was dead before ever you reached the room.

1890-the-sign-of-the-four-11-the-great-a.subject: Watson
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-11-the-great-a.statement: Watson brought the treasure box to Miss Morstan.
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-11-the-great-a.quote: I have brought something better than news,” said I, putting down the box upon the table and speaking jovially and boisterously, though my heart was heavy within me.

1890-the-sign-of-the-four-11-the-great-a.subject: Watson
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-11-the-great-a.statement: Watson told Mary that half the treasure was hers and half was Thaddeus Sholto's.
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-11-the-great-a.quote: Half of it is yours and half is Thaddeus Sholto’s.

1890-the-sign-of-the-four-11-the-great-a.subject: Watson
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-11-the-great-a.statement: Watson forced open the treasure box with a poker and found it empty.
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-11-the-great-a.quote: The box was empty!

1890-the-sign-of-the-four-11-the-great-a.subject: Mary
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-11-the-great-a.statement: Mary found that the treasure was lost.
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-11-the-great-a.quote: “The treasure is lost,” said Miss Morstan, calmly.

1890-the-sign-of-the-four-11-the-great-a.subject: Watson
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-11-the-great-a.statement: Watson told Mary that he loved her.
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-11-the-great-a.quote: Because I love you, Mary, as truly as ever a man loved a woman.

1890-the-sign-of-the-four-11-the-great-a.subject: Mary
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-11-the-great-a.statement: Mary reciprocated Watson's love.
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-11-the-great-a.quote: “Then I say, ‘Thank God,’ too,” she whispered, as I drew her to my side.

1890-the-sign-of-the-four-11-the-great-a.subject: Mary
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-11-the-great-a.statement: Mary did not withdraw her hand when Watson took it.
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-11-the-great-a.quote: She did not withdraw it.

1890-the-sign-of-the-four-11-the-great-a.subject: Watson
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-11-the-great-a.statement: Watson recounted the events since he had last seen Mary, including the chase down the Thames.
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-11-the-great-a.quote: I narrated briefly what had occurred since I had seen her last,—Holmes’s new method of search, the discovery of the _Aurora_, the appearance of Athelney Jones, our expedition in the evening, and the wild chase down the Thames.

1890-the-sign-of-the-four-11-the-great-a.subject: Mary
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-11-the-great-a.statement: Mary became so pale when Watson described the dart that he feared she might faint.
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-11-the-great-a.quote: When I spoke of the dart which had so narrowly missed us, she turned so white that I feared that she was about to faint.

1890-the-sign-of-the-four-11-the-great-a.subject: Mary
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-11-the-great-a.statement: Mary said she was all right again after the shock.
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-11-the-great-a.quote: It is nothing,” she said, as I hastened to pour her out some water. “I am all right again.

1890-the-sign-of-the-four-11-the-great-a.subject: Mary
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-11-the-great-a.statement: Mary said she was shocked that she had placed her friends in peril.
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-11-the-great-a.quote: It was a shock to me to hear that I had placed my friends in such horrible peril.

1890-the-sign-of-the-four-11-the-great-a.subject: Jones
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-11-the-great-a.statement: Jones arranged for Watson and the treasure box to be landed at Vauxhall Bridge.
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-11-the-great-a.quote: We will be at Vauxhall Bridge presently,” said Jones, “and shall land you, Dr. Watson, with the treasure-box.

1890-the-sign-of-the-four-11-the-great-a.subject: Jones
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-11-the-great-a.statement: Jones sent an inspector with Watson because Watson carried valuable property.
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-11-the-great-a.quote: I must, however, as a matter of duty, send an inspector with you, since you have so valuable a charge.

1890-the-sign-of-the-four-11-the-great-a.subject: Watson
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-11-the-great-a.statement: Watson went by cab to Mrs. Cecil Forrester's with the treasure box and an inspector.
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-11-the-great-a.quote: A quarter of an hour’s drive brought us to Mrs. Cecil Forrester’s.

1890-the-sign-of-the-four-11-the-great-a.subject: Mary
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-11-the-great-a.statement: Mary was in the drawing-room at Mrs. Cecil Forrester's when Watson arrived.
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-11-the-great-a.quote: Miss Morstan, however, was in the drawing-room: so to the drawing-room I went, box in hand, leaving the obliging inspector in the cab.

1890-the-sign-of-the-four-11-the-great-a.subject: Agra treasure
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-11-the-great-a.statement: The iron box was empty when Watson opened it.
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-11-the-great-a.quote: The box was empty!

1890-the-sign-of-the-four-11-the-great-a.subject: Agra treasure
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-11-the-great-a.value: a couple of hundred thousand pounds each for Mary and Thaddeus Sholto
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-11-the-great-a.statement: Watson expected Mary and Thaddeus Sholto each to receive a couple of hundred thousand pounds from the treasure.
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-11-the-great-a.quote: You will have a couple of hundred thousand each.

1890-the-sign-of-the-four-12-the-strange.subject: Jonathan Small
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-12-the-strange.statement: Jonathan Small was born near Pershore in Worcestershire.
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-12-the-strange.quote: I am a Worcestershire man myself,—born near Pershore.

1890-the-sign-of-the-four-12-the-strange.subject: Jonathan Small
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-12-the-strange.value: right leg amputated just above the knee
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-12-the-strange.statement: A crocodile took Small’s right leg off just above the knee.
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-12-the-strange.quote: A crocodile took me, just as I was half-way across, and nipped off my right leg as clean as a surgeon could have done it, just above the knee.

1890-the-sign-of-the-four-12-the-strange.subject: Jonathan Small
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-12-the-strange.statement: Small joined the 3rd Buffs and served as a soldier in India.
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-12-the-strange.quote: I got into a mess over a girl, and could only get out of it again by taking the Queen’s shilling and joining the 3rd Buffs, which was just starting for India.

1890-the-sign-of-the-four-12-the-strange.subject: Jonathan Small
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-12-the-strange.statement: Small was a convict in the Andaman settlement.
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-12-the-strange.quote: At last it seemed to me to have come. I was changed from Agra to Madras, and from there to Blair Island in the Andamans.

1890-the-sign-of-the-four-12-the-strange.subject: Tonga
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-12-the-strange.statement: Tonga was an Andaman Islander.
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-12-the-strange.quote: One day when Dr. Somerton was down with a fever a little Andaman Islander was picked up by a convict-gang in the woods.

1890-the-sign-of-the-four-12-the-strange.subject: Tonga
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-12-the-strange.statement: Tonga was a fine boatman.
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-12-the-strange.quote: Tonga—for that was his name—was a fine boatman, and owned a big, roomy canoe of his own.

1890-the-sign-of-the-four-12-the-strange.subject: Sherlock Holmes
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-12-the-strange.statement: Sherlock Holmes is a detective.
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-12-the-strange.quote: Sherlock Holmes and Jones sat with their hands upon their knees, deeply interested in the story, but with the same disgust written upon their faces.

1890-the-sign-of-the-four-12-the-strange.subject: Jonathan Small
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-12-the-strange.statement: Small and Tonga were faithful companions.
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-12-the-strange.quote: No man ever had a more faithful mate.

1890-the-sign-of-the-four-12-the-strange.subject: Mahomet Singh
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-12-the-strange.statement: Mahomet Singh, Abdullah Khan, Dost Akbar, and Small swore to act together and share the treasure.
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-12-the-strange.quote: We solemnly renewed our oath to stand by each other and be true to our secret.

1890-the-sign-of-the-four-12-the-strange.subject: Abdullah Khan
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-12-the-strange.statement: Abdullah Khan, Mahomet Singh, Dost Akbar, and Small swore to act together and share the treasure.
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-12-the-strange.quote: We solemnly renewed our oath to stand by each other and be true to our secret.

1890-the-sign-of-the-four-12-the-strange.subject: Dost Akbar
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-12-the-strange.statement: Dost Akbar, Mahomet Singh, Abdullah Khan, and Small swore to act together and share the treasure.
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-12-the-strange.quote: We solemnly renewed our oath to stand by each other and be true to our secret.

1890-the-sign-of-the-four-12-the-strange.subject: Jonathan Small
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-12-the-strange.statement: Small regarded Tonga as a faithful friend and mate.
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-12-the-strange.quote: No man ever had a more faithful mate.

1890-the-sign-of-the-four-12-the-strange.subject: Jonathan Small
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-12-the-strange.statement: Mary Morstan has accepted Watson as a prospective husband.
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-12-the-strange.quote: Miss Morstan has done me the honour to accept me as a husband in prospective.

1890-the-sign-of-the-four-12-the-strange.subject: Jonathan Small
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-12-the-strange.statement: Small says he hid the treasure in a safe place when the launch was about to catch them.
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-12-the-strange.quote: When I saw that your launch must catch us, I put the loot away in a safe place.

1890-the-sign-of-the-four-12-the-strange.subject: Jonathan Small
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-12-the-strange.statement: Small claims that the Agra treasure belongs to the four conspirators and himself.
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-12-the-strange.quote: I tell you that no living man has any right to it, unless it is three men who are in the Andaman convict-barracks and myself.

1890-the-sign-of-the-four-12-the-strange.subject: Jonathan Small
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-12-the-strange.statement: Small tells Holmes and Jones his account of the conspiracy, murder, and stolen treasure.
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-12-the-strange.quote: If you want to hear my story I have no wish to hold it back.

1890-the-sign-of-the-four-12-the-strange.subject: Jonathan Small
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-12-the-strange.statement: Small joined the 3rd Buffs to escape trouble involving a girl.
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-12-the-strange.quote: I got into a mess over a girl, and could only get out of it again by taking the Queen’s shilling and joining the 3rd Buffs, which was just starting for India.

1890-the-sign-of-the-four-12-the-strange.subject: Jonathan Small
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-12-the-strange.statement: A crocodile bit off Small’s right leg while he was swimming across the Ganges.
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-12-the-strange.quote: A crocodile took me, just as I was half-way across, and nipped off my right leg as clean as a surgeon could have done it, just above the knee.

1890-the-sign-of-the-four-12-the-strange.subject: John Holder
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-12-the-strange.statement: John Holder rescued Small from drowning after the crocodile attack.
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-12-the-strange.quote: I fainted, and should have drowned if Holder had not caught hold of me and paddled for the bank.

1890-the-sign-of-the-four-12-the-strange.subject: Jonathan Small
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-12-the-strange.statement: Small fled to Agra after rebels attacked Abel White’s plantation.
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-12-the-strange.quote: so I broke away across the paddy-fields, and found myself late at night safe within the walls at Agra.

1890-the-sign-of-the-four-12-the-strange.subject: Jonathan Small
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-12-the-strange.statement: Small agreed to help Abdullah Khan and the others kill Achmet in exchange for a share of the treasure.
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-12-the-strange.quote: ‘I am with you heart and soul,’ said I.

1890-the-sign-of-the-four-12-the-strange.subject: Jonathan Small
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-12-the-strange.statement: Small tripped Achmet with his firelock as Achmet ran past him.
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-12-the-strange.quote: I cast my firelock between his legs as he raced past, and he rolled twice over like a shot rabbit.

1890-the-sign-of-the-four-12-the-strange.subject: Abdullah Khan
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-12-the-strange.statement: Abdullah Khan caught Achmet and stabbed him twice in the side.
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-12-the-strange.quote: Ere he could stagger to his feet the Sikh was upon him, and buried his knife twice in his side.

1890-the-sign-of-the-four-12-the-strange.subject: Jonathan Small
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-12-the-strange.statement: Small and the Sikhs concealed Achmet’s body beneath loose bricks in a sunken part of the fort.
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-12-the-strange.quote: The earth floor had sunk in at one place, making a natural grave, so we left Achmet the merchant there, having first covered him over with loose bricks.

1890-the-sign-of-the-four-12-the-strange.subject: Sign of the Four
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-12-the-strange.statement: The four conspirators concealed the treasure in a hollow beneath bricks in a wall of the old hall.
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-12-the-strange.quote: We carried the box, therefore, into the same hall where we had buried the body, and there, under certain bricks in the best-preserved wall, we made a hollow and put our treasure.

1890-the-sign-of-the-four-12-the-strange.subject: Jonathan Small
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-12-the-strange.statement: Small made four plans showing where the treasure was hidden.
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-12-the-strange.quote: next day I drew four plans, one for each of us, and put the sign of the four of us at the bottom

1890-the-sign-of-the-four-12-the-strange.subject: Jonathan Small
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-12-the-strange.statement: Small and the three Sikhs were arrested and tried for Achmet’s murder.
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-12-the-strange.quote: we were all four seized and brought to trial on a charge of murder

1890-the-sign-of-the-four-12-the-strange.subject: Jonathan Small
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-12-the-strange.statement: Small’s death sentence was commuted to penal servitude for life.
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-12-the-strange.quote: I was condemned to death, though my sentence was afterwards commuted into the same as the others.

1890-the-sign-of-the-four-12-the-strange.subject: Jonathan Small
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-12-the-strange.statement: Small escaped from the Andaman settlement with Tonga by canoe.
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-12-the-strange.quote: I made for the boat, and in an hour we were well out at sea.

1890-the-sign-of-the-four-12-the-strange.subject: Jonathan Small
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-12-the-strange.statement: Small killed a convict guard by striking him with his wooden leg.
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-12-the-strange.quote: I struck him full, and knocked the whole front of his skull in.

1890-the-sign-of-the-four-12-the-strange.subject: Tonga
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-12-the-strange.statement: Tonga brought his canoe and provisions to help Small escape.
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-12-the-strange.quote: At the night named he had his boat at the wharf.

1890-the-sign-of-the-four-12-the-strange.subject: Jonathan Small
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-12-the-strange.statement: Small discovered that Major Sholto still possessed the jewels.
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-12-the-strange.quote: I soon found that he still had the jewels.

1890-the-sign-of-the-four-12-the-strange.subject: Major Sholto
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-12-the-strange.statement: Major Sholto took the treasure and failed to fulfill his agreement with Small and the others.
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-12-the-strange.quote: The scoundrel had stolen it all, without carrying out one of the conditions on which we had sold him the secret.

1890-the-sign-of-the-four-12-the-strange.subject: Jonathan Small
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-12-the-strange.statement: After Sholto stole the treasure, Small devoted himself to seeking revenge on him.
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-12-the-strange.quote: From that day I lived only for vengeance.

1890-the-sign-of-the-four-12-the-strange.subject: Jonathan Small
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-12-the-strange.statement: Small pinned the sign of the four to Major Sholto’s body after searching Sholto’s papers.
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-12-the-strange.quote: I scrawled down the sign of the four of us, as it had been on the chart, and I pinned it on his bosom.

1890-the-sign-of-the-four-12-the-strange.subject: Tonga
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-12-the-strange.statement: Tonga killed Bartholomew Sholto in the chemical laboratory.
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-12-the-strange.quote: Tonga thought he had done something very clever in killing him

1890-the-sign-of-the-four-12-the-strange.subject: Jonathan Small
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-12-the-strange.statement: Small took the treasure box from Bartholomew Sholto’s laboratory.
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-12-the-strange.quote: I took the treasure-box and let it down

1890-the-sign-of-the-four-12-the-strange.subject: Jonathan Small
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-12-the-strange.statement: Small left the sign of the four on the table after taking the treasure.
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-12-the-strange.quote: having first left the sign of the four upon the table

1890-the-sign-of-the-four-12-the-strange.subject: Jonathan Small
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-12-the-strange.statement: Small hired Smith and the launch Aurora to carry the group toward their escape ship.
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-12-the-strange.quote: I engaged with old Smith, and was to give him a big sum if he got us safe to our ship.

1890-the-sign-of-the-four-12-the-strange.subject: Jonathan Small
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-12-the-strange.statement: Athelney Jones takes Small into custody at the end of the chapter.
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-12-the-strange.quote: I shall feel more at ease when we have our story-teller here safe under lock and key.

1890-the-sign-of-the-four-12-the-strange.subject: Sherlock Holmes
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-12-the-strange.statement: Holmes concludes that Lal Rao was the confederate in the house.
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-12-the-strange.quote: they had, as I surmised, a confederate in the house, who could be none other than Lal Rao, the butler

1890-the-sign-of-the-four-12-the-strange.subject: Sherlock Holmes
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-12-the-strange.statement: Holmes says that the cocaine bottle remains for him.
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-12-the-strange.quote: For me,” said Sherlock Holmes, “there still remains the cocaine-bottle.”

1891-a-scandal-in-bohemia.md.subject: Holmes
1891-a-scandal-in-bohemia.md.statement: Sherlock Holmes is a consulting detective who investigates crimes.
1891-a-scandal-in-bohemia.md.quote: He was still, as ever, deeply attracted by the study of crime, and occupied his immense faculties and extraordinary powers of observation in following out those clues, and clearing up those mysteries which had been abandoned as hopeless by the official police.

1891-a-scandal-in-bohemia.md.subject: Watson
1891-a-scandal-in-bohemia.md.statement: Watson is a doctor who has returned to civil practice.
1891-a-scandal-in-bohemia.md.quote: I was returning from a journey to a patient (for I had now returned to civil practice)

1891-a-scandal-in-bohemia.md.subject: Holmes
1891-a-scandal-in-bohemia.md.statement: Holmes and Watson are friends and former companions.
1891-a-scandal-in-bohemia.md.quote: I knew little of my former friend and companion.

1891-a-scandal-in-bohemia.md.subject: Irene
1891-a-scandal-in-bohemia.md.statement: Irene Adler was born in New Jersey.
1891-a-scandal-in-bohemia.md.quote: Born in New Jersey in the year 1858.

1891-a-scandal-in-bohemia.md.subject: Irene
1891-a-scandal-in-bohemia.md.statement: Irene Adler was born in 1858.
1891-a-scandal-in-bohemia.md.quote: Born in New Jersey in the year 1858.

1891-a-scandal-in-bohemia.md.subject: Irene
1891-a-scandal-in-bohemia.md.statement: Irene Adler was a contralto and prima donna before retiring from the operatic stage.
1891-a-scandal-in-bohemia.md.quote: Contralto—hum! La Scala, hum! Prima donna Imperial Opera of Warsaw—yes! Retired from operatic stage—ha!

1891-a-scandal-in-bohemia.md.subject: Holmes
1891-a-scandal-in-bohemia.md.statement: Holmes regards Irene Adler as the woman who eclipses all others in his eyes.
1891-a-scandal-in-bohemia.md.quote: In his eyes she eclipses and predominates the whole of her sex.

1891-a-scandal-in-bohemia.md.subject: Holmes
1891-a-scandal-in-bohemia.md.statement: Holmes lives in lodgings in Baker Street.
1891-a-scandal-in-bohemia.md.quote: Holmes, who loathed every form of society with his whole Bohemian soul, remained in our lodgings in Baker Street

1891-a-scandal-in-bohemia.md.subject: Watson
1891-a-scandal-in-bohemia.md.statement: On the night of March 20, 1888, Watson visits Holmes at Baker Street.
1891-a-scandal-in-bohemia.md.quote: One night—it was on the twentieth of March, 1888—I was returning from a journey to a patient (for I had now returned to civil practice), when my way led me through Baker Street.

1891-a-scandal-in-bohemia.md.subject: Watson
1891-a-scandal-in-bohemia.md.statement: Watson is married to an unnamed woman.
1891-a-scandal-in-bohemia.md.quote: My marriage had drifted us away from each other.

1891-a-scandal-in-bohemia.md.subject: Holmes
1891-a-scandal-in-bohemia.md.value: Watson is a medical practitioner from the iodoform, silver nitrate mark, and stethoscope
1891-a-scandal-in-bohemia.md.statement: Holmes deduces that Watson is an active medical practitioner from signs on his person.
1891-a-scandal-in-bohemia.md.quote: I must be dull, indeed, if I do not pronounce him to be an active member of the medical profession.

1891-a-scandal-in-bohemia.md.subject: Holmes
1891-a-scandal-in-bohemia.md.statement: Holmes knows there are seventeen steps from the hall to his room.
1891-a-scandal-in-bohemia.md.quote: Now, I know that there are seventeen steps, because I have both seen and observed.

1891-a-scandal-in-bohemia.md.subject: Holmes
1891-a-scandal-in-bohemia.md.statement: Holmes receives an anonymous note announcing a masked visitor seeking a consultation.
1891-a-scandal-in-bohemia.md.quote: There will call upon you to-night, at a quarter to eight o’clock,” it said, “a gentleman who desires to consult you upon a matter of the very deepest moment.

1891-a-scandal-in-bohemia.md.subject: Holmes
1891-a-scandal-in-bohemia.md.value: the note was written by a German on Bohemian paper
1891-a-scandal-in-bohemia.md.statement: Holmes deduces that the note's writer is German and used paper made in Bohemia.
1891-a-scandal-in-bohemia.md.quote:
The paper was made in Bohemia,” I said.
“Precisely. And the man who wrote the note is a German.

1891-a-scandal-in-bohemia.md.subject: King of Bohemia
1891-a-scandal-in-bohemia.md.value: Wilhelm Gottsreich Sigismond von Ormstein, Grand Duke of Cassel-Felstein and hereditary King of Bohemia
1891-a-scandal-in-bohemia.md.statement: The masked visitor is Wilhelm Gottsreich Sigismond von Ormstein, hereditary King of Bohemia.
1891-a-scandal-in-bohemia.md.quote: Your Majesty had not spoken before I was aware that I was addressing Wilhelm Gottsreich Sigismond von Ormstein, Grand Duke of Cassel-Felstein, and hereditary King of Bohemia.

1891-a-scandal-in-bohemia.md.subject: King of Bohemia
1891-a-scandal-in-bohemia.md.statement: The King of Bohemia is thirty years old.
1891-a-scandal-in-bohemia.md.quote: I am but thirty now.

1891-a-scandal-in-bohemia.md.subject: King of Bohemia
1891-a-scandal-in-bohemia.md.statement: The King has come incognito from Prague to consult Holmes.
1891-a-scandal-in-bohemia.md.quote: I have come _incognito_ from Prague for the purpose of consulting you.

1891-a-scandal-in-bohemia.md.subject: King of Bohemia
1891-a-scandal-in-bohemia.md.statement: The King gives the alias Count Von Kramm.
1891-a-scandal-in-bohemia.md.quote: You may address me as the Count Von Kramm, a Bohemian nobleman.

1891-a-scandal-in-bohemia.md.subject: King of Bohemia
1891-a-scandal-in-bohemia.md.statement: The King employs Holmes to recover a compromising photograph from Irene Adler.
1891-a-scandal-in-bohemia.md.quote: Your Majesty, as I understand, became entangled with this young person, wrote her some compromising letters, and is now desirous of getting those letters back.

1891-a-scandal-in-bohemia.md.subject: King of Bohemia
1891-a-scandal-in-bohemia.md.statement: The King became entangled with Irene Adler during a visit to Warsaw about five years earlier.
1891-a-scandal-in-bohemia.md.quote: Some five years ago, during a lengthy visit to Warsaw, I made the acquaintance of the well-known adventuress, Irene Adler.

1891-a-scandal-in-bohemia.md.subject: King of Bohemia
1891-a-scandal-in-bohemia.md.statement: The King was Crown Prince when he became involved with Irene Adler.
1891-a-scandal-in-bohemia.md.quote: I was only Crown Prince then.

1891-a-scandal-in-bohemia.md.subject: King of Bohemia
1891-a-scandal-in-bohemia.md.statement: The King wrote Irene compromising letters.
1891-a-scandal-in-bohemia.md.quote: Your Majesty, as I understand, became entangled with this young person, wrote her some compromising letters, and is now desirous of getting those letters back.

1891-a-scandal-in-bohemia.md.subject: King of Bohemia
1891-a-scandal-in-bohemia.md.statement: Five attempts to recover the photograph from Irene have failed.
1891-a-scandal-in-bohemia.md.quote: Five attempts have been made. Twice burglars in my pay ransacked her house. Once we diverted her luggage when she travelled. Twice she has been waylaid. There has been no result.

1891-a-scandal-in-bohemia.md.subject: Irene
1891-a-scandal-in-bohemia.md.value: send the photograph when his betrothal is publicly proclaimed
1891-a-scandal-in-bohemia.md.statement: Irene threatens to send the photograph to the King's fiancée when his betrothal is publicly proclaimed.
1891-a-scandal-in-bohemia.md.quote: Because she has said that she would send it on the day when the betrothal was publicly proclaimed.

1891-a-scandal-in-bohemia.md.subject: King of Bohemia
1891-a-scandal-in-bohemia.md.statement: The King is about to marry Clotilde Lothman von Saxe-Meningen, second daughter of the King of Scandinavia.
1891-a-scandal-in-bohemia.md.quote: To Clotilde Lothman von Saxe-Meningen, second daughter of the King of Scandinavia.

1891-a-scandal-in-bohemia.md.subject: King of Bohemia
1891-a-scandal-in-bohemia.md.statement: The King gives Holmes carte blanche to spend money on the case.
1891-a-scandal-in-bohemia.md.quote: You have _carte blanche_.

1891-a-scandal-in-bohemia.md.subject: Irene
1891-a-scandal-in-bohemia.md.statement: Irene Adler lives at Briony Lodge on Serpentine Avenue in St. John’s Wood.
1891-a-scandal-in-bohemia.md.quote: Is Briony Lodge, Serpentine Avenue, St. John’s Wood.

1891-a-scandal-in-bohemia.md.subject: King of Bohemia
1891-a-scandal-in-bohemia.md.statement: The King stays at the Langham under the name Count Von Kramm.
1891-a-scandal-in-bohemia.md.quote: You will find me at the Langham under the name of the Count Von Kramm.

1891-a-scandal-in-bohemia.md.subject: Holmes
1891-a-scandal-in-bohemia.md.statement: Holmes disguises himself as an unemployed groom to investigate Briony Lodge.
1891-a-scandal-in-bohemia.md.quote: I left the house a little after eight o’clock this morning in the character of a groom out of work.

1891-a-scandal-in-bohemia.md.subject: Holmes
1891-a-scandal-in-bohemia.md.statement: Holmes examines the exterior and layout of Briony Lodge while disguised as a groom.
1891-a-scandal-in-bohemia.md.quote: I walked round it and examined it closely from every point of view, but without noting anything else of interest.

1891-a-scandal-in-bohemia.md.subject: Irene
1891-a-scandal-in-bohemia.md.value: at five every day and returns at seven for dinner
1891-a-scandal-in-bohemia.md.statement: Irene usually drives out at five and returns at seven for dinner.
1891-a-scandal-in-bohemia.md.quote: She lives quietly, sings at concerts, drives out at five every day, and returns at seven sharp for dinner.

1891-a-scandal-in-bohemia.md.subject: Godfrey Norton
1891-a-scandal-in-bohemia.md.statement: Godfrey Norton visits Irene at least once a day, often twice.
1891-a-scandal-in-bohemia.md.quote: He is dark, handsome, and dashing, never calls less than once a day, and often twice.

1891-a-scandal-in-bohemia.md.subject: Godfrey Norton
1891-a-scandal-in-bohemia.md.statement: Godfrey Norton is a lawyer of the Inner Temple.
1891-a-scandal-in-bohemia.md.quote: He is a Mr. Godfrey Norton, of the Inner Temple.

1891-a-scandal-in-bohemia.md.subject: Irene
1891-a-scandal-in-bohemia.md.statement: Irene Adler marries Godfrey Norton at St. Monica’s Church.
1891-a-scandal-in-bohemia.md.quote: I found myself mumbling responses which were whispered in my ear, and vouching for things of which I knew nothing, and generally assisting in the secure tying up of Irene Adler, spinster, to Godfrey Norton, bachelor.

1891-a-scandal-in-bohemia.md.subject: Watson
1891-a-scandal-in-bohemia.md.statement: Watson serves as a witness at Irene and Godfrey Norton’s wedding.
1891-a-scandal-in-bohemia.md.quote: The clergyman absolutely refused to marry them without a witness of some sort, and that my lucky appearance saved the bridegroom from having to sally out into the streets in search of a best man.

1891-a-scandal-in-bohemia.md.subject: Godfrey Norton
1891-a-scandal-in-bohemia.md.statement: Irene Adler and Godfrey Norton are married.
1891-a-scandal-in-bohemia.md.quote: Irene Adler is married,” remarked Holmes.

1891-a-scandal-in-bohemia.md.subject: Holmes
1891-a-scandal-in-bohemia.md.statement: Holmes asks Watson to assist in his plan at Briony Lodge.
1891-a-scandal-in-bohemia.md.quote: By the way, Doctor, I shall want your co-operation.

1891-a-scandal-in-bohemia.md.subject: Holmes
1891-a-scandal-in-bohemia.md.statement: Holmes tells Watson to throw a smoke rocket into Irene’s sitting room and shout fire when Holmes signals.
1891-a-scandal-in-bohemia.md.quote: And when I raise my hand—so—you will throw into the room what I give you to throw, and will, at the same time, raise the cry of fire.

1891-a-scandal-in-bohemia.md.subject: Holmes
1891-a-scandal-in-bohemia.md.statement: Holmes disguises himself as a Nonconformist clergyman.
1891-a-scandal-in-bohemia.md.quote: He disappeared into his bedroom and returned in a few minutes in the character of an amiable and simple-minded Nonconformist clergyman.

1891-a-scandal-in-bohemia.md.subject: Holmes
1891-a-scandal-in-bohemia.md.statement: Holmes stages a street scuffle outside Briony Lodge and pretends to be injured so he can be carried inside.
1891-a-scandal-in-bohemia.md.quote: Holmes dashed into the crowd to protect the lady; but, just as he reached her, he gave a cry and dropped to the ground, with the blood running freely down his face.

1891-a-scandal-in-bohemia.md.subject: Irene
1891-a-scandal-in-bohemia.md.statement: Irene allows the apparently injured Holmes to be brought into her sitting room.
1891-a-scandal-in-bohemia.md.quote:
“He can’t lie in the street. May we bring him in, marm?”
“Surely. Bring him into the sitting-room. There is a comfortable sofa. This way, please!”

1891-a-scandal-in-bohemia.md.subject: Watson
1891-a-scandal-in-bohemia.md.statement: Watson throws Holmes’s smoke rocket into the sitting room and cries fire.
1891-a-scandal-in-bohemia.md.quote: At the same instant I saw him raise his hand and at the signal I tossed my rocket into the room with a cry of “Fire!”

1891-a-scandal-in-bohemia.md.subject: Holmes
1891-a-scandal-in-bohemia.md.value: a recess behind a sliding panel above the right bell-pull
1891-a-scandal-in-bohemia.md.statement: Holmes discovers Irene’s photograph hidden behind a sliding panel above the right bell-pull in the sitting room.
1891-a-scandal-in-bohemia.md.quote: The photograph is in a recess behind a sliding panel just above the right bell-pull.

1891-a-scandal-in-bohemia.md.subject: Irene
1891-a-scandal-in-bohemia.md.statement: During the fire alarm, Irene rushes to the hidden photograph and partly draws it out.
1891-a-scandal-in-bohemia.md.quote: She would rush to secure it. The alarm of fire was admirably done. The smoke and shouting were enough to shake nerves of steel. She responded beautifully. The photograph is in a recess behind a sliding panel just above the right bell-pull. She was there in an instant, and I caught a glimpse of it as she half drew it out.

1891-a-scandal-in-bohemia.md.subject: Holmes
1891-a-scandal-in-bohemia.md.statement: Holmes plans to return to Briony Lodge with the King at eight the following morning to recover the photograph.
1891-a-scandal-in-bohemia.md.quote: At eight in the morning. She will not be up, so that we shall have a clear field.

1891-a-scandal-in-bohemia.md.subject: Irene
1891-a-scandal-in-bohemia.md.statement: Irene leaves England with her husband on the 5:15 train from Charing Cross for the Continent.
1891-a-scandal-in-bohemia.md.quote: She left this morning with her husband by the 5:15 train from Charing Cross for the Continent.

1891-a-scandal-in-bohemia.md.subject: Holmes
1891-a-scandal-in-bohemia.md.statement: Holmes retrieves Irene’s photograph and her letter from the recess behind the bell-pull.
1891-a-scandal-in-bohemia.md.quote: Holmes rushed at the bell-pull, tore back a small sliding shutter, and, plunging in his hand, pulled out a photograph and a letter.

1891-a-scandal-in-bohemia.md.subject: Irene
1891-a-scandal-in-bohemia.md.statement: Irene signs her letter as Irene Norton, née Adler.
1891-a-scandal-in-bohemia.md.quote: “IRENE NORTON, _née_ ADLER.”

1891-a-scandal-in-bohemia.md.subject: Irene
1891-a-scandal-in-bohemia.md.value: months before the King employed him
1891-a-scandal-in-bohemia.md.statement: Irene had been warned months earlier that the King might employ Holmes as his agent.
1891-a-scandal-in-bohemia.md.quote: I had been warned against you months ago. I had been told that, if the King employed an agent, it would certainly be you.

1891-a-scandal-in-bohemia.md.subject: Irene
1891-a-scandal-in-bohemia.md.statement: After the fire alarm, Irene realizes that the clergyman is Holmes and that he has tricked her.
1891-a-scandal-in-bohemia.md.quote: Until after the alarm of fire, I had not a suspicion. But then, when I found how I had betrayed myself, I began to think.

1891-a-scandal-in-bohemia.md.subject: Irene
1891-a-scandal-in-bohemia.md.statement: Irene disguises herself as a slim youth in an ulster and follows Holmes to Baker Street.
1891-a-scandal-in-bohemia.md.quote: There were several people on the pavement at the time, but the greeting appeared to come from a slim youth in an ulster who had hurried by.

1891-a-scandal-in-bohemia.md.subject: Irene
1891-a-scandal-in-bohemia.md.statement: Irene and her husband decide to flee England to avoid Holmes.
1891-a-scandal-in-bohemia.md.quote: We both thought the best resource was flight, when pursued by so formidable an antagonist; so you will find the nest empty when you call to-morrow.

1891-a-scandal-in-bohemia.md.subject: Irene
1891-a-scandal-in-bohemia.md.value: to safeguard herself and preserve a weapon against future steps by the King
1891-a-scandal-in-bohemia.md.statement: Irene keeps the King’s photograph as protection against any future action he might take against her.
1891-a-scandal-in-bohemia.md.quote: I keep it only to safeguard myself, and to preserve a weapon which will always secure me from any steps which he might take in the future.

1891-a-scandal-in-bohemia.md.subject: Irene
1891-a-scandal-in-bohemia.md.statement: Irene leaves a photograph of herself for the King to have.
1891-a-scandal-in-bohemia.md.quote: I leave a photograph which he might care to possess

1891-a-scandal-in-bohemia.md.subject: King of Bohemia
1891-a-scandal-in-bohemia.md.statement: The King accepts Irene’s promise not to use the compromising photograph against him.
1891-a-scandal-in-bohemia.md.quote: I know that her word is inviolate.

1891-a-scandal-in-bohemia.md.subject: Holmes
1891-a-scandal-in-bohemia.md.statement: Holmes asks the King to give him Irene’s photograph as his reward.
1891-a-scandal-in-bohemia.md.quote: “This photograph!”

1891-a-scandal-in-bohemia.md.subject: Holmes
1891-a-scandal-in-bohemia.md.statement: Holmes refers to Irene Adler as “the woman.”
1891-a-scandal-in-bohemia.md.quote: And when he speaks of Irene Adler, or when he refers to her photograph, it is always under the honourable title of _the_ woman.

1891-the-five-orange-pips.md.subject: John
1891-the-five-orange-pips.md.statement: John's first name is John.
1891-the-five-orange-pips.md.quote: My name,” said he, “is John Openshaw

1891-the-five-orange-pips.md.subject: John
1891-the-five-orange-pips.md.statement: John is the son of Joseph Openshaw.
1891-the-five-orange-pips.md.quote: My father had two sons—my uncle Elias and my father Joseph.

1891-the-five-orange-pips.md.subject: Elias
1891-the-five-orange-pips.md.statement: Elias was a colonel.
1891-the-five-orange-pips.md.quote: where he rose to be a colonel.

1891-the-five-orange-pips.md.subject: Elias
1891-the-five-orange-pips.md.statement: Elias and Joseph are brothers.
1891-the-five-orange-pips.md.quote: My grandfather had two sons—my uncle Elias and my father Joseph.

1891-the-five-orange-pips.md.subject: Elias
1891-the-five-orange-pips.md.statement: Elias is John's uncle.
1891-the-five-orange-pips.md.quote: My uncle Elias and my father Joseph.

1891-the-five-orange-pips.md.subject: John
1891-the-five-orange-pips.md.statement: John is Elias's nephew.
1891-the-five-orange-pips.md.quote: He begged my father to let me live with him

1891-the-five-orange-pips.md.subject: Elias
1891-the-five-orange-pips.md.statement: Elias took John into his home when John was young.
1891-the-five-orange-pips.md.quote: He begged my father to let me live with him and he was very kind to me in his way.

1891-the-five-orange-pips.md.subject: Joseph
1891-the-five-orange-pips.md.value: a factory owner and patentee of the Openshaw unbreakable tire
1891-the-five-orange-pips.md.statement: Joseph owned a factory and patented the Openshaw unbreakable tire.
1891-the-five-orange-pips.md.quote: My father had a small factory at Coventry, which he enlarged at the time of the invention of bicycling.

1891-the-five-orange-pips.md.subject: Elias
1891-the-five-orange-pips.md.statement: Elias emigrated to America when he was a young man.
1891-the-five-orange-pips.md.quote: My uncle Elias emigrated to America when he was a young man

1891-the-five-orange-pips.md.subject: Elias
1891-the-five-orange-pips.md.statement: Elias became a planter in Florida.
1891-the-five-orange-pips.md.quote: and became a planter in Florida, where he was reported to have done very well.

1891-the-five-orange-pips.md.subject: Elias
1891-the-five-orange-pips.md.statement: Elias returned to Europe around 1869 or 1870 and settled on a small estate in Sussex near Horsham.
1891-the-five-orange-pips.md.quote: About 1869 or 1870 he came back to Europe and took a small estate in Sussex, near Horsham.

1891-the-five-orange-pips.md.subject: Horsham
1891-the-five-orange-pips.md.statement: Horsham is a town in Sussex.
1891-the-five-orange-pips.md.quote: a small estate in Sussex, near Horsham.

1891-the-five-orange-pips.md.subject: Elias
1891-the-five-orange-pips.md.statement: Elias received a letter bearing a Pondicherry postmark in March 1883.
1891-the-five-orange-pips.md.quote: One day—it was in March, 1883—a letter with a foreign stamp lay upon the table in front of the colonel’s plate.

1891-the-five-orange-pips.md.subject: Elias
1891-the-five-orange-pips.md.statement: Elias's letter contained five dried orange pips.
1891-the-five-orange-pips.md.quote: Opening it hurriedly, out there jumped five little dried orange pips, which pattered down upon his plate.

1891-the-five-orange-pips.md.subject: Elias
1891-the-five-orange-pips.md.value: K. K. K.! My God, my God, my sins have overtaken me!
1891-the-five-orange-pips.md.statement: Elias exclaimed that the K.K.K. had come for him and said his sins had overtaken him.
1891-the-five-orange-pips.md.quote: ‘K. K. K.!’ he shrieked, and then, ‘My God, my God, my sins have overtaken me!’

1891-the-five-orange-pips.md.subject: Elias
1891-the-five-orange-pips.md.statement: Elias burned papers from his brass box after receiving the warning.
1891-the-five-orange-pips.md.quote: The fire was burning brightly, and in the grate there was a mass of black, fluffy ashes, as of burned paper, while the brass box stood open and empty beside it.

1891-the-five-orange-pips.md.subject: Elias
1891-the-five-orange-pips.md.statement: Elias left his estate to his brother Joseph.
1891-the-five-orange-pips.md.quote: I leave my estate, with all its advantages and all its disadvantages, to my brother, your father, whence it will, no doubt, descend to you.

1891-the-five-orange-pips.md.subject: Elias
1891-the-five-orange-pips.md.statement: Elias was found dead in a garden pool after one of his drunken sallies.
1891-the-five-orange-pips.md.quote: We found him, when we went to search for him, face downward in a little green-scummed pool, which lay at the foot of the garden.

1891-the-five-orange-pips.md.subject: Elias
1891-the-five-orange-pips.md.statement: The jury ruled Elias's death a suicide.
1891-the-five-orange-pips.md.quote: the jury, having regard to his known eccentricity, brought in a verdict of ‘suicide.’

1891-the-five-orange-pips.md.subject: Joseph
1891-the-five-orange-pips.md.statement: Joseph inherited Elias's estate and about £14,000 in the bank.
1891-the-five-orange-pips.md.quote: my father entered into possession of the estate, and of some £ 14,000, which lay to his credit at the bank.

1891-the-five-orange-pips.md.subject: Joseph
1891-the-five-orange-pips.md.statement: Joseph came to live at Horsham in early 1884.
1891-the-five-orange-pips.md.quote: Well, it was the beginning of ’84 when my father came to live at Horsham

1891-the-five-orange-pips.md.subject: Joseph
1891-the-five-orange-pips.md.statement: Joseph received five dried orange pips in a warning letter from Dundee in January 1885.
1891-the-five-orange-pips.md.quote: There he was, sitting with a newly opened envelope in one hand and five dried orange pips in the outstretched palm of the other one.

1891-the-five-orange-pips.md.subject: Joseph
1891-the-five-orange-pips.md.value: Put the papers on the sundial
1891-the-five-orange-pips.md.statement: Joseph's warning letter instructed him to put the papers on the sundial.
1891-the-five-orange-pips.md.quote: ‘Put the papers on the sundial,’ I read, peeping over his shoulder.

1891-the-five-orange-pips.md.subject: Joseph
1891-the-five-orange-pips.md.object: John's suggestion to contact the police
1891-the-five-orange-pips.md.statement: Joseph refused John's suggestion that they contact the police about the warning.
1891-the-five-orange-pips.md.quote: ‘No, I forbid you. I won’t have a fuss made about such nonsense.’

1891-the-five-orange-pips.md.subject: Joseph
1891-the-five-orange-pips.md.statement: Joseph died after falling into an unfenced chalk-pit while returning from Fareham.
1891-the-five-orange-pips.md.quote: My father had fallen over one of the deep chalk-pits which abound in the neighbourhood, and was lying senseless, with a shattered skull.

1891-the-five-orange-pips.md.subject: Joseph
1891-the-five-orange-pips.md.statement: The jury ruled Joseph's death accidental.
1891-the-five-orange-pips.md.quote: the jury had no hesitation in bringing in a verdict of ‘death from accidental causes.’

1891-the-five-orange-pips.md.subject: John
1891-the-five-orange-pips.md.statement: John inherited the estate after Joseph's death.
1891-the-five-orange-pips.md.quote: In this sinister way I came into my inheritance.

1891-the-five-orange-pips.md.subject: John
1891-the-five-orange-pips.md.statement: John received five dried orange pips in a warning letter postmarked in east London.
1891-the-five-orange-pips.md.quote: The young man took from his waistcoat a crumpled envelope, and turning to the table he shook out upon it five little dried orange pips.

1891-the-five-orange-pips.md.subject: John
1891-the-five-orange-pips.md.value: Put the papers on the sundial
1891-the-five-orange-pips.md.statement: John's warning repeated the instruction to put the papers on the sundial.
1891-the-five-orange-pips.md.quote: Within are the very words which were upon my father’s last message: ‘K. K. K.’; and then ‘Put the papers on the sundial.’

1891-the-five-orange-pips.md.subject: John
1891-the-five-orange-pips.md.statement: John came to Holmes for advice and help.
1891-the-five-orange-pips.md.quote: “I have come for advice.”

1891-the-five-orange-pips.md.subject: Holmes
1891-the-five-orange-pips.md.value: Put the surviving diary page and a note in the brass box, then leave the box on the sundial.
1891-the-five-orange-pips.md.statement: Holmes advised John to put the surviving page and an explanatory note in the brass box and place it on the sundial.
1891-the-five-orange-pips.md.quote: You must put this piece of paper which you have shown us into the brass box which you have described.

1891-the-five-orange-pips.md.subject: John
1891-the-five-orange-pips.md.statement: John promised to follow Holmes's advice.
1891-the-five-orange-pips.md.quote: I shall certainly do as you advise.

1891-the-five-orange-pips.md.subject: John
1891-the-five-orange-pips.md.value: in the Thames near Waterloo Bridge
1891-the-five-orange-pips.md.statement: John drowned after falling into the water near Waterloo Bridge on the night he left Holmes.
1891-the-five-orange-pips.md.quote: It proved to be that of a young gentleman whose name, as it appears from an envelope which was found in his pocket, was John Openshaw

1891-the-five-orange-pips.md.subject: John
1891-the-five-orange-pips.md.statement: The newspaper account described John's death as an unfortunate accident.
1891-the-five-orange-pips.md.quote: there can be no doubt that the deceased had been the victim of an unfortunate accident

1891-the-five-orange-pips.md.subject: Holmes
1891-the-five-orange-pips.md.value: an envelope containing five orange pips and the inscription S. H. for J. O.
1891-the-five-orange-pips.md.statement: Holmes sent Captain James Calhoun five orange pips in an envelope marked “S. H. for J. O.”
1891-the-five-orange-pips.md.quote: Of these he took five and thrust them into an envelope.

1891-the-five-orange-pips.md.subject: Calhoun
1891-the-five-orange-pips.md.statement: Captain James Calhoun leads the gang pursuing the Openshaws.
1891-the-five-orange-pips.md.quote: “The leader of the gang. I shall have the others, but he first.”

1891-the-five-orange-pips.md.subject: Holmes
1891-the-five-orange-pips.md.statement: Holmes traced the threats to the barque Lone Star.
1891-the-five-orange-pips.md.quote: I searched the Dundee records, and when I found that the barque _Lone Star_ was there in January, ’85, my suspicion became a certainty.

1891-the-five-orange-pips.md.subject: Lone Star
1891-the-five-orange-pips.md.statement: The Lone Star left London bound for Savannah.
1891-the-five-orange-pips.md.quote: I went down to the Albert Dock and found that she had been taken down the river by the early tide this morning, homeward bound to Savannah.

1891-the-five-orange-pips.md.subject: Holmes
1891-the-five-orange-pips.md.statement: Holmes arranged to inform Savannah police that the three American sailors were wanted for murder.
1891-the-five-orange-pips.md.quote: the cable will have informed the police of Savannah that these three gentlemen are badly wanted here upon a charge of murder.

1891-the-five-orange-pips.md.subject: Lone Star
1891-the-five-orange-pips.md.statement: The Lone Star was apparently lost in the Atlantic, and no further news of it reached Holmes and Watson.
1891-the-five-orange-pips.md.quote: We did at last hear that somewhere far out in the Atlantic a shattered stern-post of a boat was seen swinging in the trough of a wave, with the letters “L. S.” carved upon it, and that is all which we shall ever know of the fate of the _Lone Star_.

1891-the-five-orange-pips.md.subject: Ku Klux Klan
1891-the-five-orange-pips.md.statement: The Ku Klux Klan sends a recognised warning token to a marked person, who may flee or publicly renounce their former ways; if they defy the warning, death follows.
1891-the-five-orange-pips.md.quote: On receiving this the victim might either openly abjure his former ways, or might fly from the country.

1891-the-five-orange-pips.md.subject: Ku Klux Klan
1891-the-five-orange-pips.md.statement: Orange pips are one of the warning tokens used by the Ku Klux Klan.
1891-the-five-orange-pips.md.quote: a sprig of oak-leaves in some parts, melon seeds or orange pips in others.

1891-the-five-orange-pips.md.subject: Holmes
1891-the-five-orange-pips.md.statement: Holmes deduced that K.K.K. referred to the Ku Klux Klan.
1891-the-five-orange-pips.md.quote: “Have you never—” said Sherlock Holmes, bending forward and sinking his voice—“have you never heard of the Ku Klux Klan?”

1891-the-man-with-the-twisted-lip.md.subject: Isa
1891-the-man-with-the-twisted-lip.md.statement: Isa is the brother of the late Elias Whitney.
1891-the-man-with-the-twisted-lip.md.quote: Isa Whitney, brother of the late Elias Whitney, D.D., Principal of the Theological College of St. George’s, was much addicted to opium.

1891-the-man-with-the-twisted-lip.md.subject: Isa
1891-the-man-with-the-twisted-lip.md.statement: Isa is addicted to opium.
1891-the-man-with-the-twisted-lip.md.quote: Isa Whitney, brother of the late Elias Whitney, D.D., Principal of the Theological College of St. George’s, was much addicted to opium.

1891-the-man-with-the-twisted-lip.md.subject: Isa
1891-the-man-with-the-twisted-lip.md.statement: Isa has been a slave to opium for many years.
1891-the-man-with-the-twisted-lip.md.quote: for many years he continued to be a slave to the drug, an object of mingled horror and pity to his friends and relatives.

1891-the-man-with-the-twisted-lip.md.subject: Kate
1891-the-man-with-the-twisted-lip.md.statement: Kate is married to Isa Whitney.
1891-the-man-with-the-twisted-lip.md.quote: It’s about Isa. He has not been home for two days.

1891-the-man-with-the-twisted-lip.md.subject: Kate
1891-the-man-with-the-twisted-lip.md.statement: Kate is an old friend and school companion of Watson’s wife.
1891-the-man-with-the-twisted-lip.md.quote: It was not the first time that she had spoken to us of her husband’s trouble, to me as a doctor, to my wife as an old friend and school companion.

1891-the-man-with-the-twisted-lip.md.subject: Isa
1891-the-man-with-the-twisted-lip.md.statement: When Isa’s opium fit is on him, he uses the Bar of Gold opium den in Upper Swandam Lane.
1891-the-man-with-the-twisted-lip.md.quote: She had the surest information that of late he had, when the fit was on him, made use of an opium den in the farthest east of the City.

1891-the-man-with-the-twisted-lip.md.subject: Kate
1891-the-man-with-the-twisted-lip.md.statement: Kate comes to Watson’s home seeking help about Isa.
1891-the-man-with-the-twisted-lip.md.quote: Our own door flew open, and a lady, clad in some dark-coloured stuff, with a black veil, entered the room.

1891-the-man-with-the-twisted-lip.md.subject: Kate
1891-the-man-with-the-twisted-lip.md.statement: Kate asks Watson for medical advice and help about Isa.
1891-the-man-with-the-twisted-lip.md.quote: Oh, no, no! I want the doctor’s advice and help, too.

1891-the-man-with-the-twisted-lip.md.subject: Watson
1891-the-man-with-the-twisted-lip.md.statement: Watson travels alone to the Bar of Gold to find Isa.
1891-the-man-with-the-twisted-lip.md.quote: And so in ten minutes I had left my armchair and cheery sitting-room behind me, and was speeding eastward in a hansom on a strange errand, as it seemed to me at the time, though the future only could show how strange it was to be.

1891-the-man-with-the-twisted-lip.md.subject: Watson
1891-the-man-with-the-twisted-lip.md.statement: Watson finds Isa at the Bar of Gold.
1891-the-man-with-the-twisted-lip.md.quote: There was a movement and an exclamation from my right, and peering through the gloom, I saw Whitney, pale, haggard, and unkempt, staring out at me.

1891-the-man-with-the-twisted-lip.md.subject: Isa
1891-the-man-with-the-twisted-lip.md.statement: Isa is at the Bar of Gold when Watson finds him.
1891-the-man-with-the-twisted-lip.md.quote: There was a movement and an exclamation from my right, and peering through the gloom, I saw Whitney, pale, haggard, and unkempt, staring out at me.

1891-the-man-with-the-twisted-lip.md.subject: Watson
1891-the-man-with-the-twisted-lip.md.statement: Watson pays Isa’s bill, leads him to the cab, and sends him home.
1891-the-man-with-the-twisted-lip.md.quote: In a few minutes I had written my note, paid Whitney’s bill, led him out to the cab, and seen him driven through the darkness.

1891-the-man-with-the-twisted-lip.md.subject: Sherlock Holmes
1891-the-man-with-the-twisted-lip.md.statement: Sherlock Holmes is disguised as an old opium den patron at the Bar of Gold.
1891-the-man-with-the-twisted-lip.md.quote: He had turned his back so that none could see him but I. His form had filled out, his wrinkles were gone, the dull eyes had regained their fire, and there, sitting by the fire and grinning at my surprise, was none other than Sherlock Holmes.

1891-the-man-with-the-twisted-lip.md.subject: Sherlock Holmes
1891-the-man-with-the-twisted-lip.md.statement: Sherlock Holmes is conducting an inquiry into Neville St. Clair’s disappearance.
1891-the-man-with-the-twisted-lip.md.quote: Briefly, Watson, I am in the midst of a very remarkable inquiry, and I have hoped to find a clue in the incoherent ramblings of these sots, as I have done before now.

1891-the-man-with-the-twisted-lip.md.subject: Sherlock Holmes
1891-the-man-with-the-twisted-lip.md.statement: Sherlock Holmes stays at The Cedars while conducting the inquiry.
1891-the-man-with-the-twisted-lip.md.quote: Yes; that is Mr. St. Clair’s house. I am staying there while I conduct the inquiry.

1891-the-man-with-the-twisted-lip.md.subject: Watson
1891-the-man-with-the-twisted-lip.md.statement: Watson joins Holmes on the investigation as a companion and chronicler.
1891-the-man-with-the-twisted-lip.md.quote: Oh, a trusty comrade is always of use; and a chronicler still more so.

1891-the-man-with-the-twisted-lip.md.subject: Neville St. Clair
1891-the-man-with-the-twisted-lip.md.statement: Neville was seen at a second-floor window of the Bar of Gold on Monday.
1891-the-man-with-the-twisted-lip.md.quote: While she was walking in this way down Swandam Lane, she suddenly heard an ejaculation or cry, and was struck cold to see her husband looking down at her and, as it seemed to her, beckoning to her from a second-floor window.

1891-the-man-with-the-twisted-lip.md.subject: Neville St. Clair
1891-the-man-with-the-twisted-lip.md.statement: Neville St. Clair is thirty-seven years old.
1891-the-man-with-the-twisted-lip.md.quote: Mr. St. Clair is now thirty-seven years of age, is a man of temperate habits, a good husband, a very affectionate father, and a man who is popular with all who know him.

1891-the-man-with-the-twisted-lip.md.subject: Neville St. Clair
1891-the-man-with-the-twisted-lip.md.object: a husband and father of two children
1891-the-man-with-the-twisted-lip.md.statement: Neville is a husband and father of two children.
1891-the-man-with-the-twisted-lip.md.quote: By degrees he made friends in the neighbourhood, and in 1887 he married the daughter of a local brewer, by whom he now has two children.

1891-the-man-with-the-twisted-lip.md.subject: Neville St. Clair
1891-the-man-with-the-twisted-lip.md.statement: Neville is married to Mrs. St. Clair.
1891-the-man-with-the-twisted-lip.md.quote: By degrees he made friends in the neighbourhood, and in 1887 he married the daughter of a local brewer, by whom he now has two children.

1891-the-man-with-the-twisted-lip.md.subject: Neville St. Clair
1891-the-man-with-the-twisted-lip.md.statement: Neville generally returns from town on the 5:14 from Cannon Street.
1891-the-man-with-the-twisted-lip.md.quote: He had no occupation, but was interested in several companies and went into town as a rule in the morning, returning by the 5:14 from Cannon Street every night.

1891-the-man-with-the-twisted-lip.md.subject: Neville St. Clair
1891-the-man-with-the-twisted-lip.md.statement: Neville lives in a large villa in Lee.
1891-the-man-with-the-twisted-lip.md.quote: He took a large villa, laid out the grounds very nicely, and lived generally in good style.

1891-the-man-with-the-twisted-lip.md.subject: Neville St. Clair
1891-the-man-with-the-twisted-lip.md.statement: Neville writes a reassuring note to his wife and sends it with his signet ring through the Lascar.
1891-the-man-with-the-twisted-lip.md.quote: Knowing that my wife would be terribly anxious, I slipped off my ring and confided it to the Lascar at a moment when no constable was watching me, together with a hurried scrawl, telling her that she had no cause to fear.

1891-the-man-with-the-twisted-lip.md.subject: Neville St. Clair
1891-the-man-with-the-twisted-lip.md.statement: Neville St. Clair has been living a second life as the beggar Hugh Boone.
1891-the-man-with-the-twisted-lip.md.quote: Let me introduce you,” he shouted, “to Mr. Neville St. Clair, of Lee, in the county of Kent.

1891-the-man-with-the-twisted-lip.md.subject: Neville St. Clair
1891-the-man-with-the-twisted-lip.md.statement: Neville formerly worked as a reporter on a London evening paper.
1891-the-man-with-the-twisted-lip.md.quote: I travelled in my youth, took to the stage, and finally became a reporter on an evening paper in London.

1891-the-man-with-the-twisted-lip.md.subject: Neville St. Clair
1891-the-man-with-the-twisted-lip.md.statement: Neville began begging in the City while disguised as a match-seller to research articles.
1891-the-man-with-the-twisted-lip.md.quote: I took advantage now of my attainments.

1891-the-man-with-the-twisted-lip.md.subject: Neville St. Clair
1891-the-man-with-the-twisted-lip.md.statement: Neville conceals his beggar identity from his wife and children.
1891-the-man-with-the-twisted-lip.md.quote: As I grew richer I grew more ambitious, took a house in the country, and eventually married, without anyone having a suspicion as to my real occupation.

1891-the-man-with-the-twisted-lip.md.subject: Neville St. Clair
1891-the-man-with-the-twisted-lip.md.statement: Neville uses makeup, a false scar, a twisted lip, a red wig, and beggar’s clothes to disguise himself as Hugh Boone.
1891-the-man-with-the-twisted-lip.md.quote: I painted my face, and to make myself as pitiable as possible I made a good scar and fixed one side of my lip in a twist by the aid of a small slip of flesh-coloured plaster.

1891-the-man-with-the-twisted-lip.md.subject: Neville St. Clair
1891-the-man-with-the-twisted-lip.md.statement: Neville’s average takings as a beggar are less than £700 a year.
1891-the-man-with-the-twisted-lip.md.quote: I do not mean that any beggar in the streets of London could earn £ 700 a year—which is less than my average takings—but I had exceptional advantages in my power of making up, and also in a facility of repartee, which improved by practice and made me quite a recognised character in the City.

1891-the-man-with-the-twisted-lip.md.subject: Neville St. Clair
1891-the-man-with-the-twisted-lip.md.statement: Neville is dressing in his room above the opium den when he sees his wife outside.
1891-the-man-with-the-twisted-lip.md.quote: Last Monday I had finished for the day and was dressing in my room above the opium den when I looked out of my window and saw, to my horror and astonishment, that my wife was standing in the street, with her eyes fixed full upon me.

1891-the-man-with-the-twisted-lip.md.subject: Neville St. Clair
1891-the-man-with-the-twisted-lip.md.statement: Neville throws his coin-weighted coat out of the window into the Thames.
1891-the-man-with-the-twisted-lip.md.quote: I hurled it out of the window, and it disappeared into the Thames.

1891-the-man-with-the-twisted-lip.md.subject: Hugh Boone
1891-the-man-with-the-twisted-lip.md.statement: Hugh Boone is Neville St. Clair in disguise.
1891-the-man-with-the-twisted-lip.md.quote: Let me introduce you,” he shouted, “to Mr. Neville St. Clair, of Lee, in the county of Kent.

1891-the-man-with-the-twisted-lip.md.subject: Hugh Boone
1891-the-man-with-the-twisted-lip.md.statement: Hugh Boone is a professional beggar who pretends to sell wax vestas.
1891-the-man-with-the-twisted-lip.md.quote: He is a professional beggar, though in order to avoid the police regulations he pretends to a small trade in wax vestas.

1891-the-man-with-the-twisted-lip.md.subject: Hugh Boone
1891-the-man-with-the-twisted-lip.md.statement: As Hugh Boone, Neville takes his daily seat at a corner in Threadneedle Street.
1891-the-man-with-the-twisted-lip.md.quote: Some little distance down Threadneedle Street, upon the left-hand side, there is, as you may have remarked, a small angle in the wall.

1891-the-man-with-the-twisted-lip.md.subject: Hugh Boone
1891-the-man-with-the-twisted-lip.md.value: across his face from eye to chin
1891-the-man-with-the-twisted-lip.md.statement: Hugh Boone’s false scar runs across his face from eye to chin.
1891-the-man-with-the-twisted-lip.md.quote: A broad wheal from an old scar ran right across it from eye to chin, and by its contraction had turned up one side of the upper lip, so that three teeth were exposed in a perpetual snarl.

1891-the-man-with-the-twisted-lip.md.subject: Hugh Boone
1891-the-man-with-the-twisted-lip.md.statement: Hugh Boone’s disguise has bright red hair.
1891-the-man-with-the-twisted-lip.md.quote: A shock of very bright red hair grew low over his eyes and forehead.

1891-the-man-with-the-twisted-lip.md.subject: Hugh Boone
1891-the-man-with-the-twisted-lip.md.object: a lodger at the opium den
1891-the-man-with-the-twisted-lip.md.statement: Hugh Boone lodges at the opium den in Swandam Lane.
1891-the-man-with-the-twisted-lip.md.quote: This is the man whom we now learn to have been the lodger at the opium den, and to have been the last man to see the gentleman of whom we are in quest.

1891-the-man-with-the-twisted-lip.md.subject: Neville St. Clair
1891-the-man-with-the-twisted-lip.md.statement: Neville’s father was a schoolmaster in Chesterfield.
1891-the-man-with-the-twisted-lip.md.quote: My father was a schoolmaster in Chesterfield, where I received an excellent education.

1891-the-man-with-the-twisted-lip.md.subject: Neville St. Clair
1891-the-man-with-the-twisted-lip.md.statement: Neville took to the stage before becoming a reporter.
1891-the-man-with-the-twisted-lip.md.quote: I travelled in my youth, took to the stage, and finally became a reporter on an evening paper in London.

1891-the-man-with-the-twisted-lip.md.subject: Lascar
1891-the-man-with-the-twisted-lip.md.object: the keeper of a low den in Swandam Lane
1891-the-man-with-the-twisted-lip.md.statement: The Lascar keeps the low den where Neville lodges and changes his disguise.
1891-the-man-with-the-twisted-lip.md.quote: Only one man knew my secret.

1891-the-man-with-the-twisted-lip.md.subject: Neville St. Clair
1891-the-man-with-the-twisted-lip.md.statement: Neville pays the Lascar for rooms in the den so that the Lascar will keep his secret.
1891-the-man-with-the-twisted-lip.md.quote: This fellow, a Lascar, was well paid by me for his rooms, so that I knew that my secret was safe in his possession.

1891-the-man-with-the-twisted-lip.md.subject: Sherlock Holmes
1891-the-man-with-the-twisted-lip.md.statement: Holmes has used the opium den for his own investigative purposes before.
1891-the-man-with-the-twisted-lip.md.quote: Had I been recognised in that den my life would not have been worth an hour’s purchase; for I have used it before now for my own purposes, and the rascally Lascar who runs it has sworn to have vengeance upon me.

1891-the-man-with-the-twisted-lip.md.subject: Sherlock Holmes
1891-the-man-with-the-twisted-lip.md.statement: Holmes reveals Neville’s identity by washing the disguise from his face in the police cell.
1891-the-man-with-the-twisted-lip.md.quote: Holmes stooped to the water-jug, moistened his sponge, and then rubbed it twice vigorously across and down the prisoner’s face.

1891-the-man-with-the-twisted-lip.md.subject: Neville St. Clair
1891-the-man-with-the-twisted-lip.md.statement: Neville swears that he will stop living as Hugh Boone.
1891-the-man-with-the-twisted-lip.md.quote: I have sworn it by the most solemn oaths which a man can take.

1891-the-man-with-the-twisted-lip.md.subject: Upper Swandam Lane
1891-the-man-with-the-twisted-lip.md.object: an alley east of London Bridge
1891-the-man-with-the-twisted-lip.md.statement: Upper Swandam Lane is a vile alley behind the high wharves east of London Bridge.
1891-the-man-with-the-twisted-lip.md.quote: Upper Swandam Lane is a vile alley lurking behind the high wharves which line the north side of the river to the east of London Bridge.

1891-the-man-with-the-twisted-lip.md.subject: Bar of Gold
1891-the-man-with-the-twisted-lip.md.statement: The Bar of Gold is in Upper Swandam Lane.
1891-the-man-with-the-twisted-lip.md.quote: There he was to be found, she was sure of it, at the Bar of Gold, in Upper Swandam Lane.

1891-the-man-with-the-twisted-lip.md.subject: Bar of Gold
1891-the-man-with-the-twisted-lip.md.statement: The Bar of Gold is an opium den.
1891-the-man-with-the-twisted-lip.md.quote: There he was to be found, she was sure of it, at the Bar of Gold, in Upper Swandam Lane.

1891-the-man-with-the-twisted-lip.md.subject: Bar of Gold
1891-the-man-with-the-twisted-lip.md.statement: The Bar of Gold has a second-floor window that opens onto Swandam Lane.
1891-the-man-with-the-twisted-lip.md.quote: The window was open, and she distinctly saw his face, which she describes as being terribly agitated.

1891-the-man-with-the-twisted-lip.md.subject: The Cedars
1891-the-man-with-the-twisted-lip.md.statement: The Cedars is near Lee in Kent.
1891-the-man-with-the-twisted-lip.md.quote: Near Lee, in Kent.

1891-the-man-with-the-twisted-lip.md.subject: The Cedars
1891-the-man-with-the-twisted-lip.md.statement: The Cedars is the St. Clair family’s house.
1891-the-man-with-the-twisted-lip.md.quote: Yes; that is Mr. St. Clair’s house.

1891-the-man-with-the-twisted-lip.md.subject: The Cedars
1891-the-man-with-the-twisted-lip.md.statement: Mrs. St. Clair puts two rooms at The Cedars at Holmes’s disposal.
1891-the-man-with-the-twisted-lip.md.quote: Mrs. St. Clair has most kindly put two rooms at my disposal, and you may rest assured that she will have nothing but a welcome for my friend and colleague.

1891-the-man-with-the-twisted-lip.md.subject: Bar of Gold
1891-the-man-with-the-twisted-lip.md.statement: A trap-door at the back of the opium den near Paul’s Wharf has been used to pass bodies through on moonless nights.
1891-the-man-with-the-twisted-lip.md.quote: There is a trap-door at the back of that building, near the corner of Paul’s Wharf, which could tell some strange tales of what has passed through it upon the moonless nights.

1891-the-man-with-the-twisted-lip.md.subject: Sherlock Holmes
1891-the-man-with-the-twisted-lip.md.statement: Holmes initially believes Neville is dead and says he met his death on Monday.
1891-the-man-with-the-twisted-lip.md.quote: “On what day did he meet his death?” “On Monday.”

1891-the-man-with-the-twisted-lip.md.subject: Mrs. St. Clair
1891-the-man-with-the-twisted-lip.md.statement: Mrs. St. Clair receives a letter from Neville bearing his signet ring.
1891-the-man-with-the-twisted-lip.md.quote: Yes, there was a ring. His signet-ring.

1891-the-man-with-the-twisted-lip.md.subject: Holmes
1891-the-man-with-the-twisted-lip.md.statement: Holmes takes Watson to Bow Street to see the prisoner Boone.
1891-the-man-with-the-twisted-lip.md.quote: In town the earliest risers were just beginning to look sleepily from their windows as we drove through the streets of the Surrey side.

1891-the-man-with-the-twisted-lip.md.subject: Holmes
1891-the-man-with-the-twisted-lip.md.statement: Holmes reveals that the prisoner Boone is Neville St. Clair.
1891-the-man-with-the-twisted-lip.md.quote: Let me introduce you,” he shouted, “to Mr. Neville St. Clair, of Lee, in the county of Kent.

1891-the-man-with-the-twisted-lip.md.subject: Neville St. Clair
1891-the-man-with-the-twisted-lip.md.statement: Neville explains to Holmes and Inspector Bradstreet that he became a beggar to earn money and concealed his identity from his family.
