1891-the-man-with-the-twisted-lip.md.quote: As I grew richer I grew more ambitious, took a house in the country, and eventually married, without anyone having a suspicion as to my real occupation.

1891-the-man-with-the-twisted-lip.md.subject: Neville St. Clair
1891-the-man-with-the-twisted-lip.md.statement: Neville says he feared his children would be ashamed of their father if his secret became known.
1891-the-man-with-the-twisted-lip.md.quote: It was not the wife; it was the children,” groaned the prisoner. “God help me, I would not have them ashamed of their father.

1891-the-man-with-the-twisted-lip.md.subject: Neville St. Clair
1891-the-man-with-the-twisted-lip.md.object: a small cut on his face
1891-the-man-with-the-twisted-lip.md.statement: Neville had cut himself in his bedroom on the morning his wife saw him at the den.
1891-the-man-with-the-twisted-lip.md.quote: I threw open the window, reopening by my violence a small cut which I had inflicted upon myself in the bedroom that morning.

1891-the-man-with-the-twisted-lip.md.subject: Neville St. Clair
1891-the-man-with-the-twisted-lip.md.statement: Neville’s small cut was on his face.
1891-the-man-with-the-twisted-lip.md.quote: I threw open the window, reopening by my violence a small cut which I had inflicted upon myself in the bedroom that morning.

1891-the-man-with-the-twisted-lip.md.subject: Inspector Bradstreet
1891-the-man-with-the-twisted-lip.md.statement: Bradstreet says Neville must stop using the Hugh Boone identity if the police are to hush up the case.
1891-the-man-with-the-twisted-lip.md.quote: If the police are to hush this thing up, there must be no more of Hugh Boone.

1891-the-man-with-the-twisted-lip.md.subject: Isa
1891-the-man-with-the-twisted-lip.md.statement: Isa and Kate are married.
1891-the-man-with-the-twisted-lip.md.quote: It’s about Isa. He has not been home for two days.

1893-the-greek-interpreter.md.subject: Sherlock Holmes
1893-the-greek-interpreter.md.statement: Sherlock Holmes is a detective who uses observation and deduction.
1893-the-greek-interpreter.md.quote: I said that he was my superior in observation and deduction.

1893-the-greek-interpreter.md.subject: Mycroft
1893-the-greek-interpreter.md.statement: Mycroft is Sherlock Holmes’s brother.
1893-the-greek-interpreter.md.quote: Because my brother Mycroft possesses it in a larger degree than I do.

1893-the-greek-interpreter.md.subject: Mycroft
1893-the-greek-interpreter.md.value: seven years older than Sherlock Holmes
1893-the-greek-interpreter.md.statement: Mycroft is seven years older than Sherlock Holmes.
1893-the-greek-interpreter.md.quote: “Seven years my senior.”

1893-the-greek-interpreter.md.subject: Mycroft
1893-the-greek-interpreter.md.statement: Mycroft has better powers of observation and deduction than Sherlock Holmes.
1893-the-greek-interpreter.md.quote: When I say, therefore, that Mycroft has better powers of observation than I, you may take it that I am speaking the exact and literal truth.

1893-the-greek-interpreter.md.subject: Mycroft
1893-the-greek-interpreter.md.value: auditor of books in government departments
1893-the-greek-interpreter.md.statement: Mycroft audits the books in some government departments.
1893-the-greek-interpreter.md.quote: He has an extraordinary faculty for figures, and audits the books in some of the government departments.

1893-the-greek-interpreter.md.subject: Mycroft
1893-the-greek-interpreter.md.statement: Mycroft lodges in Pall Mall.
1893-the-greek-interpreter.md.quote: Mycroft lodges in Pall Mall, and he walks round the corner into Whitehall every morning and back every evening.

1893-the-greek-interpreter.md.subject: Mycroft
1893-the-greek-interpreter.md.statement: Mycroft was one of the founders of the Diogenes Club.
1893-the-greek-interpreter.md.quote: My brother was one of the founders, and I have myself found it a very soothing atmosphere.

1893-the-greek-interpreter.md.subject: Mycroft
1893-the-greek-interpreter.md.statement: Mycroft is at the Diogenes Club every day from quarter to five until twenty to eight.
1893-the-greek-interpreter.md.quote: He’s always there from quarter to five to twenty to eight.

1893-the-greek-interpreter.md.subject: Diogenes Club
1893-the-greek-interpreter.md.value: members taking notice of one another; talking is forbidden except in the Stranger’s Room
1893-the-greek-interpreter.md.statement: The Diogenes Club forbids members from taking notice of one another and allows no talking outside the Stranger’s Room.
1893-the-greek-interpreter.md.quote: No member is permitted to take the least notice of any other one. Save in the Stranger’s Room, no talking is, under any circumstances, allowed

1893-the-greek-interpreter.md.subject: Melas
1893-the-greek-interpreter.md.statement: Melas is a Greek interpreter who works in London.
1893-the-greek-interpreter.md.quote: For many years I have been the chief Greek interpreter in London, and my name is very well known in the hotels.

1893-the-greek-interpreter.md.subject: Melas
1893-the-greek-interpreter.md.statement: The interpreter’s name is Melas.
1893-the-greek-interpreter.md.quote: I have asked Mr. Melas to step across,

1893-the-greek-interpreter.md.statement: Paul Kratides is from Athens.
1893-the-greek-interpreter.md.quote: ‘Then I shall never see her. _Athens._’

1893-the-greek-interpreter.md.subject: Paul Kratides
1893-the-greek-interpreter.md.statement: Paul Kratides is unable to speak English.
1893-the-greek-interpreter.md.quote: Anybody supplying any information to the whereabouts of a Greek gentleman named Paul Kratides, from Athens, who is unable to speak English, will be rewarded.

1893-the-greek-interpreter.md.subject: Sophy
1893-the-greek-interpreter.md.statement: The Greek woman’s first name is Sophy.
1893-the-greek-interpreter.md.quote: ‘Oh, my God, it is Paul!’

1893-the-greek-interpreter.md.subject: Paul Kratides
1893-the-greek-interpreter.md.statement: Paul Kratides is Sophy’s brother.
1893-the-greek-interpreter.md.quote: Then the brother—for that, I fancy, must be the relationship—comes over from Greece to interfere.

1893-the-greek-interpreter.md.subject: Sophy
1893-the-greek-interpreter.md.statement: Sophy is living at The Myrtles when Davenport answers the advertisement.
1893-the-greek-interpreter.md.quote: She is living at present at The Myrtles, Beckenham.

1893-the-greek-interpreter.md.subject: Harold Latimer
1893-the-greek-interpreter.md.statement: Harold Latimer is an Englishman.
1893-the-greek-interpreter.md.quote: the young Englishman named Harold Latimer

1893-the-greek-interpreter.md.subject: Harold Latimer
1893-the-greek-interpreter.md.statement: Harold Latimer persuaded Sophy to fly away with him after meeting her in England.
1893-the-greek-interpreter.md.quote: While there she had met a young man named Harold Latimer, who had acquired an ascendancy over her and had eventually persuaded her to fly with him.

1893-the-greek-interpreter.md.subject: Wilson Kemp
1893-the-greek-interpreter.md.statement: Wilson Kemp is Harold Latimer’s associate.
1893-the-greek-interpreter.md.quote: The brother, on his arrival in England, had imprudently placed himself in the power of Latimer and of his associate, whose name was Wilson Kemp

1893-the-greek-interpreter.md.subject: Harold Latimer
1893-the-greek-interpreter.md.statement: Harold Latimer and Wilson Kemp kept Paul Kratides prisoner and tried to force him to sign away his and Sophy’s property.
1893-the-greek-interpreter.md.quote: These two, finding that through his ignorance of the language he was helpless in their hands, had kept him a prisoner, and had endeavoured by cruelty and starvation to make him sign away his own and his sister’s property.

1893-the-greek-interpreter.md.subject: Harold Latimer
1893-the-greek-interpreter.md.statement: Harold Latimer kidnapped Melas and took him to translate for Paul Kratides.
1893-the-greek-interpreter.md.quote: I was not surprised, therefore, on Monday night when a Mr. Latimer, a very fashionably dressed young man, came up to my rooms and asked me to accompany him in a cab which was waiting at the door.

1893-the-greek-interpreter.md.subject: Melas
1893-the-greek-interpreter.md.statement: Melas questioned Paul Kratides in Greek while the kidnappers demanded that he sign papers.
1893-the-greek-interpreter.md.quote: You are to ask the questions, Mr. Melas, and he will write the answers.

1893-the-greek-interpreter.md.subject: Paul Kratides
1893-the-greek-interpreter.md.statement: Paul Kratides refused to sign the papers unless he saw Sophy marry in his presence before a Greek priest he knew.
1893-the-greek-interpreter.md.quote: ‘Only if I see her married in my presence by a Greek priest whom I know.’

1893-the-greek-interpreter.md.subject: Sophy
1893-the-greek-interpreter.md.statement: Sophy recognized Paul Kratides when she entered the room during Melas’s first interpreting session.
1893-the-greek-interpreter.md.quote: ‘I could not stay away longer. It is so lonely up there with only—Oh, my God, it is Paul!’

1893-the-greek-interpreter.md.subject: Harold Latimer
1893-the-greek-interpreter.md.statement: Harold Latimer seized Sophy and pushed her out of the room after she recognized Paul.
1893-the-greek-interpreter.md.quote: Their embrace was but for an instant, however, for the younger man seized the woman and pushed her out of the room

1893-the-greek-interpreter.md.subject: Wilson Kemp
1893-the-greek-interpreter.md.statement: Wilson Kemp overpowered Paul Kratides and dragged him from the room.
1893-the-greek-interpreter.md.quote: while the elder easily overpowered his emaciated victim, and dragged him away through the other door.

1893-the-greek-interpreter.md.subject: Wilson Kemp
1893-the-greek-interpreter.md.statement: Wilson Kemp threatened Melas with harm if he disclosed what had happened.
1893-the-greek-interpreter.md.quote: if you speak to a human soul about this—one human soul, mind—well, may God have mercy upon your soul!”

1893-the-greek-interpreter.md.subject: Melas
1893-the-greek-interpreter.md.statement: Melas told Mycroft about the kidnapping the next morning.
1893-the-greek-interpreter.md.quote: I told the whole story to Mr. Mycroft Holmes next morning, and subsequently to the police.

1893-the-greek-interpreter.md.subject: Mycroft
1893-the-greek-interpreter.md.statement: Mycroft placed a newspaper advertisement seeking information about Paul Kratides and Sophy.
1893-the-greek-interpreter.md.quote: ‘Anybody supplying any information to the whereabouts of a Greek gentleman named Paul Kratides, from Athens, who is unable to speak English, will be rewarded. A similar reward paid to any one giving information about a Greek lady whose first name is Sophy. X 2473.’

1893-the-greek-interpreter.md.subject: Melas
1893-the-greek-interpreter.md.statement: Melas was kidnapped a second time by a man who threatened him with a life-preserver.
1893-the-greek-interpreter.md.quote: His visitor, on entering his rooms, had drawn a life-preserver from his sleeve, and had so impressed him with the fear of instant and inevitable death that he had kidnapped him for the second time.

1893-the-greek-interpreter.md.subject: Harold Latimer
1893-the-greek-interpreter.md.statement: Harold Latimer and Wilson Kemp fled The Myrtles with Sophy after their secret was exposed.
1893-the-greek-interpreter.md.quote: Finding that their secret was out, and that their prisoner was not to be coerced, the two villains with the girl had fled away at a few hours’ notice from the furnished house which they had hired

1893-the-greek-interpreter.md.subject: Sherlock Holmes
1893-the-greek-interpreter.md.statement: Sherlock Holmes went to The Myrtles with Watson, Inspector Gregson, and Mycroft to rescue the prisoners.
1893-the-greek-interpreter.md.quote: A drive of half a mile brought us to The Myrtles—a large, dark house standing back from the road in its own grounds.

1893-the-greek-interpreter.md.subject: Sherlock Holmes
1893-the-greek-interpreter.md.statement: Sherlock Holmes and the others rescued Melas from a room filled with charcoal fumes.
1893-the-greek-interpreter.md.quote: With a rush we got to the poisoned men and dragged them out into the well-lit hall.

1893-the-greek-interpreter.md.subject: Sherlock Holmes
1893-the-greek-interpreter.md.statement: Sherlock Holmes found Paul Kratides dead after rescuing him from the charcoal-filled room.
1893-the-greek-interpreter.md.quote: He had ceased to moan as we laid him down, and a glance showed me that for him at least our aid had come too late.

1893-the-greek-interpreter.md.subject: Melas
1893-the-greek-interpreter.md.statement: Melas survived the poisoning and regained consciousness within an hour.
1893-the-greek-interpreter.md.quote: Mr. Melas, however, still lived, and in less than an hour, with the aid of ammonia and brandy I had the satisfaction of seeing him open his eyes

1893-the-greek-interpreter.md.subject: Harold Latimer
1893-the-greek-interpreter.md.statement: Harold Latimer later died after being stabbed in Buda-Pesth.
1893-the-greek-interpreter.md.quote: It told how two Englishmen who had been traveling with a woman had met with a tragic end. They had each been stabbed, it seems

1893-the-greek-interpreter.md.statement: Wilson Kemp later died after being stabbed in Buda-Pesth.

1893-the-greek-interpreter.md.subject: Sherlock Holmes
1893-the-greek-interpreter.md.statement: Sherlock Holmes believed Sophy may have avenged the wrongs done to herself and her brother.
1893-the-greek-interpreter.md.quote: Holmes, however, is, I fancy, of a different way of thinking, and holds to this day that, if one could find the Grecian girl, one might learn how the wrongs of herself and her brother came to be avenged.
